chapters.title: Chapter 463: Two Hours
paragraphs: The almost-kiss sat between the plates. Private-room silence colored every ordinary sentence.
"When do you need to leave for the airport?" he asked.
"About two hours."
Stan smiled, slow and certain. "Alright... let’s make it worthwhile."

He stood. His arms found her with an ease that did not startle so much as gather. He lifted her, and Amelia’s breath caught, not from fear, from the sudden proof of his strength and the way her body softened against it without being asked. He walked her toward the bed and kissed her as he went.
Deep. Unhurried. Full of quiet intent.

Her heart pounded against her ribs as if it wanted out of the cage and into his chest. She kissed him back without hesitation, lost in the heat of his mouth, the taste of the meal they had barely touched still faint between them, the reality of a locked door and no audience. Hotel light held them in a soft, unused gold. Time narrowed to the span of his steps.
Inside her, a storm rose and did not knock anything over.

This was the first time she had ever been in a private room with a man she loved. The knowledge of what came next, her virginity, the line she had never let anyone near, filled her with a dizzy mix of nervousness, anticipation, and surrender. She still found it almost unreal: the woman who had hated men so completely, who had not been able to look at her father without anger because of the bastard he was, now clinging to Stan with trust that felt like a new organ. Before him she would not have believed a man could be this. Now she did not pull away.
She wanted this. She wanted him.
He laid her on the bed as if the mattress were a decision they had already made.
Each passing moment told Stan yes, she loved him, yes she cares for him, yes she loves every moment spent with him...
Despite their urges, the kiss did not rush to become anything else.

It deepened by degrees, Stan’s mouth learning the shape of her yes, Amelia answering with a softness that still shook. His hand found her waist first, then the rise of her ribs, giving her time to feel every station of the journey. When his palm closed over her breast through fabric she made a small sound into his mouth, not protest. Surprise at how quickly heat gathered there.

He eased the clothing aside as if it were a conversation. Mouth followed hand. He sucked her nipple with unhurried attention, fondling the other breast in the same patient rhythm, and Amelia’s back arched before she decided it would. Hotel light made a quiet gold of her skin. The uneaten food cooled on the table, irrelevant.
’This is happening. He is being careful. I can feel that he is being careful.’

Her heart would not slow. Nervousness lived in her thighs, in the way her fingers tightened in his hair when his tongue drew another helpless sound out of her. Desire lived there too, newer and louder. The old hatred of men tried, once, to stand up in the back of her mind. It had nothing to hold. This was Stan. This was the exception that had rewritten the rule.
He lifted his head. Checked her face.
"Still with me?"
"Yes." It came out thinner than she meant. She tried again. "Yes. Don’t stop. Just... slow."
"Slow," he agreed, and kissed the wet peak of her breast once more as a promise.

When he freed himself she looked, could not help looking, and the reality of him made her swallow. He did not joke. He did not hurry her eyes away. He let her see, then settled between her thighs only when her hands on his shoulders said stay.

He touched her first. Fingers, gentle, learning how ready she was, how tight, how the smallest circle made her breath break. Amelia hid her face against his neck for a second, overwhelmed by being known like this. Then she nodded.
He guided himself to her and stopped there, the blunt heat of him a question.
"Tell me if it hurts past what you can take.
"I will."
He pressed in an inch and waited.

The stretch stole her air. A burn, bright and specific, the body meeting a fact it had no practice for. Tears pricked without shame. He kissed them, kissed her mouth, held still until the burn loosened its first grip.
"That’s it. Breathe. I’ve got you."

She breathed. The panic that wanted to arrive did not; his stillness gave it nowhere to land. Another inch, given like a gift instead of a claim. She clung to him, nails careful on his back, the dizzy knowledge turning in her chest: my virginity, given, not taken. I am giving it.
He filled her by patience. When his hips finally met hers he stayed buried and shook with the effort of not moving, forehead against hers, asking without words whether the world was still acceptable.
Amelia’s voice was wrecked and certain.
"You can move. Slow. Please."

He did. Long, careful strokes that taught her body the difference between pain and fullness. The hurt receded into an ache that began, astonishingly, to want. She kissed him through it, lost and found in the same motion, the woman who had sworn off men holding this one as if he were the first true thing the category had ever produced.
Time narrowed to the hotel quiet, the give of the mattress, the sound of her own pulse, and Stan handling her as if she were something he intended to keep whole.
He kept the pace he had promised.

Each stroke was a long, careful question her body learned how to answer. When she tensed he shortened the motion and kissed her through it. When she softened he gave her more of the length and waited for the sound that meant yes. His mouth found her breast again, sucking slow, fondling the other as if attention itself were a way of holding her together.

paragraphs: They dressed without ceremony and without distance.

Amelia packed the last of the bathroom things into a side pocket while Stan checked the time once and then put the phone away. The bed was a rumpled witness. The tray of barely eaten food looked like a plan from a different hour. She smoothed her hair, winced when she sat to pull on her shoes, and caught him watching.
"I’m fine," she said. "Just... aware of myself."
"Good." He took the suitcase handle before she could. "Awareness is allowed."

Final look around the room: charger, jacket, the river still moving beyond the glass as if it had not noticed close to two hours being spent so completely. Amelia paused at the threshold with the key card in her fingers.
The suite still held the heat of them. Not perfume, not anything she could name for a clerk.

Just the particular quiet after a body has been opened and put back together. She thought of his mouth at her throat, the way he had gone still when she said his name like that, not as a request, as a fact. She thought of water earlier, of white sheets after, of the weight of him and the patience of him, of how she had come apart and then come back and still wanted more. A few days. She already missed the exact press of his hip against hers.

"I booked through today," she said. "Came back the day before yesterday to see you, and I’m really glad I made that move... My shares are at risk asof current, so . Even if I wanted to stay..." She stopped, then finished it honestly. "I want to stay. I can’t."
"Its okay, a few days is not much time," he said.
"A few days is a lot of time for me though, you underestimate how much I’ll miss you, I’ll definitely come before this week end." It was a promise she intended to keep. "I’ll text when I land."

They stepped into the corridor. She locked the suite, the click small and final, and they rode the elevator down in a quiet that felt earned rather than empty. At reception she slid the key across the desk, signed what needed signing, thanked the clerk in the polite voice of a woman who had just rewritten a private history upstairs and would not be discussing it.

Outside, late light sat on the Audi. He loaded the suitcase, opened her door, and she settled in with another careful breath. The city rolled toward Velaris Airport in familiar pieces, overpasses, signs, the particular thinning of ordinary streets into travel infrastructure.
"You’ll eat on the plane?" he asked.
"I’ll try. I don’t trust airport sandwiches, but I trust fainting less."
"Call when you reach your destination."
"I will." She looked at his profile. "Thank you for coming today. For all of it."
"Its nothing my love."

Traffic thickened near the river bend. Not a jam, exactly, just the kind of slowing that made the clock feel personal. Amelia’s hand found the edge of the seat. After a moment she said, quietly, "Can you pull off? Just for a minute. Not long."

He glanced at her, then at the next exit. A small overlook sat above the water, the kind of place people used for photos and then forgot. He took it. Hazard lights off. Engine still. The river from here was the same river as from the suite, only farther and more honest.
Amelia unclipped her belt and sat for a second with his palms on her thighs. His glasses were tinted so they had privacy...

"I keep thinking about the room," she said. "Not in a neat way. In the way my body thinks. You had me against the glass first. Then the bed. You were careful and you weren’t. I can still feel where you held me. I’m going to sit on a plane for hours pretending I’m only a woman with a meeting and a suitcase, and the whole time I’m going to remember how you looked when you..." She broke off, color high, then finished it because she had already decided to be honest today. "When you were inside me and you wouldn’t let me rush. I’ll miss that. I’ll miss you. I already do."
Stan turned in his seat. He didn’t reach for her immediately. He listened like the words were something he could keep.
"I know," he said. "I can still taste you. That’s not a line. It’s just true."
She let out a breath that was almost a laugh. "This is a terrible place to say that."
"It’s an excellent place. No one is looking."

He leaned across and kissed her, slower than the curb would allow later, deep enough that her fingers found his jacket and stayed. When they parted she rested her forehead against his for a count of three.
"If I stay another ten minutes I will miss the flight on purpose," she murmured.
"Then we go." He kissed the corner of her mouth once more, almost chaste after everything that had not been. "see you before weekend."
"I love you Stan."
"I love you too"

They pulled back onto the road. The drop-off lane was a braid of hazards and goodbyes. He pulled in, hazard lights ticking. Amelia got out. He met her at the curb with the suitcase, wheels finding the pavement.
The kiss was not hurried and was not chaste.

He framed her face, and she rose into him, mouth opening under his with the memory of the room still warm in it, and now the overlook too, the river, the confession she had given him because she would rather be known than composed. Deep. Unfinished on purpose.

A few days compressed into the press of lips and the brief catch of her breath when his hand settled at her waist. Someone’s horn sounded far away and did not matter. When they parted, her eyes were bright and steady.
"Go," she whispered. "Before I invent a delay."
"Have a safe flight."
"Take care you too..."
"Okay Amelia, I’ll miss you..."

"A few days is a lot of time for me though, you underestimate how much I’ll miss you, I’ll definitely come before this week end." It was a promise she intended to keep.
"I’ll text when I land."
They stepped into the corridor.
She locked the suite, the click small and final, and they rode the elevator down in a quiet that felt earned rather than empty.

At reception she slid the key across the desk, signed what needed signing, thanked the clerk in the polite voice of a woman who had just rewritten a private history upstairs and would not be discussing it.
Outside, late light sat on the Audi.
He loaded the suitcase, opened her door, and she settled in with another careful breath.
The city rolled toward Velaris Airport in familiar pieces, overpasses, signs, the particular thinning of ordinary streets into travel infrastructure.
"You’ll eat on the plane?" he asked.
"I’ll try.
I don’t trust airport sandwiches, but I trust fainting less."
"Call when you reach your destination."
"I will." She looked at his profile.
"Thank you for coming today.
For all of it."
"Its nothing my love."
Traffic thickened near the river bend.
Not a jam, exactly, just the kind of slowing that made the clock feel personal.
Amelia’s hand found the edge of the seat.
After a moment she said, quietly, "Can you pull off?
Just for a minute.
Not long."
He glanced at her, then at the next exit.
A small overlook sat above the water, the kind of place people used for photos and then forgot.
He took it.
Hazard lights off.
Engine still.
The river from here was the same river as from the suite, only farther and more honest.
Amelia unclipped her belt and sat for a second with his palms on her thighs.
His glasses were tinted so they had privacy...
"I keep thinking about the room," she said.
"Not in a neat way.
In the way my body thinks.
You had me against the glass first.
Then the bed.
You were careful and you weren’t.
I can still feel where you held me.

I’m going to sit on a plane for hours pretending I’m only a woman with a meeting and a suitcase, and the whole time I’m going to remember how you looked when you..." She broke off, color high, then finished it because she had already decided to be honest today.
"When you were inside me and you wouldn’t let me rush.
I’ll miss that.
I’ll miss you.
I already do."
Stan turned in his seat.
He didn’t reach for her immediately.
He listened like the words were something he could keep.
"I know," he said.
"I can still taste you.
That’s not a line.
It’s just true."
She let out a breath that was almost a laugh.
"This is a terrible place to say that."
"It’s an excellent place.
No one is looking."
He leaned across and kissed her, slower than the curb would allow later, deep enough that her fingers found his jacket and stayed.
When they parted she rested her forehead against his for a count of three.
"If I stay another ten minutes I will miss the flight on purpose," she murmured.
"Then we go." He kissed the corner of her mouth once more, almost chaste after everything that had not been.
"see you before weekend."
"I love you Stan."
"I love you too"
They pulled back onto the road.
The drop-off lane was a braid of hazards and goodbyes.
He pulled in, hazard lights ticking.
Amelia got out.
He met her at the curb with the suitcase, wheels finding the pavement.
The kiss was not hurried and was not chaste.

He framed her face, and she rose into him, mouth opening under his with the memory of the room still warm in it, and now the overlook too, the river, the confession she had given him because she would rather be known than composed.
Deep.
Unfinished on purpose.
A few days compressed into the press of lips and the brief catch of her breath when his hand settled at her waist.
Someone’s horn sounded far away and did not matter.
When they parted, her eyes were bright and steady.
"Go," she whispered.
"Before I invent a delay."
"Have a safe flight."
"Take care you too..."
"Okay Amelia, I’ll miss you..."

chapters.title: Chapter 467: Before Weekend
paragraphs: "Have a safe flight."
"Take care you too..."
"Okay Amelia, I’ll miss you..."

She took the handle. He watched her walk toward the terminal doors, departures, check-in, the long belt where luggage would be taken from her and promised to the hold of a plane she could not see yet.

The suitcase rolled a faithful rhythm. Her figure moved through the sliding glass and the crowd with the particular grace of a woman who had somewhere she had to be, and a body that still remembered being wanted without hurry.
Stan stayed at the curb a moment longer than the lane wanted.

His gaze dropped, helpless and fond, to the sway of her as she went: that full, living line of hip and ass catching the light with every step, the shape he had held in water and in white sheets only an hour ago. He licked his lower lip without thinking. Admired. Then the admiration opened into something wider and quieter.
A sigh left him.

A short stretch of calendar ago he had not had this life, companies, Qi, a sister learning to breathe energy on a floor in Inksea, a vampire on a campus, a childhood friend in Velaris, and this woman walking into an airport with his mark still somewhere under her clothes. Far. Fast. Real.

Amelia did not look back. She did not need to. Inside the terminal she found a pillar and stood for one uncounted second with her eyes closed, feeling the ache and the heat and the promise, then opened them and walked toward security like a woman who could carry both hunger and a schedule.

He watched until the glass took the last bounce of her step, then got into the Audi and pulled away from the curb, the promise of a few days already sitting in the passenger seat like a person who had only just left.
The curb released him, and the airport slipped into the distance behind the Audi.
Stan drove with one hand on the wheel, the afternoon sun still warm against his skin.
Traffic carried him away from the airport and back toward campus, but his thoughts remained somewhere else.
Amelia.
The memory returned without asking permission.
Her beneath him, trembling as they moved carefully through her first time together, with him going slow and steady into her...

That slow, uncertain beginning. The way she had gradually relaxed when she realized he wasn’t going to rush her. The change in her breathing. The quiet sounds she made once the discomfort faded and something warmer took its place.
Then the bath afterward.
Water sliding over her sexy shoulders and collarbone while she rested against him, her body loose and peaceful for the first time that day.
And her voice. ’I’m glad it was you.’
Stan’s fingers tightened slightly around the steering wheel.
He didn’t try to romanticize the memory, nor did he push it away.
It had happened. It had been intimate, complicated, and real.
And now Amelia was on the other side of an airport security gate, leaving the country again.
Stan exhaled slowly and let his attention return to the road.
There was another woman waiting for him.
’Camilla.’
Her expression when he’d left the game shop had been quiet enough that anyone else might have missed it.

Stan hadn’t. He knew that look. She hadn’t stopped him. She hadn’t demanded an explanation. She had simply watched him leave with the unmistakable expression of someone who had been looking forward to spending the afternoon with him and had just discovered that she would have to share those hours with someone else.
He couldn’t blame her. He had promised Amelia he would see her before she left. Keeping that promise had mattered.
So did coming back. By the time Stan reached campus, the sky had begun to deepen toward evening.
He parked near the same stretch of storefronts and continued the rest of the way on foot.

The game shop appeared exactly where he’d left it, its windows throwing blue-white light across the pavement. Through the glass came the muffled sounds of gunfire, explosions, and Zack’s voice rising above all of them.
"No! No, no, no! That was absolutely not my fault!"
Stan slowed, smiling at Zack’s tensed voice... ’Apparently, things had progressed.’
He pushed open the door. The cool air of the shop washed over him.
He immediately found the three of them.
Zack was half out of his stool, staring at the screen with the expression of a man who had just been personally betrayed by modern technology.
Zoey was leaning back in her chair, controller resting loosely in her hands.
And Camilla, Stan stopped.
She was still holding the controller with the same precise grip she’d had when he left. But everything else had changed.
Her character moved across the map with smooth, deliberate movements. She wasn’t wandering anymore. She wasn’t stopping to think about which button did what.
She moved, turned, crouched, aimed. Then fired.
A player appeared at the edge of the screen.
Camilla reacted instantly, one burst from the shotgun she was using, the enemy dropped and notification appeared that instant
ELIMINATION.
Camilla calmly moved on.
Stan’s eyebrows lifted. ’She’s gotten pretty good within such a short time... As expected of Camilla...’
At that moment, Zack finally noticed him. His head snapped around.
"He’s back!"
Zoey glanced over and smiled, "About time."
Stan looked at the clock. "You said you’d play for two hours, it’s been more than that but you guys are still at it..."
"Well we couldn’t help it the game is interesting."
Zoey pointed at Zack. "He spent twenty minutes arguing with the game."
"It was a tactical disagreement."
"You called the developers incompetent."
"They deserved it."
The attendant, passing behind them with a drink in one hand, heard that.
"You’ve been here for two hours."
Zack looked at him. "Time moves differently in Verdansk."
The attendant stared at him.."That’s not how time works."
"Not for you, maybe."
The attendant walked away.
Stan smiled and took in the scene again.
Zack’s character was currently lying dead behind a concrete barrier.
Zoey’s was crouched several meters away. Camilla’s was moving toward them.

chapters.title: Chapter 468: Game
paragraphs: Stan pointed toward the screen, his attention drawn to the chaotic firefight playing out across the monitor. "What’s happening?"
Zack’s expression immediately darkened as though the question had reminded him of a personal tragedy. He leaned back in his chair and folded his arms across his chest. "She looked at the map once."
Zoey, who was sitting nearby, immediately corrected him without taking her eyes off her own screen. "She looked at the map once and then killed you."
"She didn’t kill me," Zack protested.
Zoey finally turned toward him with a completely unimpressed expression. "You’re dead."
"I was strategically eliminated," Zack replied with complete seriousness, as though there were an important distinction that everyone else was refusing to acknowledge.
Camilla finally glanced away from the game for a moment. Her expression remained calm as she looked at Zack. "You ran into the open."
Zack stared at her in disbelief. "I was flanking."
"You were running in a straight line."
"I was flanking aggressively."
"You were shouting while doing it," Zoey added, her lips already twitching with amusement.
Zack immediately defended himself. "That was psychological warfare."
Camilla turned her attention back to the screen. "It did not work."

Zoey snorted, and Stan couldn’t hold back his laughter. The absurd exchange was made even funnier by the fact that Camilla delivered every sentence with the same cold, analytical tone she might have used while discussing something genuinely important.

Stan pulled out the empty stool beside her and sat down. The shop was relatively quiet compared to the noise coming from their screens, and the faint smell of warm electronics, dust, and sugary drinks from the refrigerator near the counter hung in the air. Several gaming stations occupied the room, their monitors casting a pale glow across the faces of the players. Somewhere behind the counter, the attendant was busy with something, occasionally glancing toward them whenever Zack’s increasingly dramatic complaints became too loud.
Stan rested one arm against the back of his chair and glanced at Camilla’s screen. "How long did it take you to learn?"
Camilla’s eyes remained fixed on the game as her fingers moved smoothly across the controller. "Twenty-three minutes."

Zack immediately turned toward Stan. "Twenty-three minutes to learn the controls," he clarified, clearly unwilling to let Camilla’s answer create the wrong impression. "Then she spent another forty minutes destroying everyone."
Camilla tilted her head slightly while continuing to move her character through the battlefield. "Not everyone."
Zoey looked at her scoreboard and then back at Camilla. "You’ve killed fourteen players."
Camilla paused for a brief moment before answering with complete seriousness. "Fourteen is not everyone."
There was a moment of silence before Zack muttered, "That’s exactly what a future psychopath would say.

The corner of Zoey’s mouth lifted as she tried not to laugh. Stan simply shook his head, amused by the entire situation. Camilla, however, seemed completely unconcerned by Zack’s accusation and continued playing as though nothing unusual had been said.
The attendant, who had been listening from behind the counter, finally called out, "She’s actually doing pretty well."
"Pretty well?" Zack immediately complained. "She has more kills than me."
The attendant shrugged casually. "That’s usually what pretty well looks like."
Zack stared at him as though he’d just been betrayed by someone he trusted. "I was promised a safe environment."
"You asked to play Warzone."
"I didn’t realize the enemy would be someone I came with."

Zoey laughed openly this time, while Stan leaned back and watched the exchange with an amused smile. Camilla continued to play without reacting to their conversation, her attention completely absorbed by the battlefield on the screen.
Then, without warning, her character stopped moving.
Camilla’s expression sharpened as she focused on something beyond the immediate area visible on the screen. Her fingers became still for a moment.
"Enemy."
Zack immediately leaned forward. "Where?"
Camilla lifted one hand and pointed toward the screen. "Behind that building."
Zoey narrowed her eyes and looked in the direction Camilla had indicated. "I don’t see anyone."
"He’s there."
Zack squinted at the screen, trying to find whatever Camilla had noticed. "How can you tell?"
"The grass moved."
Silence fell over the group.
Zack slowly turned his head toward Stan, his expression filled with disbelief. "She heard the grass.
Before anyone could respond, Camilla raised her weapon. A few seconds later, a player stepped out from behind the building exactly where she had predicted.
Camilla fired immediately.
The enemy dropped.
The elimination notification appeared across the screen.
Zack leaned back into his chair as though the game had personally offended him. "I don’t like this anymore."
Zoey grinned. "I do."
Camilla continued playing, seemingly unaffected by the praise or Zack’s growing despair. Her movements were becoming increasingly efficient, and Stan found himself watching her more closely.

When he had left the shop earlier, Camilla had still been struggling with the basic controls. She had walked into walls, wasted ammunition, and somehow managed to throw a grenade at her own feet. Now she was reading enemy movement, predicting positions, using terrain for cover, and recognizing subtle changes in the environment that the others had completely missed.
She hadn’t merely learned the controls.
She had understood the game.

And knowing Camilla, Stan suspected she wouldn’t stop there. Once she became interested in something, she tended to analyze it until she understood every detail. If she continued playing, it probably wouldn’t take long before she figured out the weapons, movement mechanics, map layouts, enemy habits, and every other system the developers had built into the game.
Stan leaned back slightly and smiled. "You’ve improved."

For the first time in several minutes, Camilla looked away from the screen and toward him. The coldness that had lingered in her eyes earlier hadn’t completely disappeared, but it had softened considerably.
"You came back."
"I said I would."
"You were gone longer than you said."
Stan’s smile faded slightly. He knew exactly what she meant. "I know."
Camilla’s gaze remained on him for another moment before she returned her attention to the game. "I noticed."

There was no accusation in her voice. She didn’t demand an explanation or ask where he had gone. She simply stated the fact, and somehow that made the words weigh more heavily than an angry confrontation would have.
Stan watched her for a moment before giving a faint smile. "I had something important to take care of."
"I know." Camilla didn’t ask what it was. She didn’t need to.

chapters.title: Chapter 469: Noisy Zack
paragraphs: Stan watched Camilla for a moment before giving a faint smile. "I had something important to take care of."
"I know." Camilla didn’t ask what it was. She didn’t need to.

For several seconds, neither of them said anything. The only sounds were the gunfire and movement coming from their monitors, mixed with the occasional click of controllers and the low hum of the computers around them.
Then Zack, oblivious to the tension that had settled over the two of them, broke the silence with his characteristic lack of subtlety. "Can someone revive me?"
Zoey didn’t even look at him. "No."
"Why?"
"Because you’re annoying."
"I’m literally dying."
"You’ve been doing that for twenty minutes."
"That’s different."
Camilla sighed, the sound carrying a hint of exasperation that she usually kept carefully contained. "Where are you?" she asked.
Zack immediately brightened, apparently taking this as a sign that his fortunes were about to change. "Behind the wall."
"You’re exposed."
"I know."
"Then why are you there?"
"Because I was shot."
Camilla stared at the screen, her expression unreadable. "That explains the result, not the decision."

Zoey burst out laughing, the sound filling the shop and drawing a brief glance from the attendant. Stan couldn’t help himself; he laughed too. The moment of tension had passed, broken by the absurdity of Zack’s continued struggles. Zack looked around at all three of them, his expression one of wounded dignity, apparently realizing that no one intended to take his side. "I hate this team."
The attendant walked past again, his path taking him close to their station. "You picked them," he observed.
"I didn’t know it’ll be this bad..."

Before anyone could respond to this questionable logic, the game suddenly announced the final circle. The sound effect cut through the conversation, drawing everyone’s attention back to the screen. Zack straightened in his seat, his earlier complaints forgotten as the seriousness of the moment settled over him.
"Okay. Enough comedy. This is serious."
Zoey raised an eyebrow, her expression skeptical. "You’ve said that six times."
"This time I mean it."
Camilla’s expression sharpened, her eyes narrowing as she processed information that the others couldn’t perceive. "Three enemies."
Zack froze, his earlier bravado evaporating. "How do you know?"
"Footsteps.
"I don’t hear anything."
"You’re talking."

Zack immediately shut his mouth, the lesson landing with unusual speed. Zoey covered her lips, trying not to laugh, while Stan watched Camilla’s hands. She was completely focused now, her earlier casualness replaced by something sharper and more precise. There was no hesitation in her movements, no wasted motion. She moved toward cover, checked one angle, then another, her actions carrying the fluid confidence of someone who had transcended conscious thought.
A few seconds later, gunfire erupted. Camilla returned fire, her movements quick and decisive. One enemy fell. Then another. Zack shouted a warning. "Behind you!"

Camilla turned. Fired. The screen flashed with the announcement of another elimination. For a moment, nobody spoke. The victory screen appeared, the words WARZONE VICTORY displayed in bold letters across the monitor.

Zack stared, his mouth slightly open. Zoey stared, her earlier amusement replaced by genuine surprise. The attendant looked over from the counter, his expression suggesting that he had seen something he hadn’t quite expected.
Camilla simply blinked at the victory banner, her expression strangely calm considering what had just happened.
"This seems pretty good right?" she asked.
Zack slowly removed his headset and stared at her as though he couldn’t believe what he was hearing. "Good?"
He pointed at the screen. "You just won."
Camilla looked at the victory banner again. "I see."
"You won our first match!"
"Yes."
"With us!"
"Yes."
Zack stared at her for several seconds before slowly looking toward Stan and then back at Camilla. "I think I dislike you now."
Camilla’s lips curved slightly.
It wasn’t quite a smile, but it was close enough for Stan to notice.
Zoey laughed. "She’s definitely getting another match."
Zack groaned. "No. Absolutely not."
Camilla turned toward him. "Why?"
"Because I have dignity."
Zoey glanced at the scoreboard. "You finished ninth."
Zack immediately pointed at her. "That is exactly why I need another match."

Stan laughed as he watched the three of them argue. The strange tension that had existed when he first returned seemed to have disappeared almost completely, replaced by something lighter and more familiar.
He leaned back in his chair and looked at Camilla.
"Fine.
Zack turned toward him. "You’re playing?"
Stan glanced at Camilla before looking at the screen again. He picked up one of the controllers from the table and settled himself more comfortably in his seat.
"Apparently, I have a reputation to defend."
Camilla looked at him, and for the first time since he had returned, the lingering tension in her eyes disappeared completely.
"Good."
Zack cracked his knuckles and leaned toward the screen. "Finally. Now we’re going to see who’s actually good."
Zoey immediately laughed. "You’re going to regret saying that."
The attendant passed them again and pointed toward the controllers. "Same rules as before. Don’t break the controllers."
Zack nodded solemnly. "No promises."
The attendant stopped walking and looked back at him. "Then I’m charging you for the next one."
Zack’s expression changed instantly. He looked down at the controller in his hands and adjusted his grip with exaggerated care.
"Suddenly, I have discovered restraint."

Stan laughed as the next match loaded onto the screens. Around them, the sounds of the gaming shop continued as usual, with players shouting across the room and electronic music playing softly from the speakers.
Outside, evening had begun to settle over the campus, gradually turning the windows into dark mirrors. Inside the shop, however, none of them seemed particularly interested in the passing time.
Amelia was gone and Camilla was here.
Zack was already preparing himself for revenge.
And Stan, who had only intended to return after taking care of something important, found himself sitting among them with a controller in his hands, ready to join the battle.
The loading screen disappeared.
The new match began.
And within seconds, Zack’s voice echoed through the shop.
"WHO LANDED THERE?"
Zoey laughed. Camilla calmly adjusted her position.
Stan shook his head with a smile.
Apparently, the afternoon wasn’t over yet.

chapters.title: Chapter 470: The Art Of Dying...
paragraphs: The next match began almost immediately, and Zack leaned forward in his seat with renewed determination. His earlier defeat seemed to have been completely erased from his memory, as though the previous several deaths had never happened. He tightened his grip on the controller and stared intently at the screen, his expression unusually serious.
"This time, nobody does anything stupid," he declared.
Zoey turned her head and looked at him with an expression of mild disbelief. "You’re included in that rule, right?"
"Obviously," Zack replied without hesitation.
Camilla adjusted her headset and settled more comfortably into her chair. Stan glanced in her direction, noticing how calm she remained despite the increasingly competitive atmosphere around them.
"You ready?" he asked.
"Yes," Camilla answered simply.
Zack scoffed from beside them. "She says that like she’s going into an actual battle."
Camilla looked at the screen for a moment before calmly replying, "Isn’t that what you called it?"
Zack opened his mouth, but nothing immediately came out. After a brief pause, he nodded reluctantly.
"...Fair."
The countdown appeared across the screen, and the atmosphere inside their small gaming station changed almost instantly. The casual laughter disappeared as everyone’s attention focused on the match.
Three.
Two.
One.
Their characters launched into the battlefield.
"MARK A LOCATION!" Zack shouted at once.
Zoey turned toward him. "Why are you shouting?"
"COMMUNICATION!"
"We’re sitting next to each other!"
"THE ENEMY CAN’T HEAR US!"
Stan shook his head, unable to suppress a laugh. Zack had somehow managed to turn sitting in a gaming station with his friends into a military operation.

They landed near a cluster of buildings, and Zack immediately sprinted toward the nearest structure without waiting for anyone else. The moment his character crossed through the doorway, he began searching through the rooms.
"Loot!" he announced excitedly.
Zoey followed behind him, while Stan landed slightly farther away and began searching another building. Camilla, meanwhile, landed on a rooftop and immediately began surveying the surrounding area.
After a few seconds, she asked, "Where are you?"
"I’m in the building!" Zack answered.
Camilla looked across the collection of structures surrounding them. "Which one?"
"The building!"
"There are twelve buildings."
Zack stopped moving for a moment and looked around.
"Okay, that’s a problem."
Zoey sighed as she opened the map. "Mark your location."
"I’m marking it."
Zack pressed the wrong button and placed a marker several hundred meters away from his actual position. Zoey stared at the map in silence.
"That isn’t you."
"I know."
"Then why did you mark it?"
"I was distracted."
"By what?"
"I found a gun."
Zoey slowly turned toward him. "You’ve been playing for hours."
"I still get excited."

Before Zoey could respond, Stan finished looting his building and joined them. He had already equipped a decent weapon and armor, while Camilla had descended from the rooftop and was making her way toward their position.

For a few minutes, everything went surprisingly smoothly. They moved through the buildings, collected equipment, and gradually made their way toward the center of the map. Zack even managed to avoid doing anything catastrophically reckless, which Zoey privately considered an achievement in itself.
Then a burst of gunfire suddenly echoed through the building.
Zack froze.
"Enemy."
Zoey immediately crouched. "Where?"
"North."
"How do you know?"
"I heard them."
Camilla, who had been moving through another entrance, suddenly stopped. Her eyes remained fixed on the screen.
"Two."
Zack looked at her. "Two what?"
"Two enemies."
"Where?"
Camilla calmly replied, "Behind you."
Zack’s character spun around.
A player appeared through the doorway.
"WHY ARE THEY HERE?"
Zack immediately opened fire, spraying bullets in every direction with considerably more enthusiasm than accuracy. Somehow, however, he managed to eliminate the first opponent.
"YES!" he shouted, throwing one hand into the air in celebration.
Zoey was barely able to react before another enemy entered through the same doorway.
Zack died.
His character collapsed, and the screen turned gray.
For several seconds, Zack remained completely silent.
Zoey slowly turned toward him.
"You celebrated too early."
"I was celebrating the first one."
"You died during the celebration."
"That was tactical overconfidence.
Camilla entered the room a moment later and eliminated the second opponent with almost insulting efficiency.
Zack stared at the screen.
"She saved me."
Zoey nodded. "Again."
"I wasn’t actually in danger."
"You were dead."
"I was temporarily unavailable."
Stan burst out laughing.

Despite Zack’s repeated disasters, the match continued. Surprisingly, the team managed to survive long enough to reach the final circle. By then, even Zack had become somewhat more cautious, although everyone knew it was only a matter of time before his instincts betrayed him again.
Zoey had also begun getting the hang of the game. Her movements were no longer as hesitant as they had been during their earlier matches, and she was beginning to understand positioning and timing.
Camilla, however, had become something entirely different.

She seemed to be learning the game at an absurd speed. She had started out unfamiliar with the controls, yet she was now moving with increasing confidence. She knew when to advance, when to stay behind cover, when to avoid unnecessary fights, and when an enemy had left themselves exposed.
Stan watched as she eliminated another player from a considerable distance.
"You’re getting good," he said.
Camilla didn’t take her eyes from the screen. "I am learning."
Zack shook his head. "No. You’re evolving."
The final circle began closing around them, leaving only three squads alive. Stan checked the surroundings and spoke in a more serious tone.
"Okay. Nobody rushes."
Zack nodded firmly. "Understood."
Three seconds passed.
Then Zack rushed forward.
"Zack!"
"I saw an opening!" he protested.
"You saw a death certificate!" Zoey shouted.
Gunfire erupted from several directions. Zack’s character barely survived a few seconds before collapsing.
Zoey stared at his character lying motionless on the ground.
"Impressive."
"What?" Zack asked defensively.
"You’ve somehow made the same mistake in a different location."
"I was being aggressive."
"You were being stupid."
"There’s a difference."
What do you think of the story so far

chapters.title: Chapter 471: The Art Of Loosing
paragraphs: While Zack and Zoey argued, Camilla moved around the flank. Stan followed her, keeping close enough to provide support. The two of them approached the final squad from an unexpected angle and opened fire at almost the same time.
The enemy team barely had time to react.
Within seconds, the final opponents were eliminated.
The screen flashed brightly.
VICTORY.
Zack stared at the screen in disbelief before slowly leaning back.
"We won."
Zoey glanced at him. "You contributed nothing."
"I contributed morale."
"You screamed."
"Morale."
Camilla removed one side of her headset and looked at them.
"Again?"
Zack immediately pointed toward her.
"See? She’s addicted."
"You’re the one who wanted another match," Zoey reminded him.
"Yes, but I didn’t expect consequences."
The attendant, who had been watching their increasingly chaotic session from nearby, wandered over with an amused expression. He glanced at the scoreboard and then at the four of them.
"You guys still alive?"
"Barely," Zoey replied.
The attendant looked at the scoreboard.
"Camilla carried?"
Zack’s expression tightened.
"Why does everyone keep saying that?"
The attendant pointed toward the screen.
"Because she did."
Zack stared at the statistics for several seconds before finally sighing.
"Fine."
He leaned back and folded his arms.
"I accept that she is currently better than me."
Camilla looked at him.
"Currently?"
Zack immediately straightened.
"Don’t push it."
Zoey laughed so hard that she nearly dropped her controller.

After another match, they eventually decided that they had spent enough time shooting one another. Their hands were beginning to feel stiff, and even Zack’s endless supply of competitive energy was starting to diminish.
The attendant noticed this and gestured toward another section of the gaming center.
"Why don’t you give your fingers a break from shooting each other?"
Zack frowned. "I don’t need a break."
"You’ve been holding that controller for nearly three hours."
"Exactly. I’m warmed up."
The attendant stared at him for a moment before shaking his head.
"That’s not how hands work."

They eventually followed his suggestion and moved to a racing station. The large screens displayed a collection of high-performance cars, colorful tracks, and various game modes. After spending so much time fighting enemies, the change of pace immediately felt refreshing.
Zack scrolled through the available cars and selected the fastest-looking vehicle he could find.
Zoey deliberately chose a car that looked ridiculous, with an exaggerated body and comically large tires.
Stan selected a balanced vehicle that offered decent acceleration, handling, and top speed.
Camilla remained on the selection screen for several seconds, studying the different vehicles with the same seriousness she had shown while examining weapons in the previous game.
"What is the fastest?" she asked.
The attendant pointed toward one of the cars.
"That one."
Camilla selected it without hesitation.
Zack laughed. "Speed isn’t everything."
The race began.
Camilla immediately drove straight into a wall.
Zoey burst out laughing.
"Finally!"
Camilla reversed slowly and examined the road ahead.
"Interesting."
Zack, meanwhile, had already accelerated far ahead.
"See?" he shouted. "I’m a natural!"
Five seconds later, he missed a turn, slammed into a barrier, and sent his vehicle flying off the track.
"WHAT?"
Zoey smoothly passed him.
"Natural."
Stan passed him as well.
Zack struggled to regain control while muttering under his breath. "That turn came out of nowhere."
"It was on the map," Stan pointed out.
"I wasn’t looking at the map."
"That sounds like a you problem."
Camilla gradually figured out the steering. Then she learned how to drift. Once she understood the mechanics, her improvement became almost ridiculous.
By the third lap, she had climbed into first place.
Zack stared at her vehicle on the screen.
"How?"
Camilla kept her eyes on the track.
"You told me speed wasn’t everything."
"I didn’t tell you that!"
"You said it."
"I meant it philosophically."
"You are losing."
"I am aware."
Camilla crossed the finish line first.
Zoey finished shortly afterward, followed by Stan.
Zack crossed the line in fourth place and immediately removed his headset.
"I hate racing."
The attendant grinned.
"You’ve lost every game you’ve claimed you were good at."
Zack pointed accusingly at him.
"That’s slander."
"It’s literally on the scoreboard."
They moved on before Zack could come up with another excuse.
Their next choice was a fighting game, and the moment the character-selection screen appeared, Zack’s confidence mysteriously returned.
"This," he announced, "is something I’m actually good at."
Zoey groaned.
"Here we go again."
Zack selected a heavily armored character who looked as though he had been designed specifically to survive explosions. Zoey chose a fast, agile fighter, while Stan selected a balanced character.
Camilla studied the roster for nearly a minute.
"Which one is strongest?
The attendant smiled.
"That depends on who’s playing."
Camilla considered his answer before selecting a character whose appearance she simply liked.
Zack nodded confidently.
"Finally. Something I’m actually good at."
The match began.
Zack immediately attacked.
Camilla blocked.
He attacked again.
She blocked again.
Zack attacked a third time.
Camilla blocked once more.
His expression gradually changed from confidence to confusion.
"Why aren’t you fighting?"
Camilla looked at him.
"You keep attacking."
"So?"
"I am observing."
Zoey immediately burst out laughing.
"She’s studying you."
"Stop laughing!"
Zack attacked again, this time with a longer combination of strikes.
Camilla waited until the final attack before countering.
Her character suddenly moved with incredible speed.
One strike connected.
Then another.
Then another.
Before Zack could recover, Camilla chained the attacks together into a full combo that launched his character across the arena.
Zack stared at the screen.
"Wait."
Camilla followed him and continued attacking.
His health bar rapidly disappeared.
Then came the final blow.
K.O.
The gaming attendant actually laughed.
Zack sat completely motionless, controller still in his hands.
"I was distracted."
Zoey nodded sympathetically. "By losing?"
"No. By the controller."
"You’ve been holding it for three hours."
"Exactly. My grip is tired."
Stan smiled. "Rematch?"
Zack immediately selected the rematch option.
"Absolutely."
His competitive spirit had apparently returned in full force. If anything, losing had only made him more determined to prove that his previous defeat had been a fluke.
Zoey leaned back and laughed.
Camilla quietly adjusted her grip on the controller.
The next match loaded.
And judging by Zack’s expression, the gaming session was nowhere near over.

Zoey laughed so hard that she nearly dropped her controller.
After another match, they eventually decided that they had spent enough time shooting one another.
Their hands were beginning to feel stiff, and even Zack’s endless supply of competitive energy was starting to diminish.
The attendant noticed this and gestured toward another section of the gaming center.
"Why don’t you give your fingers a break from shooting each other?"
Zack frowned.
"I don’t need a break."
"You’ve been holding that controller for nearly three hours."
"Exactly.
I’m warmed up."
The attendant stared at him for a moment before shaking his head.
"That’s not how hands work."
They eventually followed his suggestion and moved to a racing station.
The large screens displayed a collection of high-performance cars, colorful tracks, and various game modes.
After spending so much time fighting enemies, the change of pace immediately felt refreshing.
Zack scrolled through the available cars and selected the fastest-looking vehicle he could find.
Zoey deliberately chose a car that looked ridiculous, with an exaggerated body and comically large tires.
Stan selected a balanced vehicle that offered decent acceleration, handling, and top speed.
Camilla remained on the selection screen for several seconds, studying the different vehicles with the same seriousness she had shown while examining weapons in the previous game.
"What is the fastest?" she asked.
The attendant pointed toward one of the cars.
"That one."
Camilla selected it without hesitation.
Zack laughed.
"Speed isn’t everything."
The race began.
Camilla immediately drove straight into a wall.
Zoey burst out laughing.
"Finally!"
Camilla reversed slowly and examined the road ahead.
"Interesting."
Zack, meanwhile, had already accelerated far ahead.
"See?" he shouted.
"I’m a natural!"
Five seconds later, he missed a turn, slammed into a barrier, and sent his vehicle flying off the track.
"WHAT?"
Zoey smoothly passed him.
"Natural."
Stan passed him as well.
Zack struggled to regain control while muttering under his breath.
"That turn came out of nowhere."
"It was on the map," Stan pointed out.
"I wasn’t looking at the map."
"That sounds like a you problem."
Camilla gradually figured out the steering.
Then she learned how to drift.
Once she understood the mechanics, her improvement became almost ridiculous.
By the third lap, she had climbed into first place.
Zack stared at her vehicle on the screen.
"How?"
Camilla kept her eyes on the track.
"You told me speed wasn’t everything."
"I didn’t tell you that!"
"You said it."
"I meant it philosophically."
"You are losing."
"I am aware."
Camilla crossed the finish line first.
Zoey finished shortly afterward, followed by Stan.
Zack crossed the line in fourth place and immediately removed his headset.
"I hate racing."
The attendant grinned.
"You’ve lost every game you’ve claimed you were good at."
Zack pointed accusingly at him.
"That’s slander."
"It’s literally on the scoreboard."
They moved on before Zack could come up with another excuse.
Their next choice was a fighting game, and the moment the character-selection screen appeared, Zack’s confidence mysteriously returned.
"This," he announced, "is something I’m actually good at."
Zoey groaned.
"Here we go again."
Zack selected a heavily armored character who looked as though he had been designed specifically to survive explosions.
Zoey chose a fast, agile fighter, while Stan selected a balanced character.
Camilla studied the roster for nearly a minute.
"Which one is strongest?
The attendant smiled.
"That depends on who’s playing."
Camilla considered his answer before selecting a character whose appearance she simply liked.
Zack nodded confidently.
"Finally.
Something I’m actually good at."
The match began.
Zack immediately attacked.
Camilla blocked.
He attacked again.
She blocked again.
Zack attacked a third time.
Camilla blocked once more.
His expression gradually changed from confidence to confusion.
"Why aren’t you fighting?"
Camilla looked at him.
"You keep attacking."
"So?"
"I am observing."
Zoey immediately burst out laughing.
"She’s studying you."
"Stop laughing!"
Zack attacked again, this time with a longer combination of strikes.
Camilla waited until the final attack before countering.
Her character suddenly moved with incredible speed.
One strike connected.
Then another.
Then another.
Before Zack could recover, Camilla chained the attacks together into a full combo that launched his character across the arena.
Zack stared at the screen.
"Wait."
Camilla followed him and continued attacking.
His health bar rapidly disappeared.
Then came the final blow.
K.O.
The gaming attendant actually laughed.
Zack sat completely motionless, controller still in his hands.
"I was distracted."
Zoey nodded sympathetically.
"By losing?"
"No.
By the controller."
"You’ve been holding it for three hours."
"Exactly.
My grip is tired."
Stan smiled.
"Rematch?"
Zack immediately selected the rematch option.
"Absolutely."
His competitive spirit had apparently returned in full force.
If anything, losing had only made him more determined to prove that his previous defeat had been a fluke.
Zoey leaned back and laughed.
Camilla quietly adjusted her grip on the controller.
The next match loaded.
And judging by Zack’s expression, the gaming session was nowhere near over.

chapters.title: Chapter 472: The Last Battle
paragraphs: They ended up playing another five rounds, and the results were surprisingly balanced.

Zack claimed one round with a triumphant flourish that was perhaps a bit too enthusiastic for someone who had only won a single match. Zoey secured two victories with a quiet determination that suggested she had been paying closer attention than anyone realized.

Stan managed to take one round for himself, a modest achievement that he accepted with his characteristic understated nod. And then there was Camilla, who won the remaining round without uttering a single word, her victory so effortless and uncelebrated that it seemed almost to have happened in a separate, quieter dimension of the game.

When Zack leaned back in his chair, the gesture carried the weight of a man who had just witnessed something profoundly unsettling. His eyes narrowed slightly as he studied Camilla, who sat across from him with the same serene composure she had maintained throughout the entire session.
"I’m beginning to suspect she’s doing this on purpose," he announced, his voice carrying that particular tone of suspicious admiration that only hom could manage.
Camilla tilted her head in response, a gesture that was both innocent and calculated, as if she were genuinely puzzled by the accusation.
"Doing what?" she asked, and the simplicity of the question only seemed to deepen Zack’s suspicion.

"Making us look bad," he clarified, as though explaining something obvious to a particularly dense student. Camilla’s response was delivered with the same even tone she always employed. "I am simply playing."
Zack’s expression darkened. "That is worse."

Zoey laughed, while Stan shook his head. Zack had spent most of the evening trying to maintain his reputation as the group’s best gamer, only for Camilla to casually learn every game they introduced to her and start beating them at it. What made it even more frustrating was the fact that she never bragged. She didn’t celebrate excessively, tease anyone, or even look particularly proud of herself. She simply played, learned, and improved.
The attendant happened to walk past their station and glanced at the results on the screen. After seeing the exhausted expressions on their faces, he grinned.
"You should try the rhythm game."
Zack immediately looked suspicious. "Is it competitive?"
The attendant shrugged. "Everything is competitive if you have the right personality."
Zoey immediately pointed at Zack. "That’s definitely him."

Zack ignored her and followed the others toward the rhythm-game station. The game looked harmless enough. Compared to the intense shooting and racing games they had been playing, it seemed almost relaxing. The screen displayed colorful notes moving toward a timing bar while music played through the speakers.
They quickly discovered that appearances were deceiving.
For approximately thirty seconds, all four of them were terrible.

Zack missed notes so badly that his character’s score plummeted almost immediately. Zoey tried to compensate by tapping faster, only to lose track of the rhythm completely. Stan somehow managed to press the correct buttons at the wrong moments, resulting in a string of consecutive mistakes.
Camilla was struggling as well.
At least, she appeared to be.
Then something clicked.

Her movements became more precise, and her fingers began following the rhythm with increasing confidence. Instead of frantically pressing buttons whenever a note appeared, she started anticipating the patterns. One successful note became five. Five became ten. Soon, she was hitting nearly everything perfectly.
Zack stared at her screen in disbelief. "Of course."
Zoey was laughing so hard that she could barely continue playing. Stan, meanwhile, missed three notes in a row and glanced down at his controller with quiet frustration.
Camilla looked over at him. "You are off rhythm."
"I noticed."
"Try again."
Stan looked at her. "You sound like a teacher."
"You need instruction.
Zack immediately pointed toward Camilla. "She has become unbearable."
Camilla didn’t even look at him. "You lost to a rhythm game."
"I was distracted by the music."
Zoey finally managed to recover enough to speak. "That’s what the game is about."
"Exactly," Zack replied with complete seriousness.
That only made everyone laugh harder.

They played several more songs, and although Zack continued insisting that he had simply not yet found his rhythm, the truth became increasingly obvious. Camilla was once again adapting faster than everyone else.
Eventually, even she began laughing.

It wasn’t loud or dramatic. It was a brief, almost surprised laugh that escaped her before she could stop it. For someone who had spent much of the evening maintaining a calm and composed expression, the small moment stood out.
Stan noticed it immediately. He didn’t say anything. He simply smiled.
For him, that small laugh made the entire evening worthwhile.

After the rhythm game, they returned to their original station. Despite having declared multiple times that they were finished with Warzone, the familiar menu appeared on the screen again, almost inviting them to make another questionable decision.
Zack stared at it for several seconds before finally picking up the controller.
"Last game."
Zoey immediately shook her head. "You said that three games ago."
"This one is actually the last."
The attendant called from behind the counter without even looking up from what he was doing.
"You’ve said that four times."
Zack turned around. "Why are you counting?"
"Because I have to close eventually."
Zack looked at the clock and then back at the screen. "That’s unfortunate."
"It’s reality," the attendant replied.
Despite the warning, they started one final match.
As expected, it immediately descended into chaos.

They landed in a crowded area where several other teams had chosen to drop. Zack managed to separate himself from the group within the first minute, despite everyone’s repeated warnings to stay together. Zoey found herself without a proper weapon after another player looted the building she had entered, while Stan accidentally picked up an item he didn’t need and spent several seconds trying to figure out what he had actually collected.
Camilla, meanwhile, found herself alone inside a building with three enemies.
For several seconds, nobody knew where she was.
Zack eventually realized that she wasn’t anywhere near them.
"Where’s Camilla?"
"I don’t know," Zoey answered while searching another building.
Stan checked the map. "She’s somewhere east."
"Somewhere east isn’t exactly a location," Zack complained.
Before anyone could find her, an elimination notification appeared on the screen. Then another. Then another.
Zack stopped moving. "Wait."
Zoey glanced toward the kill feed. "What?"
"Camilla."
Another elimination appeared.
Zack slowly removed one side of his headset.
"How many people are in that building?" Camilla’s voice came calmly through the headset.
"Were."
Zoey burst out laughing.
Stan shook his head in disbelief. "She cleared them?"
Camilla didn’t answer. She simply continued moving.

The rest of the match progressed far more smoothly after they regrouped. Perhaps they had finally learned from their earlier mistakes, or perhaps they were simply too tired to make unnecessary ones. Either way, they reached the final circle together.
This time, nobody rushed. Nobody wandered off alone. For perhaps the first time that entire evening, they actually played like a coordinated team.

Stan took position behind cover and watched the surrounding area. Zoey maintained pressure from another angle, keeping the enemy from advancing. Zack, miraculously, resisted the urge to charge blindly into combat and instead waited for an opening.
Camilla remained beside them, quietly observing the battlefield.
Then the final enemy appeared.
Stan fired first, forcing the opponent behind cover. Zoey immediately followed up with suppressing fire, preventing the enemy from escaping. Zack finally saw his opportunity and rushed forward.
Camilla moved with him.
The enemy barely had time to react.
Camilla landed the final shots.
The screen flashed.
VICTORY.
For a moment, nobody said anything.
Then Zack suddenly jumped out of his chair.
"YES!"
Zoey burst into laughter.

chapters.title: Chapter 473: Laughter
paragraphs: Stan leaned back and released a long breath. "We actually played properly that time."
Camilla removed her headset and allowed her shoulders to relax. Even she looked tired now.
The attendant checked the time and shook his head.
"You people realize you’ve been here for almost four hours?"
Zoey blinked.
"Four?"
Zack looked toward the clock.
His expression changed.
"Oh."
Stan stood and stretched, only to wince when several joints cracked loudly.
"That explains why my legs are numb."
Zoey stood as well and flexed her fingers.
"I can’t feel my hands."
Camilla slowly opened and closed her fingers, testing them.
"Mine are tired."
Zack stared at her in disbelief.
"Even Camilla is tired."
Zoey looked at him. "Why is that surprising?"
"Because I thought nothing could defeat her anymore."
Camilla looked at him with a completely straight expression.
"Fatigue appears effective."
The attendant laughed.
"There’s your final boss."
That finally convinced them that it was time to stop.
They returned the controllers to the attendant, and Zack reluctantly handed his over as though he were surrendering a treasured possession.
"I’ll be back."
The attendant nodded. "I know."
"Tomorrow."
"Probably."
"Maybe tonight."
"Definitely not."
Zack sighed heavily before finally stepping away from the station.
They started toward the entrance, but just before they reached the doors, Zoey suddenly stopped.
"Wait."
Everyone turned toward her.
She pointed toward a refrigerated display positioned beside the counter.
"I’m hungry."
The others followed her gaze.

The display was filled with bottled drinks, chocolate bars, bags of chips, biscuits, pastries, and various other snacks. After spending nearly four hours gaming, the sight of food immediately reminded all of them that they had barely eaten anything during their session.
Stan glanced at the others.
"Snacks?"
Camilla nodded immediately.
"Yes."
Zack’s face brightened.
"Now that’s a game I can win.
Zoey looked at him.
"You’re paying."
Zack’s smile disappeared almost instantly.
"Why?"
"Because you dragged us in here."
"You enjoyed it."
"That isn’t the point."
The attendant leaned over the counter.
"She’s right."
Zack stared at him in disbelief.
"You’re supposed to be neutral."
"I work here," the attendant replied. "I’m allowed to support whoever buys snacks."
The four of them laughed.

They eventually gathered around the display and began choosing what they wanted. Zoey picked out a bottled drink and a few snacks, while Stan grabbed some biscuits and a pastry. Camilla selected a drink and a small chocolate bar, studying the available options with the same seriousness she had used when choosing weapons earlier.
Zack, meanwhile, quietly added two extra bags of chips to the growing pile.
Zoey noticed.
She immediately took them from his hands and returned them to the shelf.
"Those aren’t yours."
"They are now."
She gave him a flat look.
Zack looked genuinely wounded. "You’re cruel."
"You’ve eaten enough virtual food today."
"That doesn’t count."
"Your character ate."
"My character is not me."
"Then why did you celebrate whenever he won?"
Zack opened his mouth.
For once, he couldn’t think of a response.
He slowly closed it again.
"Fine."
They paid for the snacks and finally stepped outside.

The evening air immediately felt different after spending so long inside the gaming center. The cooler air brushed against their faces, and the sounds of traffic and people moving through the area replaced the constant noise of gunfire, engines, music, and game announcements.
For a moment, none of them spoke.
They simply stood outside, stretching their arms and shoulders after hours of sitting.
Then Zack opened a packet of chips.
"Tomorrow."
Zoey looked at him.
"No."
"Tomorrow."
"No."
"We haven’t settled the racing rematch."
"You lost four times."
"Exactly. It’s unsettled."
Stan laughed as they began walking back toward campus.

The snacks gradually passed from one person to another as they walked. Someone would open a packet, another person would reach over without asking, and within minutes there would be barely anything left.
The gaming center’s lights slowly disappeared behind them, replaced by the softer glow of streetlamps and the familiar lights of the campus buildings.
After walking for a while, Zack stretched dramatically.
"I’m exhausted."
Zoey looked at him incredulously.
"You spent four hours sitting down."
"Exactly."
He placed a hand against his lower back with exaggerated suffering. "My legs are exhausted from the emotional strain."
Zoey picked up a chip and threw it at him.
Zack caught it effortlessly.
"Thank you."
"That wasn’t for you."
"I accept your offering."
"You’re impossible."
Camilla watched the exchange from beside Stan. The faintest smile appeared on her lips.
Stan noticed it.
He didn’t comment.
He simply continued walking beside her.
After a while, Camilla glanced toward him.
"You came back."
Stan looked at her.
"I said I would."
She nodded.
There was no coldness in her expression this time. No guardedness or hesitation. She simply looked at him for a moment before quietly replying.
"Good."
Before Stan could say anything else, Zack’s voice came from several meters ahead.
"Are you two coming, or are you planning to walk home at that speed?"
Zoey looked back at them and smiled.
"Let them walk."
Zack shrugged.
"Fine. But I’m not carrying anyone if their legs stop working."
Stan shook his head.
"You’re the one who spent four hours sitting down."
"Exactly," Zack replied. "That’s why I’m tired."
Zoey laughed again.

The four of them continued down the road together, their conversation drifting between arguments about the games, complaints about sore hands, plans for another rematch, and accusations about who had contributed the least.
For all the chaos, the evening had ended simply.
They were tired, their hands were sore, and Zack was already planning his revenge in the next gaming session.
Camilla walked quietly beside Stan, occasionally taking another sip from her drink while listening to the others argue ahead of them.
The gaming center was already far behind them, but the laughter from the evening seemed to linger.
Whatever else tomorrow brought, one thing was already certain.
Zack would demand another rematch.
And, judging by the expressions on everyone’s faces, nobody was going to say no.

After walking for a while, Zack stretched dramatically.
"I’m exhausted."
Zoey looked at him incredulously.
"You spent four hours sitting down."
"Exactly."
He placed a hand against his lower back with exaggerated suffering.
"My legs are exhausted from the emotional strain."
Zoey picked up a chip and threw it at him.
Zack caught it effortlessly.
"Thank you."
"That wasn’t for you."
"I accept your offering."
"You’re impossible."
Camilla watched the exchange from beside Stan.
The faintest smile appeared on her lips.
Stan noticed it.
He didn’t comment.
He simply continued walking beside her.
After a while, Camilla glanced toward him.
"You came back."
Stan looked at her.
"I said I would."
She nodded.
There was no coldness in her expression this time.
No guardedness or hesitation.
She simply looked at him for a moment before quietly replying.
"Good."
Before Stan could say anything else, Zack’s voice came from several meters ahead.
"Are you two coming, or are you planning to walk home at that speed?"
Zoey looked back at them and smiled.
"Let them walk."
Zack shrugged.
"Fine.
But I’m not carrying anyone if their legs stop working."
Stan shook his head.
"You’re the one who spent four hours sitting down."
"Exactly," Zack replied.
"That’s why I’m tired."
Zoey laughed again.

The four of them continued down the road together, their conversation drifting between arguments about the games, complaints about sore hands, plans for another rematch, and accusations about who had contributed the least.
For all the chaos, the evening had ended simply.
They were tired, their hands were sore, and Zack was already planning his revenge in the next gaming session.
Camilla walked quietly beside Stan, occasionally taking another sip from her drink while listening to the others argue ahead of them.
The gaming center was already far behind them, but the laughter from the evening seemed to linger.
Whatever else tomorrow brought, one thing was already certain.
Zack would demand another rematch.
And, judging by the expressions on everyone’s faces, nobody was going to say no.

chapters.title: Chapter 474: Ordinary
paragraphs: After returning home, Stan remained seated inside the Audi for a while, making no immediate attempt to get out.

The engine had already been turned off, leaving the interior unusually quiet after the noise and movement of the city outside. Through the windshield and side windows, the evening streets continued to bustle with activity.

Cars passed along the roads in steady streams, their headlights sweeping across the pavement, while the countless lights illuminating the surrounding buildings turned the city into a vast landscape of artificial brilliance.
People moved along the sidewalks in groups or alone, most of them carrying strange rectangular devices in their hands and occasionally lowering their heads to stare at glowing screens.

To Stan, none of it was particularly noteworthy. He had lived on Earth long enough that the sights had become completely ordinary to him. To Camilla, however, almost everything outside that vehicle remained fascinating.
She sat quietly in the passenger seat, her gaze fixed on the world beyond the window as she tried to take in everything she had seen since arriving on Earth.
Camilla had spent most of her existence in the New Terra Realm, and her understanding of civilization had been shaped by an entirely different world.

Ancient castles stood alongside magnificent cultivation sects, powerful bloodline clans controlled territories that ordinary people could scarcely imagine, and magical artifacts were often regarded as necessities rather than curiosities. Even the occasional technological relic left behind from older eras was treated as something mysterious and valuable.

Earth was fundamentally different. Humanity had developed along a completely separate path, one that had allowed ordinary humans to construct an extraordinarily advanced civilization without relying on cultivation or spiritual energy.

During her time here, Camilla had learned just how far that development had gone. Humans had created enormous machines capable of crossing entire oceans within hours, constructed towering cities filled with millions of people, and developed communication systems that allowed individuals on opposite sides of the planet to speak to each other almost instantaneously.

They had built aircraft that carried people through the skies without requiring wings or spiritual energy, vehicles that could travel across vast distances without beasts pulling them, and countless machines that performed tasks that would have once required cultivators or magical artifacts. Even something as simple as the lights illuminating the streets had fascinated her. Entire cities could be bathed in brilliant illumination without a single strand of spiritual energy being consumed.
Yet perhaps the strangest thing of all was the people themselves.

For all of Earth’s technological achievements, the overwhelming majority of its inhabitants were still ordinary humans. They could not sense Qi, manipulate spiritual energy, refine their bodies through cultivation, or perceive the countless supernatural forces that existed beyond their world. They lived ordinary lives, went to work, attended schools, purchased food, worried about money, formed relationships, raised families, and eventually grew old without ever realizing that civilizations far beyond Earth existed.

Most of them had no idea that there existed beings capable of moving mountains, traversing space, or living for centuries. They were completely unaware that the universe was far larger and stranger than anything their current civilization could comprehend.

Camilla had initially found that ignorance almost impossible to understand. Coming from the New Terra Realm, where powerful cultivators and supernatural beings were an accepted part of reality, the idea of an entire planet being populated primarily by ordinary humans seemed almost absurd.

Yet after spending more time on Earth, she had gradually begun to see the appeal of it. There was something strangely peaceful about a civilization where most people could simply live their lives without constantly worrying about cultivation resources, bloodline conflicts, sect rivalries, territorial disputes, or powerful beings deciding their fate.

She slowly lowered her gaze, her fingers resting quietly against her knee. She did not particularly want to admit what had been going through her mind since arriving on Earth. She had enjoyed herself. More than she had expected. The realization was somewhat embarrassing, especially considering how skeptical she had been when Stan first brought her here. She had expected Earth to be little more than an interesting curiosity, a primitive world with unusual technology that she would eventually grow tired of. Instead, she had found herself fascinated by things that were almost embarrassingly simple.

The food had been strange compared to what she was accustomed to, but she had discovered that much of it was surprisingly delicious. The technology continued to capture her attention, particularly the countless devices humans used so casually that they barely seemed to notice them anymore. Even watching ordinary people interact with one another had become unexpectedly entertaining. There were no grand cultivation techniques involved, no bloodline abilities being displayed, and no spiritual pressure hanging over every interaction. People simply talked, laughed, argued, joked, worked, and went about their lives. There was an ordinary simplicity to it that Camilla had gradually found herself appreciating.
And then there was Stan.
Camilla turned her head slightly and looked at him.
She knew better than anyone that beneath his relaxed expression was an existence whose capabilities remained difficult for her to comprehend.

Nevertheless, something about the time she had spent with him had changed the way she perceived him. She had come to terms that he was the mysterious cultivator who could manipulate spatial laws with casual ease, and she couldnt even sense a spatial fluctation the few times he had done that back in Antarctica, he’s the only man whose strength and origins remained difficult to determine, and the person who had dragged her into circumstances far beyond anything she had anticipated.
While she’ve come in terms with that, she still feels conflicted when looking at him, like right now where he simply looked like a normal person..
Almost like an ordinary new age human. Almost.
Camilla’s lips curved faintly at the thought. Of course, calling Stan ordinary was ridiculous. She had personally witnessed enough of his abilities to know that there was nothing ordinary about him.
Still, there was something strangely comfortable about seeing him behave this way.
