chapters.title: Chapter 475: How Long...
paragraphs: Camilla’s fingers began tapping lightly against her knee as several conflicting thoughts passed through her mind. She had not forgotten her family. She had not forgotten the New Terra Realm, nor had her attachment to her home suddenly disappeared simply because she had spent some time on Earth. The thought of returning immediately even brought a faint ache to her heart. She missed them. She missed the familiar atmosphere of the realm, the people she had known for so long, and the life she had lived before meeting Stan.
But at the same time, she found herself reluctant to leave.

She stared through the window again, watching the passing lights and the countless people moving through the evening streets. For reasons she could not fully explain, the sight no longer seemed as alien as it had when she first arrived. There was something peaceful about it, and she was not yet ready to give that feeling up.
Eventually, Stan broke the silence.
"You can go back whenever you want," he said casually.
Camilla turned toward him, her expression carrying a hint of surprise.

Stan remained relaxed as he continued, making it clear that he was not trying to pressure her into making a decision. "I can take you back at any time. You don’t have to stay here because of me. If you want to return to your family, just tell me."

His words were simple, but they caused a complicated mixture of emotions to rise within Camilla. Her family immediately came to mind, and for a moment she imagined herself returning to the New Terra Realm. She could picture the familiar surroundings, the people waiting there, and the life she had temporarily left behind. A part of her genuinely wanted to return.
Yet another part of her was reluctant to leave.
Her gaze slowly drifted back toward the window, where Earth’s evening scenery continued to unfold before her. She remained silent for several seconds before finally answering.
"I’ll stay."
Stan raised an eyebrow. "For how long?"
Camilla hesitated before crossing her arms and leaning slightly against the seat. "For a little while longer."
"A little while?" Stan repeated, a faint smile appearing on his face.
"Yes." Camilla deliberately avoided looking at him. "I haven’t decided when I want to return yet."
There was a slight stubbornness in her tone, almost as though she was worried he might interpret her uncertainty as a weakness. Stan, however, did not press her.
"That’s fine," he replied.

Camilla finally looked at him again, studying his expression. She had expected him to ask more questions, perhaps tease her about suddenly becoming attached to Earth or point out that she had originally been eager to return home. Instead, he simply accepted her answer without making an issue of it.
"You aren’t going to ask me why?" she asked.
"No."
"Why?"
Stan shrugged lightly. "Because you’ll tell me when you’re ready."

Camilla stared at him for several seconds, her expression gradually softening. She had expected many things from Stan, but that response had caught her off guard. There was no pressure in his words, no demand for an explanation, and no attempt to influence her decision. He was simply giving her the freedom to choose for herself.
A faint smile eventually appeared on her lips.
"You really are strange."
Stan gave her a sideways glance. "Whatever."
He then opened the car door and stepped out, leaving Camilla momentarily confused.
She blinked before looking after him. "Come with me."
Camilla frowned. "Where?"
"You’ll see."
Her eyes narrowed immediately. "That’s not reassuring."
Stan merely smiled as he waited beside the vehicle. "You trust me."

Camilla stared at him for a long moment, clearly unconvinced by the confidence in his voice. She knew perfectly well that trusting Stan had a tendency to lead her into situations she could never have predicted. Nevertheless, after everything that had happened since she met him, she had already crossed the point where she could pretend she did not trust him.
She sighed softly and stepped out of the Audi.
"Unfortunately.
A quiet chuckle escaped Stan as he watched her approach.
The next instant, the space around them subtly distorted.

There was no brilliant flash of light, no explosive surge of energy, and no dramatic disturbance that could have attracted the attention of anyone nearby. Stan simply exercised his control over spatial laws and the authority Void Sovereign have him causing the distance between their current location and their destination to cease being meaningful.
For the two of them, the transition was almost instantaneous.
One moment, they were standing beside the Audi beneath the artificial lights of Earth’s evening streets.
The next, they were gone.
Camilla felt the surrounding space twist the instant Stan activated his spatial ability. The sensation was completely different from ordinary movement.

There was no feeling of acceleration, no sensation of falling, and no gradual transition from one location to another. Instead, it was as though the space around her had suddenly become fluid, folding and compressing around her body while countless invisible layers of distance were being rearranged.

Her expression immediately became serious. Instinctively, the powerful bloodline energy within her surged, and she activated her vampiric abilities in preparation for whatever situation might await them.
However, before she could fully react, the strange sensation disappeared.
Her feet touched solid ground.

Camilla’s body remained tense for a moment as she carefully surveyed her surroundings. The first thing she noticed was the silence. There was no sound of traffic, no voices, no wind, and none of the countless noises she had grown accustomed to hearing on Earth.

Instead, there was only an almost unnatural stillness that seemed to envelop the entire space. She slowly lowered her guard as her eyes adjusted to the surroundings and discovered that she was standing inside a circular room.

The room itself was surprisingly simple. There were no magnificent decorations or extravagant displays of wealth. A smooth floor stretched beneath her feet, while the curved walls extended around them in a seamless circle. At the center stood a simple wooden table accompanied by two chairs.

A small tea set had already been arranged neatly on the tabletop, and two cups sat beside one another, each releasing thin streams of steam that curled lazily into the air. The entire arrangement looked as though someone had deliberately prepared the room for two guests before their arrival.

chapters.title: Chapter 476: Tea Room (1)
paragraphs: Camilla stared at the steaming cups for several seconds before slowly turning her head toward Stan. Her expression became increasingly confused as she looked from him to the table, then back toward the room.

She had expected something entirely different after being transported through space by someone like Stan. Given the little she knew about his abilities and the strange things he’s capable of, she had imagined an ancient palace hidden in some isolated dimension, a terrifying cultivation chamber, after all for him to teleport her means he wants to reveal things to her...
Unlike what she thought, she had actually been brought into what looked like a private tea room.
"What?" she finally asked, unable to hide her confusion.
Stan walked toward the wooden table as though nothing about the situation was unusual. He pulled out one of the chairs and casually gestured toward the room. "Welcome."
Camilla’s eyebrows twitched.
"Welcome where?"
"To my Tea room."
Camilla stared at him for a moment before looking around again. "Your what?"
"My tea room."
"I heard that part, I’m just surprised by this..."

Stan chuckled softly, while Camilla continued examining the surroundings with growing disbelief. There was nothing particularly intimidating about the place. No weird secret, no mountains of treasures were piled against the walls, and there were no ominous formations carved into the floor.

There was not even a single artifact displayed for her to examine. It was simply a quiet, circular room containing a wooden table, two chairs, and a freshly prepared beverage. Why would Stan teleport her to such a place

Anyways Stan couldn’t help but frown upon seeing that the cups of tea Void Sovereign had left was still hot, even the cup he had drank had been filled back as if nothing had happened, it was strange, it made him wonder, if the Void Sovereign was not only capable of messing with space but capable of messing with time as well, if that was the case then it was terrifying...

Considering that Stan had just introduced it as the tea room without saying anything else, Camilla found the simplicity almost disappointing. Though she knew that Master Cultivators who hide their true cultivation and all those are more likely to love to keep things simple...
She wasn’t against that as she herself loves simple things but why would he bring her hear to show his tea room...
Then she sensed something.
Her expression changed immediately.

Camilla’s eyes narrowed as she became aware of something that had escaped her notice at first. She slowly closed her eyes and focused her senses, allowing her perception to spread through the room. At first, she could only feel the strange stillness surrounding them. Then, beneath that stillness, she detected an energy so immense and concentrated that her entire expression changed.
Qi.
Her eyes snapped open.
"This place..." She inhaled cautiously, and the moment she did, an enormous amount of Qi rushed into her body.
Camilla’s pupils contracted.

She immediately stopped breathing and instinctively circulated her bloodline energy through her body, preventing the sudden influx from disturbing the delicate balance of her internal energy. Even with her powerful physique as a Royal Blood vampire, she could immediately tell that carelessly absorbing the energy around them would be dangerous.
The Qi here was not merely dense.
It was overwhelmingly dense.

It did not feel as though the room had been filled with Qi from an external source. Instead, the energy seemed to have become an intrinsic part of the entire space. It flowed through the walls, permeated the floor and ceiling, and existed within every empty space between the objects around them. Even the air itself seemed saturated with spiritual energy, making the environment feel almost tangible to her senses.
Camilla slowly turned her head toward Stan.
"This place is overflowing with Qi."
Stan nodded calmly. "Yes."

For several seconds, Camilla simply stared at him. She had expected some enormous explanation about the origin of the Qi or perhaps an explanation of the room’s formation, but Stan seemed completely unconcerned about the matter. To him, the tremendous concentration of spiritual energy surrounding them was apparently nothing more than a convenient resource.

Camilla took a cautious step forward and immediately felt the pressure of the Qi against her senses. Her Royal Blood lineage gave her a powerful physique capable of absorbing vast quantities of energy, but even she understood that this environment demanded caution. If an ordinary cultivator were to sit down here and begin absorbing Qi without proper preparation, the sheer quantity of energy entering their body could easily overwhelm their meridians and cause severe internal damage. Depending on their cultivation level, they might even lose control of their energy entirely.
She looked toward Stan again. "You cultivate here?"
"You ask way too much questions..."
Camilla’s expression became incredulous. ’aa expected of a master Cultivator he can cultivate in a place with this much Chaotic Qi?’
Stan pulled out one of the chairs and sat down as though her reaction was perfectly normal.

While he hasn’t tried it yet he can actually easily cultivate here, the QI her feels chaotic and hard to control for Camilla because it’s Condensed Spatial QI which she has no affinity for, while she can still absorb and utilise it as normal Qi energy, it’ll be agonisingly slower than her normal speed...
If this was normal neutral Qi, or a Qi with an element she has affinity to, this place would’ve felt like a paradise...
Camilla stared at him, then slowly looked around the room once more. Her mind began putting together the pieces she had previously overlooked.

The room was not designed for ordinary relaxation. The absence of unnecessary decorations made sense if the purpose was cultivation, while the extraordinary concentration of Qi explained why Stan had bothered creating or maintaining such a space. It was clearly a private cultivation environment disguised as something far more mundane.
"So this is where you cultivate," Camilla said, her voice becoming more serious.
"One of the places."
Camilla’s eyes narrowed. "How many places do you have?"
Stan looked at her with an amused expression.
Camilla immediately frowned.
Stan laughed, the sound echoing softly through the quiet room.

"This place..." She inhaled cautiously, and the moment she did, an enormous amount of Qi rushed into her body.
Camilla’s pupils contracted.
She immediately stopped breathing and instinctively circulated her bloodline energy through her body, preventing the sudden influx from disturbing the delicate balance of her internal energy.
Even with her powerful physique as a Royal Blood vampire, she could immediately tell that carelessly absorbing the energy around them would be dangerous.
The Qi here was not merely dense.
It was overwhelmingly dense.
It did not feel as though the room had been filled with Qi from an external source.
Instead, the energy seemed to have become an intrinsic part of the entire space.
It flowed through the walls, permeated the floor and ceiling, and existed within every empty space between the objects around them.
Even the air itself seemed saturated with spiritual energy, making the environment feel almost tangible to her senses.
Camilla slowly turned her head toward Stan.
"This place is overflowing with Qi."
Stan nodded calmly.
"Yes."
For several seconds, Camilla simply stared at him.
She had expected some enormous explanation about the origin of the Qi or perhaps an explanation of the room’s formation, but Stan seemed completely unconcerned about the matter.
To him, the tremendous concentration of spiritual energy surrounding them was apparently nothing more than a convenient resource.
Camilla took a cautious step forward and immediately felt the pressure of the Qi against her senses.
Her Royal Blood lineage gave her a powerful physique capable of absorbing vast quantities of energy, but even she understood that this environment demanded caution.

If an ordinary cultivator were to sit down here and begin absorbing Qi without proper preparation, the sheer quantity of energy entering their body could easily overwhelm their meridians and cause severe internal damage.
Depending on their cultivation level, they might even lose control of their energy entirely.
She looked toward Stan again.
"You cultivate here?"
"You ask way too much questions..."
Camilla’s expression became incredulous. ’aa expected of a master Cultivator he can cultivate in a place with this much Chaotic Qi?’
Stan pulled out one of the chairs and sat down as though her reaction was perfectly normal.

While he hasn’t tried it yet he can actually easily cultivate here, the QI her feels chaotic and hard to control for Camilla because it’s Condensed Spatial QI which she has no affinity for, while she can still absorb and utilise it as normal Qi energy, it’ll be agonisingly slower than her normal speed...
If this was normal neutral Qi, or a Qi with an element she has affinity to, this place would’ve felt like a paradise...
Camilla stared at him, then slowly looked around the room once more.
Her mind began putting together the pieces she had previously overlooked.
The room was not designed for ordinary relaxation.
The absence of unnecessary decorations made sense if the purpose was cultivation, while the extraordinary concentration of Qi explained why Stan had bothered creating or maintaining such a space.
It was clearly a private cultivation environment disguised as something far more mundane.
"So this is where you cultivate," Camilla said, her voice becoming more serious.
"One of the places."
Camilla’s eyes narrowed.
"How many places do you have?"
Stan looked at her with an amused expression.
Camilla immediately frowned.
Stan laughed, the sound echoing softly through the quiet room.

chapters.title: Chapter 477: Tea Room (2)
paragraphs: Despite herself, Camilla’s irritation faded slightly. She walked toward the table and eventually pulled out the remaining chair before sitting down opposite him. The moment she settled into the seat, her attention was drawn to the cup placed directly in front of her. Steam still rose gently from its surface, carrying an unfamiliar but surprisingly pleasant aroma.
She reached toward it but paused before her fingers touched the cup.
Her eyes shifted toward Stan.
"This is coffee?"
"Yes."

Camilla studied the dark liquid for another moment, as though trying to determine whether it was some kind of cultivation resource disguised as an ordinary beverage. Eventually, she decided to take the risk and carefully lifted the cup toward her lips.
Stan remained completely relaxed.

When the Void Sovereign had first offered him the beverage, he had deliberately chosen not to drink it. He had no idea what the coffee contained, and given that it came from an inheritance left behind by an existence as powerful as the Void Sovereign, there was no reason to casually consume something whose effects were unknown.
But he wasn’t concerned about Camilla drinking it.
The moment she picked up the cup, Stan’s attention had naturally shifted toward their connection.

As a member of his harem, Camilla’s life was connected to him through the system. If she were about to consume something harmful enough to endanger her life, the connection would immediately reflect that danger to him. He didn’t need to wait for the substance to enter her body, nor did Camilla need to experience its effects first. If the moment she drank it would place her life in danger, Stan would sense that danger before she even took the first sip.
Yet he sensed nothing.
There was no warning from their connection, no indication of danger, and no sign that Camilla’s life would be threatened by the beverage.
That alone was enough for Stan to know that the coffee was safe.
So he simply watched.
Camilla brought the cup to her lips and took a small sip. For several seconds, her expression remained completely blank.
Stan couldn’t help but smile faintly as he waited for her reaction.

Camilla slowly swallowed and glanced down at the cup again. The bitterness was immediately noticeable, but it was accompanied by a rich aroma and a lingering flavor that she had not expected. It was nothing like blood she was accustomed to drinking in the New Terra Realm. It was far simpler, yet there was something strangely satisfying about it.
"This is better than I expected," she admitted.
Stan’s smile widened slightly.
"I knew you’d like it."
Camilla gave him a suspicious glance, clearly noticing the smugness in his voice. Nevertheless, she ignored it and took another sip, this time without nearly as much hesitation.

She leaned back slightly in her chair, allowing her gaze to wander around the room once more. The more she examined her surroundings, the more curious she became. What had initially appeared to be nothing more than a simple room was beginning to feel increasingly mysterious. Now she was starting to understand that its simplicity was precisely what made it unusual.

The enormous concentration of Qi was impossible to ignore, yet the room itself remained remarkably ordinary. There were no extravagant treasures on display, no intimidating formations carved into the walls, and nothing that immediately revealed why such a seemingly insignificant space belonged to a master cultivator.
Camilla’s gaze eventually settled on Stan again.

The more she thought about it, the more certain she became that this place probably meant very little to him. To her, the concentration of Qi alone was astonishing enough to make the room worthy of being treated as a priceless cultivation treasure. Yet Stan had brought her here with the same casual attitude someone might have when showing a friend an ordinary room in their home.
Camilla slowly lowered her cup.
She had already begun to realize that this was probably nothing more than an insignificant corner of Stan’s world.
And judging by the way he had brought her here so casually, she suspected that he had barely shown her anything yet.
This was probably just the tip of the iceberg.
She let out a quiet sigh and shook her head slightly. ’What did I even expect...?’
"This place doesn’t feel like a normal spatial artifact."
Camilla’s voice carried a rare trace of uncertainty as she slowly turned in place, allowing her gaze to travel across the enormous chamber.
She could tell that this was some kind of pocket space connected to Earth, but there was something fundamentally different about the space surrounding them.
It didn’t possess the familiar feeling of a storage artifact, secret realm, or portable dimension.
Those spaces, regardless of how advanced they were, still felt like constructed environments that obeyed recognizable principles.
This chamber was different.
It felt as though the very space around them had been rewritten according to laws that existed far beyond her current understanding.
"It’s not," Stan replied calmly.
He glanced at her for a moment before a thought crossed his mind.
He had heard Camilla mention that information about Earth and their people’s past had been passed down through the vampire lineage for generations.
Perhaps she might know something about the figure behind this chamber.
There was only one way to find out.
"You said information about Earth and your people’s past has been passed down from generation to generation through your vampire lineage."
"Then do you know who the Void Sovereign is?"
The moment she heard that name, Camilla’s hand stopped halfway through its movement.
"The Void Sovereign..."
She repeated the name quietly, her brows knitting together.
She searched through every fragment of knowledge she had inherited from her bloodline, trying to find even the slightest trace of familiarity.
Nothing. She had never heard of such a figure. Not in the records passed down through her lineage.
Not in the ancient stories.
Not even in the fragments of history concerning Earth and the beings who had once walked its lands.

chapters.title: Chapter 478: Detoriation
paragraphs: She had never heard of Void Sovereign before, Stan’s question made her wonder...
‘This Void Sovereign, who was he? And why was Stan suddenly asking her about him?”
A faint uneasiness settled in her heart.
‘Could this be connected to Stan somehow?’
‘Was there something he knew that she didn’t?’
Or was he simply trying to determine whether she possessed information about a figure he had encountered?’
Her heart shook as she thought of something, ‘Or Is Stan The Void Sovereign... Is he asking simply to know if I know his title?’
She couldn’t be certain but one thing, however, was obvious.
If a person existed who could be referred to as the “Void Sovereign,” there had to be a history behind such a title.
And high chance Stan was Void Sovereign, he had to get refrencing himself..
Her heart was shaken, she had already known that Stan was extraordinary. In fact, she had long since stopped trying to measure his potential using ordinary standards.
Yet every time she ‘discovered’ another layer of his secrets, she found herself forced to reconsider everything she thought she knew about him.
The existence of this chamber alone was enough to prove that Stan’s secrets ran far deeper than she had imagined.
Before she could say anything else, a faint hum suddenly echoed through the chamber.
The sound was subtle, almost imperceptible, but the moment it appeared, both of them reacted.
Camilla’s expression changed as she immediately turned toward the source. “What was that?”
Stan did not answer immediately. His eyes had already locked onto the far wall.
At first, nothing seemed unusual. The wall remained completely dark, its surface appearing smooth and featureless. Then, without warning, a faint line of light appeared across it.
A second line emerged.
Then another.

Within moments, hundreds of luminous lines had begun spreading across the wall. They intersected with one another in increasingly complex patterns, forming an enormous lattice of glowing symbols. What had initially looked like random threads gradually revealed itself to be a gigantic formation composed of countless interconnected runes.
Camilla instinctively took a step backward.
“What is that?”
Stan remained silent. His attention was completely focused on the formation.
The lattice continued expanding until it occupied almost the entire wall. At its center, the countless lines suddenly converged, and a massive spherical projection emerged from the formation.
The image slowly rotated.
Camilla’s eyes widened. “That’s...”
“Earth,” Stan said.

The blue planet revolved silently within the projection, surrounded by the endless darkness of space. From this distance, it looked almost peaceful, completely unaware of the immense structure surrounding it.
But Camilla quickly noticed that Earth was not alone.

Seven brilliant nodes appeared around the planet, each one connected to Earth by enormous strands of light. They were positioned at seemingly distant locations, forming a vast network that covered the entire planet.
Yet the seven nodes were not the most frightening part.
Surrounding the entire structure was a colossal formation.
It was ancient.
Enormous.
And, most importantly, dying.

Camilla’s expression gradually hardened as she stared at the projection. Even without understanding the formation’s purpose, she could sense that something was deeply wrong with it. The enormous structure surrounding Earth was riddled with faint distortions, and countless energy pathways were flickering irregularly as though they were struggling to maintain their functions.
“What am I looking at?” she asked quietly.
Stan stepped closer to the projection.
“The formation protecting Earth.”
Camilla frowned. “Protecting it from what?”
“Everything outside.”
His answer was simple, but the implications behind it caused Camilla’s expression to change.
She looked at Earth again.

The seven anchor nodes pulsed weakly, their brilliance fluctuating at different intervals. Some remained relatively stable, while others flickered so badly that they seemed moments away from extinguishing. The formation surrounding them was even worse. It was not physically damaged, but countless cracks had appeared throughout its structure.
They were not ordinary cracks.
They were Dao cracks.

The formation had been constructed from an intricate network of laws and energy pathways, and after countless years of continuous operation, those pathways had begun to deteriorate. Every cycle of energy through the formation placed additional strain on its already weakened structure.
Stan narrowed his eyes.

Since obtaining the Void Sovereign’s inheritance, his understanding of the Dao had increased dramatically. He was still far from comprehending everything contained within the ancient formation, but he could now recognize fragments of the information encoded within its structure.
Decay. Instability. Structural degradation. Projected collapse.
His expression gradually became solemn. “The decay rate increased.”
Camilla immediately looked at him. “What does that mean?”
Stan’s eyes remained fixed on the formation. He watched as several strands of light weakened before recovering, only to flicker again moments later.
For several seconds, he said nothing.
Then another series of ancient symbols appeared across the projection.
His gaze moved rapidly across them, deciphering what he could.
The information caused his expression to change slightly.
“The formation was approaching its limit and it’s getting worse with each passing day...”
Stan raised his hand and pointed toward one of the sections surrounding Earth. “This is worse than I expected.”
The moment his words fell, the projection changed again.
A thin line appeared beside the formation. It represented the remaining stability of the entire structure.
At first, the decline was almost impossible to notice. The line moved downward at an extremely slow rate, suggesting that the formation still possessed an enormous amount of remaining energy.
Then the decline accelerated.
Camilla’s expression became increasingly serious as she watched it.
“How much time does it have left?”
“2-3 months.”

Stan’s voice remained calm, but his eyes had become considerably colder. He continued examining the formation, following the movement of its energy pathways and comparing their current condition against the information left behind by the Void Sovereign.

“The problem isn’t simply that the formation is weakening,” he finally explained. “Its rate of deterioration is increasing. Every damaged section places additional pressure on the remaining structure, and that pressure accelerates the degradation of the other sections.”

chapters.title: Chapter 479: Casual Cultivation...
paragraphs: “The problem isn’t simply that the formation is weakening,” he finally explained. “Its rate of deterioration is increasing. Every damaged section places additional pressure on the remaining structure, and that pressure accelerates the degradation of the other sections.”
Camilla’s brows furrowed. “So it’s a chain reaction?”
“Something similar.”
Stan’s gaze remained fixed on the projection.
“If nothing changes, the formation won’t simply weaken until it stops functioning. Once enough critical pathways fail, the remaining structure will begin collapsing much faster.”
Camilla stared at Earth.
For the first time, she understood why Stan’s expression had become so serious.
“Can you repair it?”
Stan finally looked at her. “Not yet...”
The answer was straightforward.
However, Camilla could hear the meaning behind those two words. He had not said that it was impossible. He had said that he could not do it yet.
She studied him for several seconds before turning her attention back to the formation.
“You intend to repair it?”
“Eventually.”

Stan had already asked the system for a book or some kind of information that could help him understand how to repair the formation. Unfortunately, ever since he had made the request, the system had done nothing but display a loading panel.
Hopefully, it would eventually provide him with what he needed.

Either way, repairing a formation that spanned an entire planet was not going to be easy. His current realm was still far too low compared to that of the Void Sovereign, and the gap between them was difficult to even comprehend.
Still, Stan’s cultivation speed had been astonishingly fast.
He had already reached the peak tier of his current realm and was now standing at the threshold of the next major realm.
“You say that as though repairing a formation spanning an entire planet is an easy thing...”
A faint smile appeared on Stan’s face.
“It isn’t,” he admitted. “But I’ll try.”

He turned away from the projection and walked toward the center of the chamber. “That’s precisely why I need to understand the Void Sovereign’s inheritance first. If I want to repair something created by an existence whose mastery of the Void far exceeds mine, then understanding the foundation upon which this formation was built is the first step.”
Camilla slowly nodded as she looked around the chamber, her gaze lingering on the enormous formation that dominated the center of the room.
The intricate array of ancient runes and spatial markings continued to circulate with a faint, almost imperceptible glow, while the energy within the chamber remained unusually dense.
“So that’s why you brought me here.”
“Partly.”
The simple response caused Camilla’s eyes to narrow slightly. She turned her attention back to Stan, studying his expression as though trying to determine what he was deliberately leaving unsaid.
There was something about the way he had answered that made it clear the formation wasn’t the only reason he had brought her here.
“Partly?” she repeated, a faint note of curiosity entering her voice.
Stan stopped walking and glanced back at her. His expression remained calm, almost indifferent, as though what he was about to say were nothing particularly important.
“I also wanted you and the others to know what is waiting outside.”
Camilla’s expression became slightly more serious.
Stan continued.
“I can delay it but when this formation inevitably detoriates completely and the people of new terra are finally able to return to Earth, make sure they understand one thing.”
His gaze shifted toward the enormous formation.
“There are enemies from outside this world who have already set their sights on Earth.”
A brief silence followed.
“They’re watching us. And sooner or later, they’ll come.”
Camilla’s eyes narrowed. “So you want Earth to prepare for them.”
“Exactly.”
Stan turned fully toward her.

“Earth can’t afford to remain divided when that happens. Once the formation collapses and everyone is able to return, the different factions need to put aside their differences and unite against the enemies beyond Earth.”
His voice remained calm, but there was an unmistakable weight behind his words.
“If they continue fighting among themselves, they’ll only make Earth easier to conquer.”
Camilla remained silent for several seconds, absorbing everything he had said.
Then, slowly, she nodded.
“I’m learning a lot...” she murmured.
Camilla walked toward him and eventually sat down a short distance away. Her crimson eyes remained fixed on him, carrying an unmistakable sense of curiosity.

“You’ve accumulated too many secrets, Stan. Every time I think I’ve understood you, another one appears. You possess a place like this, and now you’re studying the formation protecting an entire planet. I want to see what you actually do when you cultivate here, I’m curious.”
Stan chuckled softly. “So that’s what this is about.”
“Exactly.”
Camilla rested her chin against one hand as she looked at him with an amused expression “I want to see you cultivate in the chaotic Qi .”
Stan looked at her for several seconds before a faint smile appeared on his face.
“Then watch.”
Camilla’s expression immediately became attentive.
Stan slowly closed his eyes.
The atmosphere within the chamber changed almost instantly.

The casual feeling that had surrounded him disappeared, replaced by an overwhelming sense of stillness. His breathing gradually slowed until it became almost imperceptible, while the surrounding space began responding to his presence.
Camilla’s eyes narrowed.
She had expected cultivation to involve meditation, energy circulation, and perhaps some kind of breathing technique.
She had not expected the Void itself to respond.
The darkness surrounding them began to ripple.

Tiny distortions appeared in the air around Stan’s body, each one resembling a miniature fracture in reality. They did not spread violently. Instead, they formed in perfect synchronization with his breathing, appearing whenever he inhaled and disappearing whenever he exhaled.
Camilla’s expression slowly changed.
She had seen powerful cultivators absorb energy before.
This was different. Stan wasn’t simply absorbing the energy surrounding him.
He was drawing upon the fundamental properties of space itself.
The Void Sovereign’s inheritance had begun to reveal its true nature.
The formation control room gradually dimmed as the surrounding lights faded into darkness, leaving the enormous projection suspended above the chamber as the primary source of illumination.
Earth continued its silent rotation at the center of the display, its blue surface illuminated against the darkness of space.

Seven ancient anchor nodes remained positioned around the planet, each one connected to the others through countless lines of intricate formation patterns. Their faint radiance pulsed at irregular intervals, a subtle reminder that the enormous formation protecting Earth was far from stable.
Stan closed his eyes and slowly adjusted his breathing until his thoughts became completely still.

With each deliberate breath, the Void Sovereign Sutra began circulating through his body. At first, there was no visible change. The chamber remained quiet, and the enormous quantity of Qi surrounding him appeared completely unaffected. Then, gradually, something began to shift.
The Qi inside the chamber started moving.

It did not surge toward Stan like a torrent, nor did it gather around him with the overwhelming force of an ordinary cultivation technique. Instead, it flowed naturally, almost peacefully, like an invisible river responding to a gravitational force that existed beyond ordinary perception.
Strands of Qi began drifting toward him from every direction before quietly entering his body through his pores. The process was so smooth that there was almost no disturbance in the surrounding air.

Once inside his body, the Qi followed the pathways of his meridians and gradually converged toward his Dantian. However, instead of simply accumulating there, the Void Sovereign Sutra immediately began refining it. Ordinary Qi was stripped of its impurities and transformed into something purer. That purer energy was compressed again, becoming denser and more concentrated until it gradually took on an almost transparent quality.
The change was subtle, but the difference in quality was enormous.

sentences.text: “The problem isn’t simply that the formation is weakening,” he finally explained.
“Its rate of deterioration is increasing.
Every damaged section places additional pressure on the remaining structure, and that pressure accelerates the degradation of the other sections.”
Camilla’s brows furrowed.
“So it’s a chain reaction?”
“Something similar.”
Stan’s gaze remained fixed on the projection.
“If nothing changes, the formation won’t simply weaken until it stops functioning.
Once enough critical pathways fail, the remaining structure will begin collapsing much faster.”
Camilla stared at Earth.
For the first time, she understood why Stan’s expression had become so serious.
“Can you repair it?”
Stan finally looked at her.
“Not yet...”
The answer was straightforward.
However, Camilla could hear the meaning behind those two words.
He had not said that it was impossible.
He had said that he could not do it yet.
She studied him for several seconds before turning her attention back to the formation.
“You intend to repair it?”
“Eventually.”
Stan had already asked the system for a book or some kind of information that could help him understand how to repair the formation.
Unfortunately, ever since he had made the request, the system had done nothing but display a loading panel.
Hopefully, it would eventually provide him with what he needed.
Either way, repairing a formation that spanned an entire planet was not going to be easy.
His current realm was still far too low compared to that of the Void Sovereign, and the gap between them was difficult to even comprehend.
Still, Stan’s cultivation speed had been astonishingly fast.
He had already reached the peak tier of his current realm and was now standing at the threshold of the next major realm.
“You say that as though repairing a formation spanning an entire planet is an easy thing...”
A faint smile appeared on Stan’s face.
“It isn’t,” he admitted.
“But I’ll try.”
He turned away from the projection and walked toward the center of the chamber.
“That’s precisely why I need to understand the Void Sovereign’s inheritance first.
If I want to repair something created by an existence whose mastery of the Void far exceeds mine, then understanding the foundation upon which this formation was built is the first step.”
Camilla slowly nodded as she looked around the chamber, her gaze lingering on the enormous formation that dominated the center of the room.
The intricate array of ancient runes and spatial markings continued to circulate with a faint, almost imperceptible glow, while the energy within the chamber remained unusually dense.
“So that’s why you brought me here.”
“Partly.”
The simple response caused Camilla’s eyes to narrow slightly.
She turned her attention back to Stan, studying his expression as though trying to determine what he was deliberately leaving unsaid.
There was something about the way he had answered that made it clear the formation wasn’t the only reason he had brought her here.
“Partly?” she repeated, a faint note of curiosity entering her voice.
Stan stopped walking and glanced back at her.
His expression remained calm, almost indifferent, as though what he was about to say were nothing particularly important.
“I also wanted you and the others to know what is waiting outside.”
Camilla’s expression became slightly more serious.
Stan continued.
“I can delay it but when this formation inevitably detoriates completely and the people of new terra are finally able to return to Earth, make sure they understand one thing.”
His gaze shifted toward the enormous formation.
“There are enemies from outside this world who have already set their sights on Earth.”
A brief silence followed.
“They’re watching us.
And sooner or later, they’ll come.”
Camilla’s eyes narrowed.
“So you want Earth to prepare for them.”
“Exactly.”
Stan turned fully toward her.
“Earth can’t afford to remain divided when that happens.
Once the formation collapses and everyone is able to return, the different factions need to put aside their differences and unite against the enemies beyond Earth.”
His voice remained calm, but there was an unmistakable weight behind his words.
“If they continue fighting among themselves, they’ll only make Earth easier to conquer.”
Camilla remained silent for several seconds, absorbing everything he had said.
Then, slowly, she nodded.
“I’m learning a lot...” she murmured.
Camilla walked toward him and eventually sat down a short distance away.
Her crimson eyes remained fixed on him, carrying an unmistakable sense of curiosity.
“You’ve accumulated too many secrets, Stan.
Every time I think I’ve understood you, another one appears.
You possess a place like this, and now you’re studying the formation protecting an entire planet.
I want to see what you actually do when you cultivate here, I’m curious.”
Stan chuckled softly.
“So that’s what this is about.”
“Exactly.”
Camilla rested her chin against one hand as she looked at him with an amused expression “I want to see you cultivate in the chaotic Qi .”
Stan looked at her for several seconds before a faint smile appeared on his face.
“Then watch.”
Camilla’s expression immediately became attentive.
Stan slowly closed his eyes.
The atmosphere within the chamber changed almost instantly.
The casual feeling that had surrounded him disappeared, replaced by an overwhelming sense of stillness.
His breathing gradually slowed until it became almost imperceptible, while the surrounding space began responding to his presence.
Camilla’s eyes narrowed.
She had expected cultivation to involve meditation, energy circulation, and perhaps some kind of breathing technique.
She had not expected the Void itself to respond.
The darkness surrounding them began to ripple.
Tiny distortions appeared in the air around Stan’s body, each one resembling a miniature fracture in reality.
They did not spread violently.
Instead, they formed in perfect synchronization with his breathing, appearing whenever he inhaled and disappearing whenever he exhaled.
Camilla’s expression slowly changed.
She had seen powerful cultivators absorb energy before.
This was different.
Stan wasn’t simply absorbing the energy surrounding him.
He was drawing upon the fundamental properties of space itself.
The Void Sovereign’s inheritance had begun to reveal its true nature.
The formation control room gradually dimmed as the surrounding lights faded into darkness, leaving the enormous projection suspended above the chamber as the primary source of illumination.
Earth continued its silent rotation at the center of the display, its blue surface illuminated against the darkness of space.
Seven ancient anchor nodes remained positioned around the planet, each one connected to the others through countless lines of intricate formation patterns.
Their faint radiance pulsed at irregular intervals, a subtle reminder that the enormous formation protecting Earth was far from stable.
Stan closed his eyes and slowly adjusted his breathing until his thoughts became completely still.
With each deliberate breath, the Void Sovereign Sutra began circulating through his body.
At first, there was no visible change.
The chamber remained quiet, and the enormous quantity of Qi surrounding him appeared completely unaffected.
Then, gradually, something began to shift.
The Qi inside the chamber started moving.
It did not surge toward Stan like a torrent, nor did it gather around him with the overwhelming force of an ordinary cultivation technique.
Instead, it flowed naturally, almost peacefully, like an invisible river responding to a gravitational force that existed beyond ordinary perception.
Strands of Qi began drifting toward him from every direction before quietly entering his body through his pores.
The process was so smooth that there was almost no disturbance in the surrounding air.
Once inside his body, the Qi followed the pathways of his meridians and gradually converged toward his Dantian.
However, instead of simply accumulating there, the Void Sovereign Sutra immediately began refining it.
Ordinary Qi was stripped of its impurities and transformed into something purer.
That purer energy was compressed again, becoming denser and more concentrated until it gradually took on an almost transparent quality.
The change was subtle, but the difference in quality was enormous.

chapters.title: Chapter 480: Authorization Needed
paragraphs: The aura surrounding Stan continued to grow stronger with every passing moment.
Camilla watched in silence. Her crimson eyes gradually widened as she relied on the heightened perception granted by her Royal Blood lineage to observe the changes taking place within his body.
She could clearly see the Qi flowing through his meridians.

At first, the process had seemed straightforward. Stan was simply absorbing the dense energy filling the chamber. But the longer she observed, the more she realized that something far more profound was happening.
His Qi was not merely becoming stronger.
It was becoming purer. Cleaner and more refined.

Almost none of the energy entering his body was wasted. Every trace of Qi was being drawn through his meridians, stripped of impurities, compressed, and transformed into an increasingly profound form of energy.
It was as though Stan was not merely cultivating with Qi.
He was refining the very essence of Qi itself.
Camilla’s lips parted slightly. “He’s refining the Qi itself...”

Stan gave no response. He had already entered a deep state of meditation, his awareness gradually withdrawing from the physical sensations of his body as the Void Sovereign Sutra continued circulating.
His consciousness sank deeper. The chamber disappeared.
The sound of Camilla’s movements vanished.
Even the sensation of his own body gradually faded until only his consciousness remained within an endless expanse of darkness.
Then the Void Sovereign Sutra unfolded before him.
It no longer appeared as a simple cultivation technique.
It resembled an ancient scripture written across the darkness of existence itself.
One Dao character after another emerged before his consciousness, each carrying a meaning so profound that ordinary language could barely describe it.
Space.
Void.
Distance.
Existence.
Nonexistence.
The boundary between them.
Stan’s comprehension slowly deepened as he contemplated each concept.

Previously, he had understood space primarily through practical application. He could manipulate spatial laws, distort distances, open passages, and move between locations, but his understanding had largely remained limited to what he could perceive and control.
Now, that perception was beginning to change.
Space no longer appeared empty.
Instead, it seemed layered.

Countless invisible planes appeared to overlap one another, each existing within a structure far more intricate than he had previously imagined. He could sense the distance between objects, but as his comprehension continued to deepen, he began perceiving something even more fundamental.
The distance between spaces.
The invisible boundaries separating one location from another.
The countless laws that determined why two points could be considered distant in the first place.
And eventually, a strange realization surfaced within his consciousness.
If distance was governed by laws...
Then perhaps distance itself could be erased.
The thought caused his consciousness to tremble.
His comprehension of the Dao of Space began rising.
There was no explosive phenomenon.
No surge of power.
No dramatic breakthrough.
It simply happened gradually, almost imperceptibly.
Every cycle of the Void Sovereign Sutra brought him a little closer to understanding the true nature of space.
Outside his meditation, Camilla continued watching him.
Minutes passed.
Then an hour.
Then several more.

Yet time seemed strangely difficult to perceive inside the chamber. The environment remained so peaceful that Camilla eventually realized she had spent far longer observing Stan than she had intended.
Even the coffee beside her remained warm.
She glanced at the cup before looking toward Stan again.
He had not moved even once.
Camilla finally sighed and rose from her chair.
“Ridiculous. Who cultivates like this?”
She decided there was little point in continuing to watch someone sit motionless for hours.
Instead, she began exploring the chamber.
The further she walked, the more unusual the room became.
At first glance, the walls appeared completely smooth. But once she paid closer attention, she began noticing faint traces of ancient inscriptions embedded within their surface.
Dao markings.
Some were so subtle that they were almost impossible to notice. Others were partially concealed beneath layers of spatial laws.
Camilla examined several of them carefully.
Even with her bloodline-enhanced perception, she could not decipher most of what she saw.
The inscriptions were simply too profound.
They were not ordinary characters carved into stone.
Each marking seemed to contain a fragment of law.
A concept.
A principle.
Something that could perhaps take an ordinary cultivator decades, or even centuries, to comprehend.
Camilla’s expression gradually became more serious.
Whoever had created this place had possessed an understanding of the Dao far beyond anything she had encountered before.
Eventually, she stopped before one particular inscription.
It was partially concealed within the wall, surrounded by several intricate spatial patterns.
Camilla leaned closer.
“What exactly are you hiding?”
She raised her hand and slowly brought her fingers toward the inscription.
The moment her fingertips approached it, the ancient markings suddenly illuminated.
Camilla immediately pulled her hand back.
“What was that?”
A faint ripple spread across the wall.
Then a small projection appeared above the inscription, formed from pale energy.
A single line of text emerged.
[Authorization insufficient.]
Camilla stared at it. For several seconds, she remained completely silent.
Then her gaze slowly shifted toward Stan.
He was still sitting in meditation, completely unaware of what had just happened.
Camilla looked back at the inscription. Understanding gradually dawned on her.
“Of course...” She folded her arms across her chest. “Even the walls recognize him.”
A helpless expression appeared on her face.
Clearly, this place possessed some kind of authority system, and whatever permission Stan possessed was far beyond hers.
Rather than waste time attempting to force her way through an ancient formation she barely understood, Camilla continued exploring.
A few moments later, something else caught her attention.
A transparent panel was embedded within another section of the wall.
Its surface was so perfectly integrated into the surrounding structure that she had initially mistaken it for another layer of the chamber’s architecture.
Curiosity got the better of her. Camilla reached out and touched it.
The panel flickered and a faint wave of energy spread across its surface.
Then several words appeared.
[Void Sovereign Inheritance.]
Camilla froze. Her eyes widened. For several seconds, she simply stared at the words.
“The Void Sovereign...” She whispered the name.
Her gaze slowly moved toward Stan..A strange thought surfaced in her mind.
He has to be the Void Sovereign. The possibility suddenly seemed far more plausible than it had moments earlier.
She began mentally piecing together everything she had witnessed since arriving.
Stan possessed an extraordinary understanding of spatial laws.
He could traverse enormous distances almost instantaneously.
He could enter this strange chamber without causing any disturbance.
The space itself seemed to respond to his presence.
Even the walls recognized his authority while rejecting hers.
And now, right before her eyes, she had discovered a system identifying this place as the Void Sovereign’s inheritance.
The pieces seemed to fit together too perfectly.
If Stan truly was the Void Sovereign, then his strange behavior suddenly became much easier to understand.
His mastery of spatial laws. His mysterious abilities.
The unfathomable depths hidden beneath his seemingly casual personality.
Even his confidence whenever he manipulated space.
Camilla’s thoughts accelerated.
If he’s void Sovereign and this is his inheritance theb his strength was even more unfathomable that she thiught..
And people of such level loves to leave behind a legacy. A cultivation ground. Perhaps even several inheritances scattered throughout the world, waiting for suitable successors to discover them.
Camilla’s gaze returned to the panel. But another question immediately followed.
‘hen why did he ask me if I knew the Void Sovereign?’
Was he testing whether her vampire lineage contained information about the Void Sovereign?
Was he trying to determine whether her ancestors had encountered him?
Camilla frowned slightly. There were too many unanswered questions.

chapters.title: Chapter 481: Formation
paragraphs: She had originally believed Stan had brought her here simply because he wanted to show her a strange place.
Now she realized that this chamber was connected to something far older and far more powerful than she had imagined.
The enormous concentration of Qi suddenly made sense.
It could have been deliberately accumulated here to nurture the inheritor.
The strange spatial laws surrounding the chamber could be remnants of the Void Sovereign’s understanding.
Even the ancient inscriptions might contain fragments of his comprehension.
And then there was the most obvious detail.
Stan.
He could move through this place effortlessly.
The chamber recognized him.
The space responded to him.
Yet he had never once behaved as though any of this were particularly remarkable.
Camilla narrowed her eyes. ‘Just who exactly are you, Stan?’
Her curiosity deepened.
She had already known that Stan was extraordinary. She had simply never realized how deep that extraordinariness might go.
If this truly was the Void Sovereign’s inheritance, then whatever secrets Stan was hiding were probably far greater than she had imagined.
Camilla glanced at him once more.
He remained completely immersed in cultivation, his breathing slow and steady as faint spatial distortions continued to ripple around his body.
She folded her arms and quietly watched him.
For the first time, she found herself genuinely eager to discover what would happen when he eventually opened his eyes.
Camilla couldn’t help but find the contrast almost ridiculous.

She was standing inside an inheritance belonging to an existence whose very title had made her instinctively cautious, yet Stan sat beside her as though they were simply spending an ordinary afternoon together.
If he really was the Void Sovereign, then just how deep did his secrets go?
And if this chamber was merely one of the inheritances he had prepared for a future successor, how many other places like this existed?
Camilla’s gaze lingered on the words displayed across the screen.
For the first time, she seriously wondered whether she had underestimated Stan by far more than she had ever realized.
Her attention eventually returned to him.
Stan remained perfectly still, his breathing slow and controlled. Yet a faint distortion had begun to form around his body.
It was subtle enough that an ordinary person would never have noticed it, but Camilla’s heightened perception allowed her to clearly see the space surrounding him gently warping.
There was no violent surge of energy.
No uncontrolled eruption.
Reality itself simply seemed to be responding to his presence.
Camilla’s pupils narrowed.
“He’s affecting space without even consciously controlling it...”
She instinctively took a step backward.
A faint chill ran down her spine.

The phenomenon was unsettling precisely because Stan wasn’t deliberately doing anything. His comprehension of space had apparently reached a point where his very existence was beginning to influence his surroundings.
Yet despite the danger such a phenomenon represented, Camilla couldn’t deny that she found it fascinating.
She continued watching for a while longer.
Then Stan’s aura changed.

The distortion around his body gradually faded, and his breathing slowed until it was almost imperceptible. The turbulent flow of Qi within the chamber settled with him, and an unnatural silence descended over the entire space.
Even the enormous projection of Earth seemed to respond.
Its rotation slowed.
The seven anchor nodes ceased their irregular flickering.
For a brief moment, it felt as though the entire chamber had fallen into a state of absolute stillness.
Then Stan opened his eyes.
Camilla froze.
For the briefest instant, she felt as though she wasn’t looking into human eyes at all.

An endless void seemed to be reflected within them, an immeasurable expanse where distance itself had ceased to have meaning. There was no beginning or end to that darkness, only an overwhelming depth that made her instinctively hold her breath.
Then it disappeared.
Stan blinked once.
His expression returned to normal, as though nothing unusual had happened.
“How long?”
Camilla stared at him for another moment before answering.
“Several hours.”
Stan looked genuinely surprised.
“That long?”
Camilla gave him an incredulous look.
“You didn’t notice?”
“No.”
She sighed and shook her head.
“Of course you didn’t.”
Stan ignored the remark and turned his attention toward the enormous formation surrounding Earth.
Something had changed during his meditation.
The formation was still impossibly complex, but the ancient Dao inscriptions that had once appeared almost incomprehensible to him were no longer completely beyond his perception.
His cultivation had deepened his understanding of the Dao of Space, while the information recently provided by the system had also given him a basic foundation in formation theory.
Together, the two improvements allowed him to see the formation from an entirely different perspective.
He still couldn’t decipher everything.
In fact, he suspected that what he understood amounted to only a small fraction of the formation’s true structure.
Its age alone made it extraordinarily difficult to analyze, while the countless energy pathways and ancient inscriptions intertwined in patterns far beyond his current realm.
But he no longer saw an incomprehensible mass of information.
Patterns were beginning to emerge.
He could distinguish several major energy pathways, identify repeating structures, and recognize some of the fundamental principles governing the formation’s operation.
Most importantly, he could now see how its different sections depended on one another.
Stan’s eyes narrowed.
“The formation has seven primary anchors.”
Camilla, who had been standing a short distance away, immediately approached.
She raised her head and followed his gaze toward the enormous projection.
“Yes.”
Her eyes moved between the seven brilliant nodes.
“Each one stabilizes a different section.”
Stan nodded.
That was precisely what he had discovered.

The seven anchors were far more than simple sources of energy. They formed the structural foundation of the entire formation, distributing power throughout its countless pathways while keeping the enormous network stable.
If one anchor suffered severe damage, the surrounding sections would be forced to compensate.
That additional burden would then be transferred throughout the formation, placing greater strain on the remaining anchors.
It explained the accelerating deterioration he had observed earlier.
Camilla studied the projection for another moment before turning toward him.
Her expression became serious.
“Can they be repaired?”
Stan didn’t answer immediately.

His eyes moved from one anchor to another, carefully examining the flow of energy around each node. He compared their current condition, searched for damaged pathways, and traced the connections linking them to the rest of the formation.
His understanding had improved considerably.
But understanding the structure was one thing.
Repairing it was another.
Even identifying a damaged component didn’t mean he possessed the knowledge or power required to restore it without destabilizing everything connected to it.
After several seconds, Stan finally shook his head.
“Not immediately.”

Camilla froze.
For the briefest instant, she felt as though she wasn’t looking into human eyes at all.
An endless void seemed to be reflected within them, an immeasurable expanse where distance itself had ceased to have meaning.
There was no beginning or end to that darkness, only an overwhelming depth that made her instinctively hold her breath.
Then it disappeared.
Stan blinked once.
His expression returned to normal, as though nothing unusual had happened.
“How long?”
Camilla stared at him for another moment before answering.
“Several hours.”
Stan looked genuinely surprised.
“That long?”
Camilla gave him an incredulous look.
“You didn’t notice?”
“No.”
She sighed and shook her head.
“Of course you didn’t.”
Stan ignored the remark and turned his attention toward the enormous formation surrounding Earth.
Something had changed during his meditation.
The formation was still impossibly complex, but the ancient Dao inscriptions that had once appeared almost incomprehensible to him were no longer completely beyond his perception.
His cultivation had deepened his understanding of the Dao of Space, while the information recently provided by the system had also given him a basic foundation in formation theory.
Together, the two improvements allowed him to see the formation from an entirely different perspective.
He still couldn’t decipher everything.
In fact, he suspected that what he understood amounted to only a small fraction of the formation’s true structure.
Its age alone made it extraordinarily difficult to analyze, while the countless energy pathways and ancient inscriptions intertwined in patterns far beyond his current realm.
But he no longer saw an incomprehensible mass of information.
Patterns were beginning to emerge.
He could distinguish several major energy pathways, identify repeating structures, and recognize some of the fundamental principles governing the formation’s operation.
Most importantly, he could now see how its different sections depended on one another.
Stan’s eyes narrowed.
“The formation has seven primary anchors.”
Camilla, who had been standing a short distance away, immediately approached.
She raised her head and followed his gaze toward the enormous projection.
“Yes.”
Her eyes moved between the seven brilliant nodes.
“Each one stabilizes a different section.”
Stan nodded.
That was precisely what he had discovered.
The seven anchors were far more than simple sources of energy.
They formed the structural foundation of the entire formation, distributing power throughout its countless pathways while keeping the enormous network stable.
If one anchor suffered severe damage, the surrounding sections would be forced to compensate.
That additional burden would then be transferred throughout the formation, placing greater strain on the remaining anchors.
It explained the accelerating deterioration he had observed earlier.
Camilla studied the projection for another moment before turning toward him.
Her expression became serious.
“Can they be repaired?”
Stan didn’t answer immediately.
His eyes moved from one anchor to another, carefully examining the flow of energy around each node.
He compared their current condition, searched for damaged pathways, and traced the connections linking them to the rest of the formation.
His understanding had improved considerably.
But understanding the structure was one thing.
Repairing it was another.
Even identifying a damaged component didn’t mean he possessed the knowledge or power required to restore it without destabilizing everything connected to it.
After several seconds, Stan finally shook his head.
“Not immediately.”

chapters.title: Chapter 482: Damien
paragraphs: "Can the damaged anchors be repaired?"
Stan shook his head. "Not immediately."
He could identify the damaged areas, and he could even determine some of the reasons behind their instability, but that did not mean he possessed the ability to repair them...
The formation was protecting an entire planet, and even the smallest mistake could potentially produce consequences that neither of them could predict.

Stan’s gaze eventually settled upon the seventh anchor node. Unlike the others, its light flickered violently, and the energy circulating through it was noticeably less stable. Every few moments, the flow of energy around the node would fluctuate before returning to its previous pattern, creating subtle distortions throughout the surrounding section of the formation.
"That one is the weakest," Stan said, pointing toward the seventh anchor.
Camilla immediately followed his gaze. She studied the unstable node for several seconds before asking, "What happens if it fails?"

Stan did not answer immediately. Instead, he continued examining the formation, tracing the energy pathways connected to the seventh anchor and observing how they interacted with the other six nodes. The longer he looked, the heavier his expression became. The consequences were not difficult to understand once the structure was viewed as a whole, but that did not make them any less serious.
"The entire formation becomes unstable."

Camilla’s expression changed immediately. She had already understood that the formation was important, but hearing Stan state the consequence so plainly made the situation considerably more serious. Her eyes returned to the enormous projection, and she watched as the seventh anchor continued flickering within the vast network of energy.
"And Earth?" she asked.

Stan slowly shifted his attention toward the blue planet suspended within the center of the formation. From this perspective, Earth appeared almost impossibly small compared to the enormous structure surrounding it. Yet despite its apparent insignificance, the entire formation seemed to revolve around protecting that distant world.
"Earth is protected by the formation.
Stan paused as his gaze remained fixed upon the planet. There was no need to explain further for Camilla to understand what that meant, but he eventually continued in a quieter voice.
"If the formation collapses completely..."
He stopped there.

The unfinished sentence hung in the air for several seconds, but Stan did not need to complete it. The implication was obvious. If the formation was the barrier protecting Earth, then its complete collapse would leave the planet exposed to whatever forces the ancient formation had been designed to keep away.
Camilla understood immediately.

She slowly turned her attention back toward Earth, and for the first time since entering the chamber, she no longer viewed the planet simply as a strange modern world inhabited by ordinary humans and filled with unfamiliar technology.

The blue planet now looked entirely different in her eyes. It was a world that had unknowingly existed beneath the protection of an ancient structure for countless years, completely unaware of how fragile that protection had become.

The realization caused Camilla’s expression to become unusually solemn. The world she had once regarded as little more than a strange place filled with humans and modern technology was, in reality, standing precariously above an abyss. Between Earth and whatever dangers existed beyond its boundaries stood an ancient formation that had already endured an unknown number of years and had now begun to deteriorate.
She remained silent for a while before slowly turning toward Stan.
"You really intend to save this place."

There was no accusation in her voice. Instead, there was genuine curiosity, perhaps even a faint trace of admiration. he was a master Cultivator but was still concerned about a world that had never asked him to protect it.
A faint smile appeared on Stan’s face.
"I live here."

His answer was simple, almost casual, but Camilla understood the meaning behind it. Whatever other reasons Stan might have had, this was ultimately the place he had chosen to live. As far as he was concerned, protecting Earth also meant protecting the home he had built for himself.
Camilla stared at him for several seconds before the solemnity in her expression gradually faded. A small smile appeared on her lips as she gave a slight nod.
"Fair enough."

The tension that had settled over the room gradually eased. The enormous formation continued hovering before them, its countless energy pathways moving in an endless cycle while the seven primary anchors maintained their positions around Earth. Although the situation remained serious, neither of them continued discussing the possible consequences of the formation’s eventual collapse.

Camilla reached down and picked up the cup of coffee she had brought earlier. She took another slow sip, allowing the warmth of the drink to settle her thoughts as she continued looking around the chamber.
As a Vampire, despite her love for blood making most other things tasteless, she was somehow able to taste and love this tea...
The ancient inscriptions covering the walls, the immense amount of Qi permeating the air, and the countless mysteries hidden within the inheritance were all things she had never encountered before.
Meanwhile, far from Stan and Camill a was Blackridge Correctional Facility a prison...

Located far from Inksea, the massive prison complex was surrounded by several layers of reinforced concrete walls, steel fencing, surveillance towers, and security checkpoints designed to ensure that no inmate could simply walk out. It housed criminals who had committed offenses serious enough to warrant years, and in some cases decades, behind bars. Once someone passed through its gates, the outside world became little more than a distant memory.

The facility operated under a strict and unforgiving system. Cameras monitored nearly every corridor, common area, and cell block, while armed guards patrolled the prison grounds around the clock. Heavy steel doors separated one section from another, opening only when authorized personnel permitted them to do so. Behind those doors lived hundreds of men who had long since learned that kindness was not something they could afford to give freely. In Blackridge, weakness attracted attention, and attention could quickly become a problem.
Among those inmates was a man who, less than three weeks ago, had lived a life that seemed completely disconnected from a place like this.
Damien.

chapters.title: Chapter 483: Prison
paragraphs: In the Prison, Among those inmates was a man who, less than three weeks ago, had lived a life that seemed completely disconnected from a place like this.
Damien.

The same Damien who had once believed that wealth could place him above consequences. The same man who had become obsessed with Sophie Youngs after watching her streams repeatedly, eventually becoming so fixated on her that he had gone as far as impersonating Stan’s alias in an attempt to get close to her and win her over.
It was also the same Damien who had been arrested and imprisoned after attempting to rape Zoey, Sophie’s friend and Zack’s girlfriend, only for Stan to arrive in time and save her.

Damien had been born into wealth and had grown up surrounded by luxury, influence, and people who were willing to bend over backward simply because of his family name. He had never needed to worry about the consequences of his actions because there had always been someone willing to clean up his messes. Money had opened doors for him, influence had protected him, and his family’s reputation had ensured that most people thought twice before crossing him.

His obsession with Sophie, however, had eventually twisted into something much darker. After she rejected and ignored his advances, Damien had developed a deep resentment toward female streamers in general. In his distorted mind, Sophie’s rejection had become an insult he could not accept, and he eventually began targeting other female streamers, including Zoey, as though they were somehow responsible for what Sophie had done to him.

Outside the prison walls, Damien’s money could buy almost anything. Business owners had welcomed him. Powerful people had answered his calls. Those who worked for his family knew better than to question him unnecessarily. Even women who wanted nothing to do with him had learned that rejecting him could come with consequences.
None of that mattered inside Blackridge.

Here, there were no luxury cars waiting outside the gates, no private security detail following him around, no servants attending to his needs, and no family connections capable of making the inmates respect him. His surname meant nothing to the men around him. His wealth could not purchase freedom, and his influence could not intimidate prisoners who had already spent years living among violence.
Inside these walls, Damien was simply another inmate.
And that was something he had yet to accept.
"Get up."
Damien’s head snapped upward at the command.

A large man stood directly in front of him. He was easily over six feet tall, with a thick neck, broad shoulders, and a heavily built frame that made Damien look almost insignificant by comparison. Several faded scars crossed his arms, while another thin scar ran along the side of his jaw. Two other inmates stood several steps behind him, positioned in a way that effectively blocked Damien’s path.
Damien’s jaw tightened as he looked at them.
"Move."

The large inmate stared at him for several seconds before letting out a low laugh. There was nothing friendly about it. The sound carried nothing but contempt, as though Damien had just said something genuinely amusing.
"You still haven’t learned, have you?"
Damien slowly pushed himself to his feet. Despite the circumstances, his expression remained arrogant.
"I said move."
The man’s amusement disappeared.

He stepped closer until his massive frame towered over Damien, then suddenly reached out and grabbed him by the collar. Damien’s expression changed immediately as the fabric tightened against his neck.
The inmate pulled him forward until their faces were only inches apart.
"Listen carefully, rich boy. I don’t give a damn who you were outside."
Damien narrowed his eyes.
"You think that name of yours means something in here?"
Before Damien could answer, the man shoved him backward.
Damien stumbled several steps before catching himself.

Several inmates nearby turned their attention toward the confrontation. Some watched openly, clearly entertained by what was happening, while others continued eating as though nothing unusual had occurred. Fights were not exactly uncommon inside Blackridge. Most prisoners had seen enough of them that another beating barely qualified as an event.
The large inmate slowly cracked his knuckles.
"Out there, maybe you had people jumping whenever you snapped your fingers. Maybe you had servants, bodyguards, and people who were afraid of what your family could do to them."
He gestured casually toward the prison walls.
"But in here, none of that matters."
A cruel smile appeared on his face.
"You’re nobody."
Damien’s hands slowly curled into fists.
"You’d better watch your mouth."
The man’s smile vanished.
"Wrong answer."
His fist slammed into Damien’s stomach before Damien could react.

The impact drove the air violently from his lungs. Damien’s body folded forward, and he staggered backward while desperately trying to breathe. Before he could recover, another punch struck the side of his face.
His vision flashed white.
He stumbled sideways and crashed hard against the concrete wall.
Laughter immediately erupted from several nearby inmates.
"Look at him."
"Rich boy doesn’t look so rich anymore."
"Maybe somebody should teach him where he stands."

Damien wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth and glared at them. His breathing had become ragged, but rather than lowering his head or showing submission, he continued staring at the men with the same defiance that had protected his ego outside these walls.
That only made things worse.

The large inmate grabbed him by the front of his prison uniform and slammed him against the wall again before throwing another punch. Damien’s head snapped to the side from the impact, and his legs nearly gave out beneath him.
"You still don’t understand, do you?"
Another punch struck his ribs.
Damien groaned and stumbled forward.
The beating continued.

Every time he attempted to regain his footing, one of the three inmates struck him again. A kick sent him sprawling across the cold concrete floor, and before he could push himself up, someone stepped on his back and forced him down.
"You’re going to learn."
A kick struck his side.
"You’re in prison now."
Another blow landed against his ribs.
"We’re the ones who make the rules."
