chapters.title: Chapter 484: Birth Of Resentment...
paragraphs: “You’re in prison now.”
Another blow landed against his ribs.
“We’re the ones who make the rules.”

Damien coughed violently as another wave of pain spread through his battered body. His fingers trembled against the cold concrete as he struggled to push himself upright, but before he could gather enough strength, a heavy kick struck his side and sent him rolling helplessly onto his back.

The impact drove the remaining air from his lungs, leaving him gasping as agony radiated through his ribs. For several seconds, he could do nothing except lie there and struggle to breathe while the three inmates stood over him with expressions that held neither sympathy nor hesitation.

The largest of the three eventually crouched beside him. His thick fingers seized Damien by the hair and roughly lifted his head from the floor, forcing his battered face upward. Damien’s swollen eye barely remained open, and the blurred figure before him seemed to sway in his vision. The inmate stared directly into his eyes, his expression carrying the cold certainty of someone who had delivered the same lesson to countless newcomers.
“Remember this. You don’t have money here.”

His palm suddenly cracked against Damien’s face. The slap echoed through the corridor, snapping Damien’s head to the side and sending another burst of pain through his already swollen cheek. Before he could recover, the inmate continued.
“You don’t have influence here.”
Another slap followed, harder than the first. Damien’s head jerked in the opposite direction, and the metallic taste of blood immediately filled his mouth.
“And nobody gives a damn about your family.”
The inmate’s expression hardened as he stared into Damien’s eyes, making certain that every word sank in. “In this place, we’re the bosses.”

He finally released Damien’s hair, allowing his head to fall heavily against the concrete. The back of Damien’s skull struck the floor with a dull impact, leaving his vision spinning once again. The inmate rose to his feet and looked down at him with open contempt.
“So you either learn to bow your head, or somebody will keep putting you on this floor until you do.”

With that, the three men turned around and walked away. Their footsteps gradually faded down the corridor, leaving behind only the faint sounds of prison life resuming around them. The inmates who had gathered to watch the beating slowly returned to whatever they had been doing. Some continued their conversations, others went back to their bunks, and a few merely glanced at Damien before losing interest. The brief entertainment was over, and with it went whatever small amount of attention he had received.
Nobody approached him. Nobody offered him a hand. Nobody asked whether he was still conscious or whether he needed help.
Nobody cared.
For several long seconds, Damien remained motionless on the floor. His entire body throbbed with pain, and every breath sent a sharp ache through his ribs.

His cheek had already begun to swell beneath the repeated blows, while blood continued to trickle slowly from his split lip and stain the concrete beneath his face. His body was covered in injuries, but somehow, the physical pain seemed insignificant compared with the humiliation burning inside his mind.
He had never imagined that he could be treated this way.

Damien had grown up surrounded by wealth, influence, and people who were willing to bend over backward to accommodate him. Even when he had behaved arrogantly, there had always been someone willing to tolerate it because of his family name.
His mistakes could be covered with money, his problems could be solved through connections, and his displeasure had always been treated as something worth addressing.
Blackridge had stripped all of that away in a matter of days.

Here, his surname meant nothing. His money meant nothing. The people he once considered beneath him had no reason to fear him, and the people who had once rushed to his side were nowhere to be found. For the first time in his life, Damien had been forced to confront a world in which he possessed no special privileges.
He should have been furious at the men who had beaten him.
He should have hated them for what they had done.
Yet, as he lay there staring blankly at the concrete, his thoughts slowly drifted somewhere else.
Sophie.

The image of her face surfaced in his mind with painful clarity. He remembered the way she had looked at him, the calm indifference in her eyes, and the complete lack of hesitation when she rejected him. She had not cared about his wealth or his family. She had not been impressed by the things that had always made other people treat him differently. To Sophie, Damien had simply been another man whose feelings she did not share.
That memory hurt more than he wanted to admit.
His fingers slowly curled against the concrete.
Then another face appeared in his mind.
‘Stan. That bastard.’
The man who had interfered. The man who had humiliated him.
The man who had somehow appeared in Sophie’s life and stood between Damien and what he believed should have been his.
Damien’s jaw tightened despite the pain.

The memories began overlapping in his mind. Sophie’s rejection. Stan’s interference. The humiliation he had suffered. His arrest. His imprisonment. The beating he had just endured. Every unpleasant event seemed to connect itself to the two people he had already come to resent.
In the distorted logic of his mind, the responsibility for everything that had happened to him had already been transferred onto them.
It was because of them.

If Sophie had simply accepted him, none of this would have happened. If Stan had never appeared in his life, Damien would never have been humiliated. If neither of them had stood in his way, he would never have ended up inside Blackridge, lying helplessly on a filthy concrete floor while complete strangers beat him as though he were nothing more than a worthless animal.

The possibility that his own decisions had played a major role in his downfall never seriously entered his thoughts. His pride refused to accept it. Rather than examine his own actions, Damien’s mind searched for someone else to blame, someone who could carry the weight of his anger and humiliation.
It found Sophie and it found Stan.

Damien’s head jerked in the opposite direction, and the metallic taste of blood immediately filled his mouth.
“And nobody gives a damn about your family.”
The inmate’s expression hardened as he stared into Damien’s eyes, making certain that every word sank in.
“In this place, we’re the bosses.”
He finally released Damien’s hair, allowing his head to fall heavily against the concrete.
The back of Damien’s skull struck the floor with a dull impact, leaving his vision spinning once again.
The inmate rose to his feet and looked down at him with open contempt.
“So you either learn to bow your head, or somebody will keep putting you on this floor until you do.”
With that, the three men turned around and walked away.
Their footsteps gradually faded down the corridor, leaving behind only the faint sounds of prison life resuming around them.
The inmates who had gathered to watch the beating slowly returned to whatever they had been doing.
Some continued their conversations, others went back to their bunks, and a few merely glanced at Damien before losing interest.
The brief entertainment was over, and with it went whatever small amount of attention he had received.
Nobody approached him.
Nobody offered him a hand.
Nobody asked whether he was still conscious or whether he needed help.
Nobody cared.
For several long seconds, Damien remained motionless on the floor.
His entire body throbbed with pain, and every breath sent a sharp ache through his ribs.
His cheek had already begun to swell beneath the repeated blows, while blood continued to trickle slowly from his split lip and stain the concrete beneath his face.
His body was covered in injuries, but somehow, the physical pain seemed insignificant compared with the humiliation burning inside his mind.
He had never imagined that he could be treated this way.
Damien had grown up surrounded by wealth, influence, and people who were willing to bend over backward to accommodate him.
Even when he had behaved arrogantly, there had always been someone willing to tolerate it because of his family name.
His mistakes could be covered with money, his problems could be solved through connections, and his displeasure had always been treated as something worth addressing.
Blackridge had stripped all of that away in a matter of days.
Here, his surname meant nothing.
His money meant nothing.
The people he once considered beneath him had no reason to fear him, and the people who had once rushed to his side were nowhere to be found.
For the first time in his life, Damien had been forced to confront a world in which he possessed no special privileges.
He should have been furious at the men who had beaten him.
He should have hated them for what they had done.
Yet, as he lay there staring blankly at the concrete, his thoughts slowly drifted somewhere else.
Sophie.
The image of her face surfaced in his mind with painful clarity.
He remembered the way she had looked at him, the calm indifference in her eyes, and the complete lack of hesitation when she rejected him.
She had not cared about his wealth or his family.
She had not been impressed by the things that had always made other people treat him differently.
To Sophie, Damien had simply been another man whose feelings she did not share.
That memory hurt more than he wanted to admit.
His fingers slowly curled against the concrete.
Then another face appeared in his mind.
‘Stan.
That bastard.’
The man who had interfered.
The man who had humiliated him.
The man who had somehow appeared in Sophie’s life and stood between Damien and what he believed should have been his.
Damien’s jaw tightened despite the pain.
The memories began overlapping in his mind.
Sophie’s rejection.
Stan’s interference.
The humiliation he had suffered.
His arrest.
His imprisonment.
The beating he had just endured.
Every unpleasant event seemed to connect itself to the two people he had already come to resent.
In the distorted logic of his mind, the responsibility for everything that had happened to him had already been transferred onto them.
It was because of them.
If Sophie had simply accepted him, none of this would have happened.
If Stan had never appeared in his life, Damien would never have been humiliated.

If neither of them had stood in his way, he would never have ended up inside Blackridge, lying helplessly on a filthy concrete floor while complete strangers beat him as though he were nothing more than a worthless animal.
The possibility that his own decisions had played a major role in his downfall never seriously entered his thoughts.
His pride refused to accept it.
Rather than examine his own actions, Damien’s mind searched for someone else to blame, someone who could carry the weight of his anger and humiliation.
It found Sophie and it found Stan.

chapters.title: Chapter 485: A Power Born From Hatred...
paragraphs: Damien anger rose to unimaginable hieght... His fingers dug into the rough concrete as hatred slowly spread through his mind. He remembered every moment he considered humiliating, every rejection that had wounded his pride, every time he had felt powerless, and every occasion when he believed someone had treated him as though he were insignificant.
Those memories had always existed separately, buried beneath his arrogance and self-confidence, but now they were being dragged to the surface by the pain he was experiencing.
“I’ll kill you...”
The words escaped his mouth in a weak whisper. Nobody nearby heard him.
Damien swallowed painfully and continued staring at the floor. His breathing grew heavier as the anger inside him intensified. “I’ll make you pay.”

He was no longer thinking about the inmates who had beaten him. Their faces had already faded into the background of his thoughts. His hatred had found a different target, and every painful memory seemed to feed it.
‘Sophie. Stan.’

He imagined them suffering. He imagined them experiencing the same humiliation that had been forced upon him. He imagined taking everything from them and watching the confidence disappear from their faces. The more he thought about it, the stronger the desire became.
Yet something strange began happening within him.

At first, Damien did not notice the change. He was too consumed by his resentment to realize that the hatred filling his mind was gradually becoming something more intense than ordinary anger. It no longer felt like a temporary emotional response to humiliation. It had begun to sink deeper, reaching into something fundamental within his consciousness.

Every rejection he had suffered, every humiliation he had endured, every grievance he had carried, and every person he believed had wronged him seemed to gather together inside the depths of his mind. The emotions began overlapping until they became difficult to distinguish from one another. Anger merged with resentment. Resentment became hatred. Hatred became an overwhelming desire to retaliate against those he believed responsible for his suffering.
And eventually, all of those emotions converged upon a single concept.
‘Revenge.’ Damien’s consciousness suddenly trembled.

For a brief moment, the prison corridor seemed to disappear from his awareness. The cold concrete beneath his body, the distant conversations of the inmates, the footsteps moving through the corridor, and even the throbbing pain in his ribs gradually became distant and indistinct. It was as though his consciousness had slipped beneath the surface of reality and entered a place where none of those things mattered.
There was only darkness. And within that darkness, there was only one desire.
He wanted them to suffer.

The thought became clearer as it repeated itself within his mind. He wanted Sophie and Stan to experience the same humiliation and helplessness that had consumed him. He wanted them to understand what it felt like to be powerless, to have everything they valued stripped away, and to realize that nobody was coming to save them. More than anything, he wanted them to feel the same hatred that now consumed him.
Another tremor passed through his consciousness.
Damien had no idea what was happening.

He could not explain the strange sensation spreading through his mind, nor did he understand why his hatred suddenly seemed so incredibly clear. It was no longer simply an emotion he was experiencing. It felt as though he had grasped something intangible, something that had always existed but had remained beyond his perception.
The realization was almost frightening.
His hatred had become a concept. A principle. A path. Revenge.
And somewhere beyond Damien’s understanding, something answered.
A faint ripple passed through the unseen fabric of the world.

It was subtle enough that no ordinary human could have noticed it. There was no explosion of energy, no brilliant light, and no dramatic change in the surrounding environment. The prison remained exactly as it had been, with the inmates continuing their conversations and the guards continuing their routines. Yet beneath that ordinary appearance, something fundamental had shifted.
The world had begun to change. Damien’s eyes suddenly widened.
For the first time since entering Blackridge, he felt something other than pain.

Something was entering his body. At first, the sensation was so faint that he almost dismissed it as another consequence of his injuries. His body was exhausted, his mind was unstable, and he had just endured a brutal beating. It would have been easy to assume that the strange sensation was nothing more than another symptom of his battered condition.
But the feeling continued.

As Damien focused on it, he realized that something unfamiliar was slowly moving through his body. It was weak, almost imperceptible, yet undeniably real. He could feel it entering through his surroundings, slipping into his body and gradually spreading through his flesh.
His breathing stopped. “What...”
The word came out barely above a whisper.

Damien stared blankly ahead, unable to understand what he was experiencing. He had never felt anything like this before. There was no scientific explanation he could immediately associate with the sensation. Yet despite his confusion, there was an undeniable certainty within him.
Something had changed. Something had awakened.

The unfamiliar energy continued moving through his body, slowly circulating through his muscles and blood before following pathways he had never known existed. The sensation was neither entirely warm nor cold. It felt almost weightless, yet at the same time, it carried a presence that Damien could somehow perceive with absolute clarity.
Deep within the depths of his body, an unfamiliar force had begun to take root.
Damien did not know what it was. He did not know where it had come from.
He did not understand why he could suddenly perceive something that should have been completely invisible to ordinary human senses.
He certainly did not know that the change occurring within his body was connected to something far greater than himself.

For countless years, humanity had lived without ever realizing that another form of energy existed beyond the limits of ordinary scientific understanding. The world had changed, civilizations had risen and fallen, and generations of humans had lived and died without ever sensing it.
Qi had existed in the world all along.
It had simply remained dormant, sealed and absorbed out of the world by the formation
But now it was back and something had changed.
The barrier that had separated humanity from that ancient energy was beginning to weaken.
And Damien, consumed by hatred and driven by an overwhelming desire for revenge, had become one of the first humans on Earth to comprehend dao and establish a connection with it.
He did not know its name. He did not understand its origin. He did not know what it would eventually bring.
All he knew was that something was flowing through him.
Something that had never existed within his awareness before.
Something that would change his life forever.
Deep within his body, Qi slowly circulated through his meridians.

chapters.title: Chapter 486: Stirring
paragraphs: For several seconds, Damien remained completely still on the cold concrete floor, unable to make sense of the strange sensation spreading through his body. He had no idea what had just happened or why he could suddenly feel something moving beneath his skin.
The sensation had begun as a faint warmth somewhere around the center of his chest, so subtle that he had initially mistaken it for the lingering heat caused by the beating he had just received.

However, the longer he remained still, the more clearly he could feel it. The warmth gradually spread outward from his chest, flowing through his shoulders, arms, abdomen, and legs in a slow, steady current.
It wasn’t painful. In fact, it was the complete opposite.
There was something strangely refreshing about the sensation, almost as though his entire body was being washed from the inside.
After days of exhaustion, humiliation, and physical pain, the unfamiliar warmth felt almost comforting.

Yet that only made it more unsettling because Damien had never experienced anything remotely similar before. He had no explanation for it, no knowledge that could help him understand what was happening, and no idea why his body suddenly seemed capable of perceiving something that had never existed in his awareness until now.
Slowly, Damien pushed himself up from the floor. His arms trembled beneath his weight, and the movement caused a dull ache to spread through his battered ribs.

His face was swollen from the beating, and dried blood remained caked around his lips and along his chin. A few fresh drops still trickled from one of the cuts on his face, but despite the injuries covering his body, he noticed something strange.
The pain wasn’t as overwhelming as it had been only moments ago.

Damien lowered his gaze toward his hands. They were still trembling slightly, although he wasn’t certain whether the shaking came from his injuries or the strange sensation coursing through his body. He slowly flexed his fingers, opening and closing his hands while examining them as though they belonged to someone else.
“What the hell...” His voice was barely audible.
Something felt different.

He couldn’t explain exactly what had changed, because his body hadn’t suddenly returned to perfect condition. The bruises were still visible, the cuts were still there, and his ribs still hurt whenever he moved too quickly.

Yet beneath all of that pain was a strange sense of vitality that hadn’t existed before. It felt as though something had been added to his body, some source of energy that had been absent throughout his entire life and had only now begun flowing through him.
Damien swallowed as he stared at his hands. ‘What is this?’
Almost instinctively, he closed his eyes.
The moment he stopped relying on his ordinary senses, the strange energy became easier to perceive.
It was still faint, but now he could distinctly feel it moving through him. Tiny streams of unfamiliar energy traveled through his body, following pathways he didn’t know existed.
They flowed from one part of his body to another with a rhythm that seemed almost natural, as though they had always belonged there.

Damien had never studied cultivation. He had never heard anyone seriously discuss meridians, energy circulation, or the existence of Qi. As far as he knew, such things belonged in ancient legends, fantasy novels, and fictional stories.
Yet his body seemed to understand something that his mind could not.
The energy continued circulating through him.

With every cycle, the sensation became clearer. It was almost as if his body were instinctively learning how to handle this unfamiliar force, slowly adapting to its presence without requiring conscious instruction from Damien.
Then something even stranger happened.
A subtle change on his forearm caught his attention.
Damien opened his eyes and immediately looked down.

A shallow cut stretched across his forearm, one of the injuries he had received during the beating. The bleeding had already stopped, which by itself wasn’t particularly unusual. A wound could stop bleeding after some time, especially if it wasn’t particularly deep.
But then Damien noticed something that made his expression slowly change.
The edges of the wound were moving. His eyes widened as he leaned closer.
The damaged skin was gradually pulling itself together.

It wasn’t happening instantly, nor was it some dramatic transformation that would have looked unnatural to an observer. Instead, the process was slow and subtle. The raw flesh beneath the damaged skin began closing little by little, while the edges of the wound gradually drew closer together.
Damien stared at his arm in complete disbelief. “No...”
He leaned closer, almost afraid that his eyes were deceiving him. But they weren’t. The wound was actually healing.
“What...” The word escaped his mouth, but he couldn’t finish the sentence.

For several seconds, Damien simply watched as his own body repaired itself in front of his eyes. A dark bruise near his wrist slowly began to fade, while the swelling around his knuckles diminished. Even the deep ache that had been spreading through his ribs since the beating gradually became less severe.
Damien’s breathing became faster.

He reached down and touched his forearm with trembling fingers. The skin felt warm and completely normal beneath his fingertips. He rubbed the area where the wound had been, almost expecting to feel an open cut, but there was now barely any trace of the injury.
He stared at his arm for several seconds before suddenly looking around the cell.
Nobody seemed to have noticed.

The inmates nearby had already returned to their own activities. Some were talking among themselves, while others were sitting quietly or eating. None of them appeared interested in Damien anymore. As far as they were concerned, the confrontation was over and the rich boy had learned his place.
Damien slowly pushed himself to his feet. This time, his legs felt different. Stronger. Much stronger.

He stood there for a moment, testing his balance before slowly clenching his fists. The strange energy was still circulating through his body, and now that he had become aware of it, he could feel it much more clearly.

chapters.title: Chapter 487: Payback
paragraphs: Feeling energised, Damien stood there for a moment, testing his balance before slowly clenching his fists. The strange energy was still circulating through his body, and now that he had become aware of it, he could feel it much more clearly.
There was strength within him.

Not an overwhelming amount. He certainly didn’t feel invincible, nor did he suddenly possess enough power to destroy everything around him. However, compared to the ordinary strength he had possessed only minutes ago, the difference was undeniable.
Damien looked toward the steel bars separating his cell from the corridor.
A thought suddenly entered his mind.
‘Could I...?’
He immediately dismissed it. That was ridiculous.

The bars were made of reinforced steel and were designed specifically to prevent inmates from escaping. Even a physically powerful man would struggle to bend them without some kind of tool, let alone with his bare hands.
Still, curiosity continued gnawing at him. Damien glanced around once more.
Nobody was paying attention. Slowly, he approached the bars.
When he reached them, he wrapped his fingers around one of the thick metal rods. The cold steel pressed against his palm, and for a moment he simply stood there, staring at it.
He hesitated. Then he pulled. Nothing happened.
Damien frowned. He tightened his grip and pulled again, this time using more strength. His muscles tensed as he leaned backward, putting his entire body behind the movement.
For a moment, the bar remained completely motionless.
Then a faint metallic sound echoed through the cell.
Creak. Damien froze. His eyes widened.
The sound had been faint, but there was no mistaking it.
He slowly looked at the metal bar before shifting his gaze toward his hands.
“No way.”
He tried again.
This time, he put considerably more strength into the movement.
GNNNG—!
The steel groaned. Damien’s eyes nearly bulged from their sockets.
The bar had moved.
He stared at the warped section in disbelief, unable to comprehend what he was seeing. He had expected nothing to happen, yet the reinforced steel had actually bent beneath the force of his hands.
For several seconds, Damien remained frozen. Then he grabbed the bar with both hands.
Something inside him changed.
The disbelief in his expression slowly gave way to excitement.
He pulled with everything he had.
BANG!

The reinforced steel bent outward with a violent metallic groan. The surrounding bars shook from the force, and when Damien finally released them, a gap large enough for a person to pass through had appeared.
Damien stared at the opening.
He couldn’t speak.
His heart was pounding so hard that he could feel it against his chest.
Then, slowly, a grin spread across his battered face.
“Superpowers...”
He laughed quietly, almost unable to believe the words coming from his own mouth.
“Are superpowers actually real?”

Damien looked down at his hands again. Only a short while ago, he had been lying helplessly on the prison floor while three inmates beat him. Now he had bent reinforced steel with nothing but his bare hands.
He flexed his fingers. “Did I just awaken some kind of superpower?”
The realization sent a surge of excitement through him.

His mind immediately began racing through the possibilities. Strength. Regeneration. Some kind of energy. He didn’t know what this strange power was, but he already understood one thing: he was no longer an ordinary human.
And if this power could continue growing...
Damien’s grin widened. He could leave. He could escape Blackridge.
He could return to the outside world, reclaim everything he had lost, and find the people responsible for his downfall.
‘Sophie. Stan.’ His expression slowly darkened as their faces surfaced in his mind.
He could find them.
He could make them pay.
But just as quickly as the thought of escape entered his mind, another thought followed.
Damien’s gaze shifted toward the inmates who had beaten him earlier.
The large man was several meters away, sitting with the other two inmates as they casually talked among themselves. None of them seemed to have noticed what Damien had just done.
Damien stared at them for several seconds.
Then his smile slowly returned.
Why leave now?

He rolled his shoulders, testing his body again. The injuries were still present, but the pain had become almost insignificant compared to what it had been earlier. The strange energy continued circulating through him, gradually easing the effects of the beating.
Damien slowly cracked his knuckles.
Crack.
The sharp sound caught the attention of one of the nearby inmates, who glanced in his direction.
Damien began walking.
One step.
Then another.
The three men eventually noticed him approaching.
The large inmate frowned as he looked up.
“What are you looking at?”
Damien didn’t answer. He simply continued walking toward them.
The man’s expression hardened. “Hey.”
Damien kept coming.
“Who the hell are you staring at like that?” The other two inmates also rose from their seats. One of them scoffed as he looked Damien over. “Looks like the rich boy didn’t learn his lesson.”
The large inmate cracked his neck and stepped forward. “Maybe we need to teach him again.”

Several nearby prisoners began paying attention. Conversations gradually died down as more inmates turned toward the confrontation. The sight of Damien willingly approaching the same three men who had just beaten him was enough to spark curiosity.
Damien eventually stopped a few meters away from them.
He looked at the three men in silence.
There was no fear in his eyes anymore.
The large inmate stared back at him with a mixture of confusion and irritation.
Then Damien smiled. It wasn’t the nervous smile of someone trying to hide his fear, nor was it the forced confidence of someone pretending to be brave. It was colder than that.
There was something unsettling in his expression now, something that hadn’t been there before.
“You should have killed me when you had the chance.”
The large inmate’s brows furrowed. “What?”
Damien’s smile widened.
He slowly tightened his fists as the strange energy within his body continued circulating through his muscles.
“Because now...”
His eyes hardened as he stared directly at the man who had beaten him only moments earlier.
“...it’s my turn.”

The strange energy was still circulating through his body, and now that he had become aware of it, he could feel it much more clearly.
There was strength within him.
Not an overwhelming amount.
He certainly didn’t feel invincible, nor did he suddenly possess enough power to destroy everything around him.
However, compared to the ordinary strength he had possessed only minutes ago, the difference was undeniable.
Damien looked toward the steel bars separating his cell from the corridor.
A thought suddenly entered his mind.
‘Could I...?’
He immediately dismissed it.
That was ridiculous.
The bars were made of reinforced steel and were designed specifically to prevent inmates from escaping.
Even a physically powerful man would struggle to bend them without some kind of tool, let alone with his bare hands.
Still, curiosity continued gnawing at him.
Damien glanced around once more.
Nobody was paying attention.
Slowly, he approached the bars.
When he reached them, he wrapped his fingers around one of the thick metal rods.
The cold steel pressed against his palm, and for a moment he simply stood there, staring at it.
He hesitated.
Then he pulled.
Nothing happened.
Damien frowned.
He tightened his grip and pulled again, this time using more strength.
His muscles tensed as he leaned backward, putting his entire body behind the movement.
For a moment, the bar remained completely motionless.
Then a faint metallic sound echoed through the cell.
Creak.
Damien froze.
His eyes widened.
The sound had been faint, but there was no mistaking it.
He slowly looked at the metal bar before shifting his gaze toward his hands.
“No way.”
He tried again.
This time, he put considerably more strength into the movement.
GNNNG—!
The steel groaned.
Damien’s eyes nearly bulged from their sockets.
The bar had moved.
He stared at the warped section in disbelief, unable to comprehend what he was seeing.
He had expected nothing to happen, yet the reinforced steel had actually bent beneath the force of his hands.
For several seconds, Damien remained frozen.
Then he grabbed the bar with both hands.
Something inside him changed.
The disbelief in his expression slowly gave way to excitement.
He pulled with everything he had.
BANG!
The reinforced steel bent outward with a violent metallic groan.
The surrounding bars shook from the force, and when Damien finally released them, a gap large enough for a person to pass through had appeared.
Damien stared at the opening.
He couldn’t speak.
His heart was pounding so hard that he could feel it against his chest.
Then, slowly, a grin spread across his battered face.

“Are superpowers actually real?”
Damien looked down at his hands again.
Only a short while ago, he had been lying helplessly on the prison floor while three inmates beat him.
Now he had bent reinforced steel with nothing but his bare hands.
He flexed his fingers.
“Did I just awaken some kind of superpower?”
The realization sent a surge of excitement through him.
His mind immediately began racing through the possibilities.
Strength.
Regeneration.
Some kind of energy.
He didn’t know what this strange power was, but he already understood one thing: he was no longer an ordinary human.
And if this power could continue growing...

He could leave.
He could escape Blackridge.
He could return to the outside world, reclaim everything he had lost, and find the people responsible for his downfall.

Stan.’ His expression slowly darkened as their faces surfaced in his mind.
He could find them.
He could make them pay.

The large man was several meters away, sitting with the other two inmates as they casually talked among themselves.
None of them seemed to have noticed what Damien had just done.

Then his smile slowly returned.
Why leave now?
He rolled his shoulders, testing his body again.
The injuries were still present, but the pain had become almost insignificant compared to what it had been earlier.
The strange energy continued circulating through him, gradually easing the effects of the beating.
Damien slowly cracked his knuckles.
Crack.
The sharp sound caught the attention of one of the nearby inmates, who glanced in his direction.
Damien began walking.

Then another.

chapters.title: Chapter 488: Payback 2
paragraphs: "You should have killed me when you had the chance. Because now, it’s my turn."
The large inmate stared at Damien for several seconds, seemingly unable to decide whether he was serious. Then, gradually, a low chuckle escaped his throat.

The sound quickly grew into loud laughter that echoed through the cell block, drawing the attention of several prisoners who had already begun watching the confrontation. He looked Damien up and down, taking in his bruised face, bloodstained clothes, and battered appearance before shaking his head in disbelief.
"You?" His laughter continued for another moment. "You’ve got to be joking."
The other two inmates immediately joined him. One of them leaned against the wall as he laughed, while the other shook his head with an expression of open ridicule.
"I think that beating finally scrambled his brain," one of them said. "Maybe he doesn’t even remember what happened five minutes ago."
The other inmate stepped forward and casually shoved Damien’s shoulder. "Get back on the floor before we put you there ourselves."
Damien didn’t move.
The inmate frowned. He shoved him again, this time with considerably more force.
Yet Damien barely shifted. The man’s expression changed.

He had expected Damien to stumble backward just as he had earlier, but the prisoner standing in front of him now seemed completely different. Damien’s feet remained firmly planted on the floor, and his body didn’t even sway beneath the force of the push.
The inmate stared at him for a moment before trying again.
He pushed harder. Nothing happened.
Damien simply stood there.

The laughter around them gradually died away. A strange silence spread through the nearby section of the cell block as the prisoners began to realize that something was wrong. The inmate slowly lowered his hand and looked at it as though trying to understand why his strength had suddenly become useless.
"What the..."
Damien lowered his gaze toward the hand resting against his chest. He studied it for a moment before slowly raising his eyes to meet the inmate’s.
His expression was remarkably calm.
"You should move."
The inmate’s face twisted with anger. Rather than listening, he pulled his hand away and drew his fist backward.
"Who the hell do you think—"
His sentence never reached its end.
BAM!
Damien’s fist slammed directly into his face.

The impact was so violent that the inmate’s feet immediately left the ground. His massive body was launched backward as though he had been struck by something far heavier than a human fist. He flew several meters before crashing into the concrete wall with a thunderous BOOM that reverberated throughout the cell block.
The man’s body dropped heavily to the floor.
He didn’t move. Silence immediately descended over the entire area.

The prisoners who had been watching stared at the unconscious inmate in disbelief. Some looked from the fallen man to Damien, while others remained completely frozen, seemingly unable to process what they had just witnessed.
Damien himself was equally stunned. He slowly lowered his fist and stared at it.
He had intended to hit the man. He had wanted to teach him a lesson and prove that he was no longer helpless. But he hadn’t expected the result to be anything like this.
He had sent a grown man flying several meters with a single punch.
Damien’s breathing became slightly heavier as he looked at the unconscious inmate.
’So this is my strength now...’

A strange thrill spread through him. For the first time in his life, Damien felt genuine power coursing through his body. It wasn’t the kind of power that came from his family’s wealth, connections, or influence. This was something that belonged entirely to him. Nobody had given it to him, and nobody could take it away.
Before he could dwell on the thought any further, a furious shout erupted from the side.
"YOU BASTARD!" The second inmate charged toward him.
Damien turned just in time to see the man’s fist flying toward his face. The punch came with enough force to injure him badly if it landed, but Damien’s body reacted almost instinctively.
He raised his arm.
THUD!
The fist slammed into his forearm.
Damien didn’t even flinch.

The attacking inmate’s expression immediately changed. He had expected the punch to send Damien staggering backward, but the impact seemed to have done absolutely nothing. Damien’s arm remained firmly in place, and his expression showed no sign of pain.
Before the inmate could pull his arm back, Damien’s hand shot forward and clamped around his wrist.
The man’s eyes widened.
Damien’s fingers tightened.
"AH!"
A sharp cry escaped the inmate as pain shot through his wrist. Damien looked at him calmly, studying the man’s reaction as though he were testing the limits of his newly acquired strength.
"You hit me with this hand earlier," Damien said.
His grip tightened further.
"Remember?"
The inmate’s knees began to buckle.
"Let go!"
Damien ignored him. Instead, he twisted his body and swung the inmate sideways with a single powerful motion.
CRASH!
The man’s body slammed into the metal bars of the opposite cell. The impact caused the entire section of bars to rattle violently, and the inmate collapsed to the floor in a heap.
The third man froze.
Whatever confidence he had possessed moments earlier disappeared completely. His eyes moved from one unconscious companion to the other before slowly returning to Damien.
The expression on his face was no longer mocking.
It was fear.
"What... what happened to you?"
Damien slowly turned toward him. For a moment, neither man spoke.
Then a smile appeared on Damien’s face. It was not a reassuring smile.

There was something deeply unsettling about the expression of a man who had spent days being humiliated and beaten, only to suddenly discover that he possessed enough strength to overpower the people who had tormented him.
"I don’t know," Damien admitted.
He took a step forward.
"But I like it."
The inmate immediately took a step backward. "Stay back."
Damien continued walking.
"Don’t come any closer."
Another step.

The inmate’s breathing became increasingly frantic. He looked around desperately, searching for somewhere to escape, but there was nowhere to go. The prisoners who had been watching the confrontation had already moved aside, leaving the two men with a clear path between them.

chapters.title: Chapter 489: Prison Break
paragraphs: Suddenly, the inmate turned and ran. But he didn’t even make it three steps.
Damien moved.

His hand shot forward and grabbed the back of the man’s prison uniform. With the strength now coursing through his body, the motion was effortless. Damien yanked him backward, and the inmate stumbled violently before losing his balance.
Damien stepped forward and drove his fist into the man’s stomach.
THUD!
The inmate doubled over immediately, a strangled gasp escaping his mouth as the force of the blow drove the air from his lungs.
Before he could recover, Damien struck him again.
The second blow sent him crashing onto the floor.
The inmate remained there, coughing and struggling to breathe.
Damien stood over him.
For several seconds, he simply stared.

The sight of the man lying helplessly on the floor brought back memories of what had happened earlier. He remembered being surrounded by the three inmates. He remembered the punches, the kicks, the laughter, and the humiliation. He remembered lying helplessly against the concrete while they told him that nobody cared about his family or his money.
Something inside him twisted.
His foot slowly lifted.
For a brief moment, Damien considered bringing it down.
Then he stopped.
His expression changed as a strange thought entered his mind.
They’re already defeated.
His raised foot remained suspended for another moment before he slowly lowered it.
Damien looked at the three men lying around him.
There was no need to continue. He had already proven what he wanted to prove.
More importantly, he had begun to understand something about the strange power that had awakened within him.

The sensation inside his body had grown stronger during the confrontation. The unfamiliar energy was still circulating through his muscles and limbs, moving through him in a steady rhythm. Each time he used his strength, he became more aware of it.
His awakening hadn’t simply made him physically stronger.
Something else had changed. Something had happened inside him when his hatred had reached its absolute limit.
The moment he had truly desired revenge, something had answered.

Damien didn’t understand the nature of that power yet. He didn’t know where it came from or what it would eventually allow him to do. He didn’t even know the name of the energy moving through his body.
But he knew it was connected to what had happened earlier.
His hatred had awakened something. And that realization filled him with an excitement that was almost intoxicating.
Damien glanced down at the three defeated inmates.
"Pathetic."
He turned away from them and walked toward the steel bars separating the cell from the main corridor.
The surrounding prisoners watched him carefully.
Nobody laughed now. Nobody mocked him. Nobody dared challenge him.

There was a new tension throughout the cell block, and Damien could feel it. The same men who had ignored him earlier were now staring at him with a mixture of fear and uncertainty. They didn’t understand what had happened either, but they had witnessed enough to know that Damien was no longer the weak, arrogant rich boy they had seen earlier.
Damien reached the bars and placed one hand around one of the reinforced steel rods.
He stared at it for a moment.
A grin slowly appeared across his face.
This time, he didn’t hesitate.
He tightened his grip and pulled.
GNNNNG!
The metal immediately groaned beneath his strength.
The reinforced bar began bending outward.
Damien’s eyes widened slightly as he watched the steel deform beneath his hand. He applied more force, and the gap widened until there was enough room for a person to pass through.
He released the bar.
For several seconds, Damien simply stared at the opening.
Then he stepped through.
He was free.
For the first time since being imprisoned, Damien stood outside his cell.
He slowly looked down the long corridor.

Rows upon rows of cells stretched in both directions, their steel doors and reinforced bars separating hundreds of inmates from one another. The prison’s harsh fluorescent lighting cast a pale glow over the corridor, illuminating the faces of countless prisoners who were now staring directly at Damien.
Some looked confused.
Others looked frightened.
A few appeared excited by the sudden development.
Damien’s eyes moved across them all.
Then his gaze shifted toward the distant security doors.
He could leave.
He could simply run.
If his current strength allowed him to break through the cell bars, perhaps he could also overpower the prison guards and escape the facility entirely.
The thought was tempting.
Very tempting.
But another thought entered his mind.
Damien looked back at the rows of prisoners surrounding him.
A slow smile spread across his face.
"Why should I be the only one?"
He approached the nearest cell.
A prisoner inside immediately backed away from the bars, watching Damien with suspicion.
"What are you doing?"
Damien didn’t answer.
He simply grabbed the reinforced bars.
The prisoner watched as Damien’s fingers tightened around the steel.
CREAK.
The metal began bending.
The prisoner’s eyes widened.
"What the hell?"
Damien pulled harder.
The bars groaned loudly as they twisted beneath his strength. Within seconds, the opening became wide enough for the prisoner to squeeze through.
Damien released the metal and looked at him.
"You’re free."
For several seconds, the prisoner remained frozen.
His expression shifted from confusion to disbelief as he looked at the opening and then back at Damien.
Then excitement took over.
He immediately ran into the corridor.
Damien watched him disappear before turning toward the next cell.
Then the next.
And the next.

Every time his hands wrapped around the reinforced bars, the result was the same. The metal bent beneath his strength, creating openings where there had previously been none. Some bars required more effort than others, but none were capable of stopping him.
CREAK.
BANG.
CRASH.
One cell after another opened.
The atmosphere of the prison changed almost instantly.
What had begun as confusion quickly transformed into chaos.
"What happened?"
"The cells are open!"
"Get out!"
"Run!"
"Life sentence my ass, I’m out of here..."

chapters.title: Chapter 490: Prison Break (2)
paragraphs: Prisoners poured into the corridors.

Some immediately rushed toward the exits, desperate to take advantage of the unexpected opportunity. Others stood frozen for several seconds before finally realizing that they were no longer trapped inside their cells. A few began shouting and laughing, while others hurried after the prisoners who had already escaped.
Within moments, the orderly environment of Blackridge Correctional Facility had collapsed into disorder.

Damien continued moving from cell to cell, tearing open the reinforced barriers as though they were nothing more than ordinary metal fences. The noise of bending steel, shouting prisoners, running footsteps, and slamming doors filled the facility.
He wasn’t thinking about the consequences anymore.
He wasn’t thinking about the guards.
He wasn’t thinking about the prison administration or what would happen when the authorities discovered what he had done.
For the first time in his life, Damien had discovered something that felt like genuine power.
His wealth had given him influence.
His family name had given him status.
But this...
This belonged entirely to him.
And he wanted to know exactly how far it could take him.
Then the prison alarm suddenly erupted.
WEEEEEE-OOO!
The piercing sound echoed through every corridor of Blackridge.

Red warning lights immediately began flashing across the facility, bathing the walls and faces of the prisoners in an ominous glow. Heavy security doors began closing in distant sections, while hurried footsteps echoed through the corridors as guards scrambled to respond to the sudden breach.
A mechanical voice boomed through the prison’s speaker system.
"PRISON BREACH DETECTED."
The message repeated throughout the facility.
"ALL SECURITY PERSONNEL REPORT TO CELL BLOCK C."
Damien stopped in the middle of the corridor.
He slowly raised his head and looked toward the ceiling as the alarm continued screaming around him.
Then he turned toward the approaching sound of hurried footsteps.
The guards were coming.
Damien’s grin gradually widened.
He rolled his shoulders and slowly cracked his neck.
"Ah."
His eyes narrowed with anticipation.
"Here they come.
The alarm continued to blare throughout Blackridge Correctional Facility, its piercing siren reverberating against the thick concrete walls.
Red warning lights flashed continuously across the cell block, bathing the prison in an eerie crimson glow.

Heavy footsteps thundered through the corridors as security personnel rushed toward the disturbance, their voices mixing with the commotion of hundreds of prisoners who had suddenly been released from their cells.
The inmates scattered in every direction.

Some sprinted toward the nearest exits, desperate to escape before the prison authorities could regain control. Others wandered through the corridors in confusion, seemingly unable to believe that the cell doors that had confined them for years were suddenly open.
Amid all of it, Damien remained completely still.

He stood in the middle of the corridor, surrounded by the remnants of the prison cells he had torn open. The red emergency lights reflected off his battered face, illuminating the bruises and dried blood that still covered him.
Only a short while earlier, he had been lying helplessly on the concrete floor after being beaten by three inmates.
Now, those injuries seemed almost insignificant.
His attention remained fixed on the corridor ahead.

He could hear the guards approaching. There were several of them, judging from the number of footsteps echoing through the corridor. Their voices grew progressively louder as they moved closer, accompanied by the hurried clatter of equipment and heavy boots pounding against the concrete.
"Lock down the entire block!"
"Get those prisoners back into their cells!"
"Move! Don’t let them reach the next section!"
Damien listened calmly.
A few seconds later, a heavy metal security door at the end of the corridor opened with a loud mechanical hiss.
A squad of armed guards rushed through the doorway, their weapons raised as they immediately began scanning the chaotic cell block.

The guards were clearly prepared to deal with a prison disturbance. Some shouted at fleeing inmates while others spread out across the corridor, attempting to establish a defensive line and prevent the prisoners from reaching the deeper sections of the facility.
One of them suddenly spotted Damien.
"You!"
The guard immediately pointed his weapon at him.
"Get on the ground!"
Damien slowly turned his head.
His eyes moved from the guard’s face to the weapon pointed directly at him.
Then his gaze shifted toward the bent steel bars beside him, the same reinforced bars he had torn apart with his bare hands.
For some reason, the command almost made him laugh.
Only a few hours ago, Damien would have obeyed immediately. He would have lowered his head, followed the guards’ instructions, and done whatever was necessary to avoid further trouble.
But that Damien no longer existed.
The man standing in the corridor now had experienced something that had fundamentally changed his perception of himself.
He had discovered strength within his own body.
Strength that had nothing to do with money, family connections, or social status.
He wasn’t afraid.
"Get on the ground!" the guard shouted again.
Damien tilted his head slightly.
"No."
The simple response caused several of the guards to exchange surprised glances.
The officer at the front stepped forward, his expression becoming more serious.
"Don’t make this worse for yourself."
Damien looked at him for a moment before a faint smile appeared on his face.
"You have no idea how much worse this already is."
The officer’s expression hardened.
"Last warning."
He raised his weapon slightly.
Damien’s eyes briefly moved toward the guns.
Unlike the prisoners he had just defeated, these men were armed and trained. Whatever power had awakened inside him, Damien understood that it did not necessarily make him invulnerable.
He could bend steel and overpower grown men.
But he had no idea how his body would respond to a bullet.
That realization made him cautious.
He couldn’t simply charge toward a group of armed men and assume his newfound strength would protect him.
His gaze briefly swept across the chaotic corridor.
Hundreds of prisoners were still running through the facility.
The guards couldn’t simply open fire.
Not here.
Not with so many inmates scattering in every direction.

chapters.title: Chapter 491: Prison Break (3)
paragraphs: The guards couldn’t simply open fire. Not here, not with hundreds of inmates scattering through the prison in every direction. The corridors were crowded with desperate prisoners trying to escape, and a stray bullet could easily strike someone who had nothing to do with the confrontation. A burst of uncontrolled gunfire could turn an already chaotic prison riot into a massacre within seconds. Even if the guards wanted to eliminate the threat in front of them, they would have to think carefully before pulling their triggers.
Damien’s eyes narrowed as he considered the situation.

The hesitation of the guards was already working in his favor. Their firearms were powerful, but the presence of so many prisoners made using them recklessly far too dangerous. That meant they would probably try other methods first, relying on their numbers and whatever non-lethal equipment they had available before resorting to their rifles.
And if they eventually decided that shooting him was their only option, Damien already had an answer for that.

His gaze slowly shifted toward the surrounding prisoners. There were dozens of bodies moving through the corridor, each one another potential obstacle between him and a bullet. If the guards truly decided to fire, he would simply find something—or someone—to put between himself and their weapons.

A cold smile gradually spread across his face at the thought, but he kept the plan to himself. There was no reason to reveal his intentions before he needed to. For now, the most important thing was to observe the guards and see what they would do.
The officer standing at the front of the group lowered his weapon slightly before barking another command. "Take him down!"
Three guards immediately stepped forward.

Unlike the heavily armed security personnel who were still making their way toward the cell block, these men weren’t carrying firearms. The prison had descended into chaos too quickly for every guard to properly equip himself. Those who had arrived first had grabbed whatever equipment was immediately available, while the more heavily armed security teams were still moving through the facility toward the source of the disturbance.
Damien didn’t retreat. He remained exactly where he was, watching the approaching guards with an unsettling calmness.
The first guard suddenly charged at him, lowering his shoulder as he attempted to tackle Damien to the ground before the strange strength in his body could become a greater problem.
Damien waited until the very last possible moment.
Then he stepped aside.

The guard rushed past him, his momentum carrying him forward as he suddenly realized that his target was no longer in front of him. Before he could recover his balance, Damien reached out, seized his arm, and used the man’s own momentum against him. With a powerful pull, Damien redirected him toward the wall.
BAM!

The guard’s body slammed violently into the concrete. The impact reverberated through the corridor as his shoulder and back struck the hard surface, leaving him momentarily stunned. He collapsed heavily onto the floor, struggling to regain his senses.
The second guard attacked almost immediately.
He swung his baton toward Damien’s head with enough force to seriously injure an ordinary man. Damien reacted instinctively, raising his arm to protect himself.
CLANG!
The baton smashed against his forearm.
The guard’s expression changed almost instantly.
Damien didn’t even flinch.

He slowly glanced down at his arm as though inspecting the spot where the weapon had struck him. There was no serious pain, no fracture, and not even the reaction the guard had expected from a normal human being.
Damien then raised his eyes toward him.
Before the guard could swing again, Damien reached forward and grabbed the baton.

The guard instinctively pulled backward, attempting to wrench the weapon from Damien’s grasp, but the effort was completely useless. Damien’s grip felt immovable. No matter how hard the guard pulled, the baton didn’t move even an inch.
Then Damien tightened his fingers and yanked.
The baton tore free so effortlessly that the guard nearly stumbled forward.
Damien tossed the weapon aside without giving it another thought. Before the guard could recover, Damien planted one hand against his body and shoved him backward.
The force behind the movement was far beyond what the guard expected.

His feet actually left the ground as his body was launched several meters backward before crashing heavily onto the concrete. He rolled across the floor and came to a stop, dazed and unable to immediately understand how a man of Damien’s size had produced that kind of strength.
The third guard had been preparing to attack, but he stopped.

After watching his two companions get thrown aside with almost no effort, whatever confidence he had possessed disappeared. His grip on his weapon tightened, but his feet remained firmly planted where they were.
Damien slowly turned toward him.
The guard instinctively took a step backward.
His face had gone pale, and the fear in his eyes was impossible to hide.
"What are you?" he asked, his voice trembling.
For a moment, Damien didn’t answer.

The question struck closer to home than the guard could have known. Damien himself still didn’t understand what had happened to his body. He didn’t know what had triggered the sudden transformation, where this incredible strength had come from, or what exactly the strange power coursing through his muscles represented.
He only knew that he was no longer the same man who had entered the prison.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"I don’t know yet," Damien finally replied.
He took a slow step forward, forcing the frightened guard to retreat another step.
"But I’m starting to like the answer."
The guard’s fear intensified. Whatever courage he had left finally abandoned him, and he turned around and ran. His footsteps echoed through the corridor as he disappeared around the corner.
Damien watched him leave but made no attempt to pursue him. There was no point wasting time on a man who had already decided to flee.
His attention shifted toward the security doors ahead.

Beyond those doors were more checkpoints, more security barriers, and eventually the outside world. The prison was still filled with chaos, but every second he remained inside increased the chance of encountering a response team capable of stopping him.
Freedom was within reach.
Damien took another step toward the security doors.

chapters.title: Chapter 492: A Human Shield
paragraphs: Damien could see that freedom was within reach as he took another step toward the security doors.
But then a groan came from the side of the corridor.
He turned his head and noticed one of the guards caught in the earlier chaos lying against the wall.

His uniform was torn, and several bruises covered his face. Blood stained part of his clothing, and although he was conscious, he looked barely capable of moving. He struggled to push himself upright, but his arms trembled beneath him.
Damien glanced at him for only a moment before turning his attention back toward the corridor.
Then he heard something.

Footsteps were approaching from his side and more footsteps were approaching from the distance ahead, but these were different from the frantic movements of the guards who had rushed into the area earlier.
These footsteps were steady, deliberate, and coordinated. There was none of the confusion or panic that had characterized the first response.
Then came another sound. It was the sound of metal: the unmistakable mechanical clicks of weapons being prepared.
Damien’s expression immediately hardened.

Several guards emerged from the distant corridor, and unlike the men who had confronted him moments earlier, these guards were properly equipped. Rifles were already raised, their barrels pointed directly toward him as they advanced cautiously through the corridor.
Damien’s eyes immediately settled on the injured guard lying against the wall.
The decision was instantaneous.

Before the armed guards could properly react, Damien crossed the distance between them and the injured man with startling speed. He bent down, grabbed the front of the guard’s uniform, and hauled him upright.
The injured man barely had time to react before Damien pulled him against his body and positioned him directly between himself and the armed guards.
The guard groaned weakly from the sudden movement.
"What are you doing?" he managed to whisper.
Damien didn’t answer.
Instead, he tightened his grip and kept the injured man firmly in front of him.
The armed guards immediately stopped advancing.
They understood what Damien had done. They understood his plan, it was very obvious Damien was set on using the guard as a meat shield...
If they fired now, there was a very real possibility that they would hit their own man.
"Don’t shoot!" one of them shouted.
Damien stared calmly at the rifles aimed in his direction.

"Put the guns down." His voice was surprisingly calm considering the situation. He wasn’t shouting, nor did he sound particularly angry. He simply spoke with the confidence of someone who knew the people in front of him were now trapped by their own hesitation.
The guards exchanged uncertain looks, some of them knew the guy, and didn’t want to take the risk...
This was someone life they’re talking about... They can’t bear to kill their fellow comrade in arms...
"Lower your weapons!" one of them shouted.
For a brief moment, it appeared that they might actually comply.
But then everything went wrong. A nervous finger tightened around a trigger.
BANG!
The gunshot exploded through the corridor.
The injured guard in Damien’s arms jerked violently as the bullet struck him. A pained groan escaped his throat, and his body briefly went rigid from the impact.
The armed guards froze.
For a moment, the entire corridor seemed to fall silent.
Then another gunshot rang out.
BANG!
The injured guard cried out as another bullet struck him. His body convulsed in Damien’s grip, and his breathing became increasingly ragged.
"Stop!"
One of the armed guards shouted desperately, but the situation had already spiraled beyond their control.
More shots followed.
BANG! BANG!

The injured guard’s body jerked repeatedly from the impacts as the rifles continued to thunder through the corridor. His face twisted in agony, and his strength rapidly began to disappear. His head eventually sagged weakly against Damien’s shoulder, his breathing reduced to shallow, painful gasps.
Damien, however, didn’t release him.
Instead, he tightened his grip and began moving forward.
Slowly, deliberately and without hesitation, he was already set on escaping no matter what..

Each step forward carried him closer to the security doors while the injured guard remained positioned between him and the rifles. The armed men were forced to hesitate every time they considered firing again, knowing that another bullet could easily kill their own colleague.
The situation had finally shifted in Damien’s favor.
The guards had the weapons. But Damien had the shield and he was careful utilising it perfectly well, not daring to expose any part that’ll put him in danger...
The injured guard’s strength was fading rapidly. His body had become increasingly limp in Damien’s arms, and his head rested heavily against Damien’s shoulder.
"Please..."
The word was barely audible.
Damien lowered his eyes toward him, scoffing coldly...
For a moment, the injured guard seemed to be searching for some sign of mercy in his expression.
But he found none.
There was no sympathy in Damien’s eyes. No hesitation. The man was simply a means to an end, and Damien had no intention of allowing emotion to interfere with his escape.
He adjusted his grip, keeping the injured guard firmly between himself and the rifles, and continued toward the security doors.
The guards couldn’t simply shoot him anymore.
Not without risking the life of their own man.
Not without potentially turning the entire corridor into an even greater disaster.
For the first time since the armed guards had arrived, Damien felt that he had control of the situation.
But then, a powerful voice suddenly thundered through the corridor, cutting through the lingering gunfire and confusion with such authority that even the panicked prisoners seemed to hesitate.
"CEASE FIRE!"
The command echoed off the concrete walls, overpowering the alarms and the scattered shouts that had filled the prison moments earlier.

The firing stopped almost immediately. One by one, the guards lowered their weapons, though many kept their fingers close to the triggers as they continued watching Damien warily. The sudden silence that followed felt almost unnatural after the chaos of the previous few minutes. Smoke from the gunfire lingered in the air, mixing with the metallic scent of blood and the stale odor of the prison corridors.

He adjusted his grip, keeping the injured guard firmly between himself and the rifles, and continued toward the security doors.
The guards couldn’t simply shoot him anymore.
Not without risking the life of their own man.
Not without potentially turning the entire corridor into an even greater disaster.
For the first time since the armed guards had arrived, Damien felt that he had control of the situation.
But then, a powerful voice suddenly thundered through the corridor, cutting through the lingering gunfire and confusion with such authority that even the panicked prisoners seemed to hesitate.
"CEASE FIRE!"
The command echoed off the concrete walls, overpowering the alarms and the scattered shouts that had filled the prison moments earlier.
The firing stopped almost immediately.
One by one, the guards lowered their weapons, though many kept their fingers close to the triggers as they continued watching Damien warily.
The sudden silence that followed felt almost unnatural after the chaos of the previous few minutes.
Smoke from the gunfire lingered in the air, mixing with the metallic scent of blood and the stale odor of the prison corridors.

chapters.title: Chapter 493: The Escape
paragraphs: "CEASE FIRE!" as the guards all stopped on order, a senior officer pushed his way through the formation of guards and stepped into view. He was clearly the highest-ranking officer present, judging by the way the others immediately made room for him. His uniform was more heavily decorated than those of the ordinary guards, and the expression on his face carried the authority of someone accustomed to being obeyed without question.
His eyes immediately settled on the injured guard Damien was holding.
Then they shifted to Damien.
The officer’s expression darkened.
"Stop firing!" he ordered again, raising both hands toward the guards behind him. "Nobody shoots unless I give the order."

The remaining guards obeyed, reluctantly lowering their weapons while maintaining their positions. Their attention remained fixed on Damien, their bodies tense as they waited for the slightest movement from him.
Damien simply stared at the officer.
Then, slowly, the corners of his mouth lifted into a smile.
This was exactly what he had been waiting for.

He had already realized that the guards were reluctant to fire while one of their own men remained in his grasp. The officer’s arrival had only confirmed it. As long as Damien maintained control of the wounded guard, the firearms pointed in his direction were little more than threats.
The head guard stared at him for several seconds before speaking.
"Let him go."

Damien glanced down at the wounded guard in his arms. The man’s face was pale, his breathing shallow and uneven, and blood continued to seep through his uniform. He was barely conscious, but he was still alive.
Damien looked back at the officer.
"You’re not going to shoot me."
The officer’s jaw tightened. "You’re holding one of my men."
"Exactly."
Damien’s smile widened slightly.

The officer’s expression became increasingly grim. He understood the situation perfectly. Damien had found himself a shield, and as long as he continued using the injured guard as protection, firing at him would risk killing their own man.
"Put him down and surrender," the officer ordered.
Damien gave a quiet laugh. "Surrender?"
His gaze slowly traveled around the prison.

The cells were open. Prisoners were running through the corridors in every direction, some desperately searching for exits while others took advantage of the chaos to attack guards or escape deeper into the facility. Alarms continued screaming overhead, emergency lights flashed across the walls, and the guards were struggling to coordinate their response.
The prison was already falling apart around them.
Damien looked back at the officer.
"After all this?"
The head guard took a cautious step forward. "You won’t get far."
Damien’s smile widened.
"That’s what everyone keeps telling me."

He began moving backward, keeping the wounded guard positioned between himself and the armed men. Every step was deliberate. He did not rush, because he knew there was no reason to give the guards an excuse to react.
The guards remained completely still.
Nobody fired.
Damien continued retreating.

Behind him, the heavy security doors leading toward the outer section of the facility gradually came into view. He had been hoping to reach them from the moment the officer ordered the shooting to stop.
When his back finally reached the doors, Damien briefly glanced over his shoulder.

The doors were heavily reinforced, constructed from thick metal and secured by an electronic locking mechanism. Under normal circumstances, forcing them open would have been impossible without the proper authorization or specialized equipment.
Damien stared at them for a moment.
Then he smiled.
He released the injured guard with one arm and placed his free hand against the metal.
The moment the guards realized what he intended to do, several of them immediately raised their weapons again.
"Stop him!" the head guard shouted.
Damien ignored him.

The strange energy that had awakened within his body surged through his limbs. He still didn’t understand what it was or where it came from, but he could feel it moving beneath his skin, responding to his will with an almost instinctive obedience.
His fingers tightened around the edge of the security door.
Then he pulled.
The metal groaned.

At first, nothing seemed to happen. Then the locking mechanism began to bend beneath the tremendous force he was applying. The sound of twisting metal echoed through the corridor, and the guards stared in disbelief as the reinforced mechanism slowly distorted.
"What the hell...?" one of them muttered.
Damien gritted his teeth and pulled harder.
The strange energy within his body surged again.
With a violent metallic shriek, the damaged locking mechanism finally gave way.
The heavy security door swung open.
For several seconds, nobody moved.
The guards simply stared.

Even the head officer appeared momentarily stunned. Whatever Damien had become, he was clearly no longer an ordinary prisoner. A man who could tear apart a reinforced security mechanism with his bare hands was not someone they could casually restrain.
Damien looked back at them.
A smug smile appeared across his battered face.
"Goodbye."
Before anyone could respond, he turned and disappeared through the opening.
"After him!" the head guard shouted.
But Damien was already running.

He sprinted through the outer section of the facility as the prison continued descending into chaos behind him. Sirens echoed throughout the grounds, emergency lights flashed against the concrete walls, and distant shouting followed him as guards attempted to reorganize their forces. Somewhere behind him, prisoners were still fighting, escaping, and taking advantage of the confusion.
Damien did not look back.

He continued running until he reached one of the service areas surrounding the facility. Several vehicles were parked there, but most appeared to have been abandoned in the middle of the emergency response.
Then he spotted one that immediately caught his attention.
A prison staff vehicle sat near the edge of the service area.
Damien ran toward it. He tried the driver’s door forcing it open...
