chapters.title: Chapter 494: Chase
paragraphs: A prison staff vehicle sat near the edge of the service area.
Damien ran toward it. He tried the driver’s door forcing it open...
After forcing the car open Damien climbed into the vehicle and immediately checked the ignition.
His eyes widened slightly when he found the keys still sitting where the previous driver had left them. The car had no door keys but there was an ignition key inside...
For a moment, he simply stared at them, almost unable to believe that something so convenient had fallen into his hands. Then, slowly, a grin spread across his battered face.
"Perfect."
He turned the key, and the engine roared to life.

Damien slammed his foot onto the accelerator. The vehicle lurched forward with enough force to push him back against the seat, and the tires screeched as they struggled for traction against the pavement. He tore across the prison grounds, weaving between abandoned vehicles, overturned equipment, scattered debris, and the remnants of the riot that had transformed Blackridge Correctional Facility into a battlefield.

Behind him, alarms continued to scream through the compound. Their shrill wailing echoed against the concrete buildings, blending with the shouting of guards and the thunderous roar of hundreds of prisoners flooding through corridors and courtyards. Smoke drifted through the air, doors hung open, and security personnel rushed from one crisis to another, hopelessly overwhelmed by the sudden collapse of order. The entire facility had descended into chaos, and Damien barely spared it a glance.
His attention remained fixed on the road ahead.

His hands tightened around the steering wheel as he accelerated toward the outer security gate. The massive gate stood open, its usual security measures rendered useless by the prison riot. The guards stationed nearby were far too distracted to notice him immediately. Most were occupied with prisoners escaping into the surrounding areas, while others desperately tried to restore some semblance of control within the facility.
Then one guard turned.
His eyes widened when he saw the vehicle speeding toward the open gate.
"Stop that vehicle!"
Damien didn’t even consider slowing down.
The guard hurriedly reached for his radio. "Suspect escaping through the east gate! Repeat, suspect escaping through the east gate!"

Damien shot through the opening before anyone could react. The vehicle bounced violently as it crossed the boundary, its suspension groaning beneath the impact, before its tires slammed onto the road outside the prison.
For the first time in a while, Damien was outside.
He was free.
The realization struck him with such force that a laugh escaped his throat. It began as a quiet, disbelieving chuckle before growing louder, until he was laughing openly behind the steering wheel.
"I’m free..."
The words sounded almost foreign coming from his mouth.
He pressed harder on the accelerator, and the vehicle surged forward.

For several minutes, Damien simply drove. The prison gradually disappeared behind him, swallowed by distance as city streets replaced the walls and security towers of Blackridge. Buildings rose along either side of the road, traffic moved through the intersections, and ordinary life continued around him as though nothing extraordinary had happened.
Then he heard it.
A faint siren.
Damien’s smile disappeared.
He glanced into the rearview mirror and saw flashes of red and blue approaching in the distance. One police cruiser emerged from behind the traffic, followed by another.
"Already?"
The police vehicles accelerated.
A loudspeaker crackled behind him.
"Pull the vehicle over!"
"Pull over immediately!"

Damien looked at the road ahead, then back at the police vehicles closing in behind him. Under normal circumstances, the sight of multiple police cruisers pursuing him would have filled him with fear. Instead, something entirely different began to stir inside his chest.
Excitement.
His hands tightened around the steering wheel, and a strange smile slowly returned to his face.
"So they want to catch me?"
He pressed the accelerator to the floor.

The engine roared, and the vehicle surged forward with startling force. The speed climbed rapidly, far faster than Damien had expected. Within seconds, the distance between him and the nearest police cruiser began to increase.
The officer behind the wheel immediately realized what was happening.
"He’s accelerating!"
He grabbed the radio while keeping his eyes locked on the fleeing vehicle. "Dispatch, suspect is refusing to stop. Request additional units and an intercept ahead."
Another voice answered through the radio. "Units are being dispatched. Maintain pursuit."
More sirens soon joined the first.

Damien glanced into the rearview mirror and saw several additional police vehicles entering the pursuit. Their lights flashed across the surrounding buildings, while the combined wail of their sirens echoed through the streets.
"All of you?
His grin widened.
He pushed the accelerator even farther.
The vehicle shot forward.

Buildings blurred past the windows. Streetlights became elongated streaks of light, and the surrounding traffic seemed to move almost unnaturally slowly. Damien’s grip tightened as he approached a major intersection, where one of the pursuing cruisers suddenly accelerated ahead of him and attempted to position itself across his path.
Damien noticed the maneuver almost immediately.
He should have been too late.
Yet something strange happened.
His perception seemed to sharpen.

For a brief moment, the world appeared clearer. He could see the police cruiser, the movement of the surrounding traffic, the gaps between vehicles, and the narrow opening beside the cruiser. His mind processed everything with an unnatural speed, calculating the available space almost instinctively.
His newly awakened body reacted before he had consciously finished thinking.
Damien jerked the steering wheel.

The vehicle swerved sharply and slipped through the narrowing gap between the police cruiser and the surrounding traffic. The police vehicle missed him by only a few feet before Damien straightened the wheel and continued down another road.
"Where did he go?!"
Damien laughed.
His heartbeat pounded against his chest, but there was no fear in it. If anything, he felt exhilarated.
This wasn’t simply driving anymore.
Something inside him had changed.

His enhanced perception allowed him to recognize openings before they fully developed. His reactions were faster than they should have been, and his body seemed capable of responding to danger almost before his conscious mind registered it.
But the pursuit wasn’t over.
More police vehicles appeared ahead.

Damien’s expression hardened as he continued through the city. He wasn’t merely relying on speed anymore. He watched everything around him—the roads, intersections, traffic patterns, approaching vehicles, and the positioning of the police cruisers behind him. Whenever the authorities attempted to close one route, he shifted toward another before their blockade could fully form.

chapters.title: Chapter 495: Fugitive
paragraphs: The pursuit continued through several streets.
Eventually, Damien noticed something strange on the vehicle’s dashboard. A small indicator light caught his attention, one he hadn’t noticed during his initial escape.
His eyes narrowed.
A tracking signal.
He stared at it for several seconds before understanding what it meant.
Then he remembered the vehicle itself.
Of course.
It belonged to the prison.
The authorities could probably track it.
"So that’s how they’re keeping up..."
His expression darkened.

He didn’t need to be a genius to understand the problem. As long as he remained inside the prison vehicle, the police would always have a way to locate him. Speed alone wouldn’t solve the problem. Eventually, they would coordinate enough units to surround him.
Damien looked toward the road ahead, then glanced at the pursuing vehicles in his mirrors.
A cold smile slowly appeared.
"Fine."
He began searching for an opportunity.

The pursuit continued through several more streets, with police vehicles attempting to intercept him from multiple directions. Damien repeatedly changed course whenever he noticed them forming a blockade ahead. He was no longer simply running from the police; he was studying them, anticipating their movements, and exploiting every weakness in their pursuit.
Eventually, he found what he needed.

A quieter stretch of road appeared ahead. There were fewer vehicles, and several large buildings lined one side of the street. On the opposite side, a narrow service road branched away between the buildings, leading into a darker and more secluded section of the city.
Damien’s eyes narrowed.
’That would do.’ He deliberately slowed the vehicle.
The pursuing officers immediately reacted.
"He’s slowing down!"
"He’s boxed in!"
One cruiser moved into position behind him while another approached from farther ahead, attempting to close the remaining escape route.
Damien’s lips curled upward.
They thought they had him. At the last possible moment, he turned sharply.

The vehicle shot toward the service road, forcing the pursuing cruisers to adjust their positions and follow. Damien drove deeper into the narrow passage before finally spotting the secluded area he had been looking for—a concealed space between several large buildings where the surrounding structures would block the line of sight from the main road.
He slammed on the brakes.
The tires screamed against the pavement, and the vehicle lurched violently as it came to a stop.
Before the pursuing officers could understand what he was doing, Damien had already thrown open the driver’s door.
He jumped out.

His boots struck the pavement hard, but instead of stumbling, he immediately recovered his balance. The strange energy flowing through his body surged instinctively, absorbing much of the impact and leaving him surprisingly steady.
Damien looked back at the vehicle for only a moment.
Then he disappeared between the buildings.

He moved quickly through the narrow passage, keeping his body low as he passed through the shadows. The sound of approaching sirens grew louder behind him, but Damien didn’t look back. He continued deeper into the maze of buildings before slipping into an even darker area and changing direction.
Within seconds, he was gone.
The police vehicles came rushing around the corner shortly afterward.
Several cruisers surrounded the prison vehicle, and officers immediately jumped out with their weapons drawn.
"Hands where we can see them!
"Step out of the vehicle slowly!"
"Do not make any sudden movements!"
Their weapons remained trained on the vehicle.
For several seconds, nothing happened.
The engine was still running.
The doors remained closed.
Nobody emerged.
One officer cautiously moved closer.
"Suspect!"
He raised his voice.
"Put your hands in the air and step out slowly!"
Silence.
The officer glanced at his colleagues.
"Keep your weapons trained on it."
Another officer approached from the side, his weapon raised as he carefully inspected the vehicle.
"Could he be refusing to cooperate?"
"Maybe."
The officer reached the driver’s side and looked through the window.
His expression immediately changed.
"Wait."
He moved closer.
The driver’s seat was empty.
"What the hell?"
Another officer hurried over.
"What’s wrong?"
"He’s not here."
"What?"
The second officer looked inside for himself, and his expression immediately darkened.
The vehicle was empty.
The engine was still running, but Damien was gone.
The passenger seat was empty as well.
One of the officers immediately grabbed his radio.
"Dispatch, we have a problem."
A pause followed.
"The suspect has abandoned the vehicle."
Another officer turned toward the surrounding streets and scanned the area.
"Where did he go?"
Nobody had an answer.

They searched the immediate area, checking alleys, entrances, nearby buildings, and the surrounding streets. But there was no obvious trail. Damien had disappeared too quickly, and the chaos of the pursuit had given him enough time to put distance between himself and the vehicle.
The officer who had first reached the car clenched his jaw in frustration.
"Dammit."
He looked down the empty road, where the flashing lights of the police cruisers illuminated the darkness.
"We’ve lost him."
Several officers exchanged frustrated looks.
They had spent several minutes chasing the vehicle, believing Damien was still behind the wheel. They had coordinated an entire pursuit around that assumption.
All that time, they had been chasing an empty car.
Meanwhile, several blocks away, Damien emerged from the shadows.

He slowed to a walk, allowing himself a moment to catch his breath. His breathing remained surprisingly steady despite everything that had happened. He turned his head and looked back toward the distant flashing lights, watching the red and blue reflections flicker between the buildings.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"They actually thought I was still in the car."
He chuckled quietly.
Then his expression gradually became colder.
The prison was behind him.
The police were searching for him.
And nobody knew where he was.

For the first time in years, Damien understood just how drastically his circumstances had changed. He had escaped Blackridge Correctional Facility, a place he had once believed would hold him for the rest of his life. He had awakened an inexplicable strength, discovered the existence of Qi within his body, and used abilities he hadn’t even understood only hours earlier to evade an organized police pursuit.
The realization sent a strange sensation through him.
He was no longer powerless.
He looked down at his hands and slowly clenched them into fists.
There was strength in them now.
Real strength.
The kind of strength he had once believed belonged only to other people.
But power alone wasn’t what occupied his mind.
There was still one thing he wanted more than anything else.
Revenge.
The name surfaced in his mind almost immediately.
"Sophie..."
His smile faded.

Memories of her rejection, his humiliation, and everything that had happened afterward twisted together inside his mind. His resentment toward her had survived imprisonment, punishment, and years of isolation. If anything, the hatred had only grown stronger in the darkness of his cell.
Then another name surfaced.
"Stan."
Damien’s fists tightened until his knuckles turned pale.
The faint smile that returned to his face contained none of the excitement from his escape. It was colder now, sharpened by years of resentment and obsession.
"I’ll find you both."
He turned away from the distant police lights and began walking deeper into the city.

Behind him, the abandoned prison vehicle remained surrounded by confused officers who still had no idea where their prisoner had disappeared. They didn’t know what had happened inside the vehicle, and they certainly didn’t understand the transformation that had taken place within Damien.
As far as they were concerned, they were searching for a dangerous escaped prisoner.
They had no idea that the man they were hunting had become something far more dangerous.
Damien Bale was no longer the powerless inmate who had entered Blackridge Correctional Facility.
He was now one of the first humans on Earth to awaken to Qi.
And somewhere within the vast city ahead, he had begun his new life as a fugitive.
A life driven by power, hatred, and revenge.

"So that’s how they’re keeping up..."
His expression darkened.
He didn’t need to be a genius to understand the problem.
As long as he remained inside the prison vehicle, the police would always have a way to locate him.
Speed alone wouldn’t solve the problem.
Eventually, they would coordinate enough units to surround him.
Damien looked toward the road ahead, then glanced at the pursuing vehicles in his mirrors.
A cold smile slowly appeared.
"Fine."
He began searching for an opportunity.
The pursuit continued through several more streets, with police vehicles attempting to intercept him from multiple directions.
Damien repeatedly changed course whenever he noticed them forming a blockade ahead.
He was no longer simply running from the police; he was studying them, anticipating their movements, and exploiting every weakness in their pursuit.
Eventually, he found what he needed.
A quieter stretch of road appeared ahead.
There were fewer vehicles, and several large buildings lined one side of the street.
On the opposite side, a narrow service road branched away between the buildings, leading into a darker and more secluded section of the city.
Damien’s eyes narrowed.
’That would do.’ He deliberately slowed the vehicle.
The pursuing officers immediately reacted.
"He’s slowing down!"
"He’s boxed in!"
One cruiser moved into position behind him while another approached from farther ahead, attempting to close the remaining escape route.
Damien’s lips curled upward.
They thought they had him.
At the last possible moment, he turned sharply.
The vehicle shot toward the service road, forcing the pursuing cruisers to adjust their positions and follow.

Damien drove deeper into the narrow passage before finally spotting the secluded area he had been looking for—a concealed space between several large buildings where the surrounding structures would block the line of sight from the main road.
He slammed on the brakes.
The tires screamed against the pavement, and the vehicle lurched violently as it came to a stop.
Before the pursuing officers could understand what he was doing, Damien had already thrown open the driver’s door.
He jumped out.
His boots struck the pavement hard, but instead of stumbling, he immediately recovered his balance.
The strange energy flowing through his body surged instinctively, absorbing much of the impact and leaving him surprisingly steady.
Damien looked back at the vehicle for only a moment.
Then he disappeared between the buildings.
He moved quickly through the narrow passage, keeping his body low as he passed through the shadows.
The sound of approaching sirens grew louder behind him, but Damien didn’t look back.
He continued deeper into the maze of buildings before slipping into an even darker area and changing direction.
Within seconds, he was gone.
The police vehicles came rushing around the corner shortly afterward.
Several cruisers surrounded the prison vehicle, and officers immediately jumped out with their weapons drawn.
"Hands where we can see them!
"Step out of the vehicle slowly!"
"Do not make any sudden movements!"
Their weapons remained trained on the vehicle.
For several seconds, nothing happened.
The engine was still running.
The doors remained closed.
Nobody emerged.
One officer cautiously moved closer.
"Suspect!"
He raised his voice.
"Put your hands in the air and step out slowly!"
Silence.
The officer glanced at his colleagues.
"Keep your weapons trained on it."
Another officer approached from the side, his weapon raised as he carefully inspected the vehicle.
"Could he be refusing to cooperate?"
"Maybe."
The officer reached the driver’s side and looked through the window.
His expression immediately changed.
"Wait."
He moved closer.
The driver’s seat was empty.
"What the hell?"
Another officer hurried over.
"What’s wrong?"
"He’s not here."
"What?"
The second officer looked inside for himself, and his expression immediately darkened.
The vehicle was empty.
The engine was still running, but Damien was gone.
The passenger seat was empty as well.
One of the officers immediately grabbed his radio.
"Dispatch, we have a problem."
A pause followed.
"The suspect has abandoned the vehicle."
Another officer turned toward the surrounding streets and scanned the area.
"Where did he go?"
Nobody had an answer.
They searched the immediate area, checking alleys, entrances, nearby buildings, and the surrounding streets.
But there was no obvious trail.
Damien had disappeared too quickly, and the chaos of the pursuit had given him enough time to put distance between himself and the vehicle.
The officer who had first reached the car clenched his jaw in frustration.
"Dammit."
He looked down the empty road, where the flashing lights of the police cruisers illuminated the darkness.
"We’ve lost him."
Several officers exchanged frustrated looks.
They had spent several minutes chasing the vehicle, believing Damien was still behind the wheel.
They had coordinated an entire pursuit around that assumption.
All that time, they had been chasing an empty car.
Meanwhile, several blocks away, Damien emerged from the shadows.
He slowed to a walk, allowing himself a moment to catch his breath.
His breathing remained surprisingly steady despite everything that had happened.
He turned his head and looked back toward the distant flashing lights, watching the red and blue reflections flicker between the buildings.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"They actually thought I was still in the car."
He chuckled quietly.
Then his expression gradually became colder.
The prison was behind him.
The police were searching for him.
And nobody knew where he was.
For the first time in years, Damien understood just how drastically his circumstances had changed.
He had escaped Blackridge Correctional Facility, a place he had once believed would hold him for the rest of his life.
He had awakened an inexplicable strength, discovered the existence of Qi within his body, and used abilities he hadn’t even understood only hours earlier to evade an organized police pursuit.
The realization sent a strange sensation through him.
He was no longer powerless.
He looked down at his hands and slowly clenched them into fists.
There was strength in them now.
Real strength.
The kind of strength he had once believed belonged only to other people.
But power alone wasn’t what occupied his mind.
There was still one thing he wanted more than anything else.
Revenge.
The name surfaced in his mind almost immediately.
"Sophie..."
His smile faded.
Memories of her rejection, his humiliation, and everything that had happened afterward twisted together inside his mind.
His resentment toward her had survived imprisonment, punishment, and years of isolation.
If anything, the hatred had only grown stronger in the darkness of his cell.
Then another name surfaced.
"Stan."
Damien’s fists tightened until his knuckles turned pale.
The faint smile that returned to his face contained none of the excitement from his escape.
It was colder now, sharpened by years of resentment and obsession.
"I’ll find you both."
He turned away from the distant police lights and began walking deeper into the city.
Behind him, the abandoned prison vehicle remained surrounded by confused officers who still had no idea where their prisoner had disappeared.
They didn’t know what had happened inside the vehicle, and they certainly didn’t understand the transformation that had taken place within Damien.
As far as they were concerned, they were searching for a dangerous escaped prisoner.
They had no idea that the man they were hunting had become something far more dangerous.
Damien Bale was no longer the powerless inmate who had entered Blackridge Correctional Facility.
He was now one of the first humans on Earth to awaken to Qi.
And somewhere within the vast city ahead, he had begun his new life as a fugitive.
A life driven by power, hatred, and revenge.

chapters.title: Chapter 496: Pause
paragraphs: Despite that improvement, Stan had deliberately stopped cultivating afterward.

Space rippled around Stan and Camilla, but there was none of the violent distortion that usually accompanied powerful spatial techniques. There was no thunderous explosion, no oppressive fluctuation of energy, and no sensation of being dragged through a turbulent spatial passage. Instead, the surrounding space behaved almost naturally, as though reality itself had briefly become flexible beneath Stan’s control. The boundaries of the world seemed to fold inward, overlapping for an instant before reconnecting somewhere else. Stan simply stepped forward, and in the next moment, the unfamiliar environment surrounding them vanished, replaced by the familiar interior of his residence.

Camilla followed closely behind him. The spatial fluctuations continued for several seconds after their arrival before gradually settling down, leaving the room completely silent. The air was still, the furniture remained exactly where they had left it, and nothing about the residence suggested that the two of them had just crossed an enormous spatial distance through an inheritance space that existed under entirely different spatial laws.

Stan glanced around the room and felt a subtle sense of relief. Home. After spending several days inside the strange chamber connected to the Void Sovereign’s inheritance, surrounded by an environment that seemed to exist beyond the ordinary boundaries of space, the familiar sight of his residence suddenly felt far more comfortable than he had expected. The walls, furniture, and ordinary atmosphere lacked the grandeur and mystery of the inheritance, but that was precisely what made them reassuring. He released a quiet breath and allowed the tension that had accumulated during their journey to ease from his body.
“Back,” Stan said simply.
Camilla stepped forward and looked around the room as though confirming for herself that they had actually returned. After several seconds, she nodded slightly. “So we’re really back.”
“Obviously.” Stan glanced at her with an amused expression. “You thought I’d gotten us lost?”
Camilla immediately gave him a flat look. “Considering where you took me, I wouldn’t have been surprised.”

Stan couldn’t help but chuckle. Their journey back had technically been far more complicated than her words suggested. What appeared to have been a simple teleportation was actually the result of Stan manipulating multiple spatial boundaries simultaneously. They had first needed to leave the strange tea room and enter the surrounding spatial domain connected to the Void Sovereign’s inheritance. From there, Stan had to locate and establish a stable connection with Earth before transporting both himself and Camilla back to his residence.

Under normal circumstances, accomplishing something like that would have been extraordinarily difficult. The spatial environments involved were fundamentally different from ordinary physical distance. It was not simply a matter of traveling from one location to another. Stan had effectively crossed the boundaries separating distinct spatial environments, each governed by rules that could easily reject an outsider’s interference. A cultivator without sufficient comprehension of spatial laws could spend years studying such a technique and still fail to reproduce what Stan had accomplished.

Stan, however, possessed an advantage that most cultivators could never hope to obtain. The Void Sovereign had already granted him authority over that mysterious space. Because of that authority, the spatial barriers that should have resisted his movements were practically nonexistent to him. Rather than forcibly tearing through the boundaries between spaces, Stan could interact with them as though he had been granted permission to pass through a door. His rapidly improving comprehension of spatial laws, combined with his current cultivation realm, made the entire process even easier.

For Stan, the teleportation had therefore felt almost effortless. It had not been a desperate display of power or a dangerous gamble with unstable spatial energy. It had simply been a matter of determining where he wanted to go and allowing space to accommodate his intention.
Camilla, however, clearly hadn’t forgotten what she had witnessed.
She stared at him for several seconds before finally speaking. “You really make teleportation look too easy.”
“It isn’t.”
“It looked easy.”
Stan shrugged casually. “That’s because I’m good at it.”
Camilla rolled her eyes. “Arrogant.”
“Accurate.”

She chose not to argue with him and instead walked toward the sofa. The moment she sat down, she leaned back and allowed her body to sink into the cushions, visibly relaxing now that they were safely home. For several days, she had been surrounded by an environment saturated with an astonishing concentration of Spatial Qi. Although she possessed considerable strength herself, that energy was fundamentally different from the Qi she was accustomed to cultivating. She had no affinity for Spatial Qi, nor did she possess the ability to properly utilize the vast reserves surrounding the tea room.

Simply existing within such an environment had therefore been mentally exhausting. Every moment spent there had required her to remain conscious of an energy that was constantly pressing against her senses without truly becoming part of her cultivation system. It had not harmed her, but the unfamiliarity had made the experience considerably more taxing than it had been for Stan.
Stan, meanwhile, felt almost completely different from when he had entered the inheritance.

His entire body seemed lighter, while his spiritual perception had become noticeably sharper. More importantly, there was now an indescribable sense of stability within his cultivation. The change was subtle, but Stan could feel it clearly. The barrier that had previously stood before him was gone, and the cultivation bottleneck that had restrained his advancement for some time had finally been broken.

The breakthrough itself had been surprisingly uneventful. There had been no earth-shattering phenomenon, no terrifying pressure spreading across the surrounding space, and no massive surge of energy announcing his advancement to the world. His cultivation had simply crossed the barrier. One moment, he had been standing before a bottleneck that seemed firmly entrenched within his cultivation. The next, the bottleneck no longer existed.

The immense concentration of Spatial Qi inside the tea room had ultimately provided him with the final push he needed. His comprehension of spatial laws had deepened at the same time, and the Void Sovereign Sutra, which had previously contained many concepts he could only partially understand, had become considerably clearer.
Despite that improvement, Stan had deliberately stopped cultivating afterward.

chapters.title: Chapter 497: Advancing Quickly
paragraphs: He could have remained inside that environment for much longer. In fact, if he continued cultivating within the tea room, his cultivation speed would probably remain absurdly high. The concentration and purity of Spatial Qi there were simply too extraordinary to ignore. For another cultivator, such an environment would have been an unimaginable treasure, something they might spend their entire lives searching for.
For Stan, however, that abundance had become a problem.
He was advancing too quickly.
Far too quickly.

Although rapid advancement sounded like an advantage, Stan understood that cultivation was never simply a matter of accumulating power as quickly as possible. A cultivator’s foundation needed to be strong enough to support every increase in strength. If cultivation advanced faster than the body, spiritual energy, comprehension, and foundation could adapt, hidden weaknesses would eventually accumulate beneath the surface.

Stan had already noticed subtle signs that his foundation needed time to stabilize. They were not dangerous yet, and there was no immediate threat to his cultivation. Nevertheless, Stan had enough experience to understand that ignoring such warning signs simply because he could continue advancing would be foolish.
He had no intention of becoming powerful quickly only to suffer the consequences of rushing his cultivation later.

He needed time to consolidate what he had gained. His body needed to adapt to the new level of power, his spiritual energy needed to become fully integrated with his cultivation realm, and his comprehension needed time to settle into something stable rather than remaining in a state of rapid expansion. Only after those aspects had caught up with his cultivation would further advancement be truly beneficial.
That was why he had ultimately decided to leave the inheritance space.
Stan walked over and sat down opposite Camilla. He leaned back comfortably, his gaze briefly falling upon her before he noticed the thoughtful expression on her face.
“So,” Camilla said.
Stan raised an eyebrow. “So?”
“You dragged me into some spatial space for several days, went deep into cultivation all of a sudden, broke through another realm, and then suddenly decided it was time to come home.”
Stan nodded calmly. “That’s basically what happened.”
Camilla stared at him for several seconds, clearly dissatisfied with how casually he had summarized the entire experience. “You make it sound incredibly ordinary.”
“It was.”
“You’re impossible.”
Stan laughed quietly.

For a moment, the room fell silent again. The silence was not uncomfortable. After the strange and dangerous environment they had spent the past several days in, the ordinary quietness of the residence was almost relaxing. Neither of them felt any particular need to fill it with conversation.
Then Camilla’s expression suddenly changed.
Her eyes brightened as though she had just remembered something important.
“Oh.”
Stan looked toward her. “What?”
“I just remembered something.”

Camilla immediately stood and walked toward one of the cabinets. Stan watched her curiously as she opened it and began searching through its contents. A few seconds later, she returned carrying two boxes in her hands.
She placed them carefully on the table between them.
One was a set of Uno cards.
The other was a chess set.
Stan stared at the two boxes for a moment before looking back at Camilla.
“You want to play?”
“Of course.” Camilla looked almost offended by the question. “You bought them for me.”
“I remember.”
“Then why wouldn’t I play?”

Stan smiled faintly. Camilla had always possessed an unusual curiosity toward games. Despite her strength and her experience as a cultivator, she could become surprisingly interested in simple activities that required thought, strategy, or sometimes nothing more than luck. There was something amusing about watching someone who could survive battles involving powerful cultivators become genuinely invested in something as ordinary as a card game.
The contrast was even more ridiculous when Stan considered everything that had happened recently.

He had access to an inheritance left behind by an existence whose power was difficult for even him to comprehend. He had obtained authority over a mysterious spatial domain, cultivated within an environment saturated with Spatial Qi, comprehended deeper aspects of the Void Sovereign Sutra, and broken through another cultivation bottleneck.
Yet after all of that, he was sitting in his residence with Camilla preparing to play Uno and chess.
Stan looked at the two boxes again before shaking his head with a faint smile.
Cultivation, inheritances, ancient powers, spatial laws, and mysterious treasures could wait.
For the moment, apparently, Camilla wanted to play a game.

Camilla sat across from Stan with the box of Uno cards resting on the table between them. She picked it up and turned it over in her hands, examining it briefly before looking at Stan with an expectant expression. “Which one first?” she asked, already knowing what his answer would probably be.
“Uno.”
“Good.”

She immediately opened the box and began arranging the cards. Stan watched her carefully sort through them, noticing how seriously she approached something that was supposed to be nothing more than a casual game. She organized her hand with deliberate precision, grouping cards together and occasionally glancing at the different colors and numbers as though she were preparing for an important battle.
“You know the rules, right?” Stan asked.
Camilla raised an eyebrow and looked at him as though he had just insulted her intelligence. “I’ve played enough times.”
“That’s not what I asked.”
“I know the rules.”
“You’re sure? That og chess”
Her eyes narrowed slightly. “I used the phone to learn more about it..”
Stan smiled and raised his hands in surrender. “Fine.”
With that, they began.
The first few rounds were surprisingly relaxed.

Neither of them seemed particularly concerned about winning or losing, and the conversation continued naturally as they played. However, Stan quickly noticed that Camilla was taking the game more seriously than he had expected. More importantly, the number of cards remaining in the opponent’s hand had to be monitored constantly. Allowing an opponent to reach only a few cards without adjusting one’s strategy could result in an unexpected defeat.

chapters.title: Chapter 498: Relaxation
paragraphs: Stan quickly noticed that Camilla was taking the game more seriously than he had expected. More importantly, the number of cards remaining in the opponent’s hand had to be monitored constantly. Allowing an opponent to reach only a few cards without adjusting one’s strategy could result in an unexpected defeat.

As the game progressed, her relaxed expression gradually disappeared. Her posture became straighter, her attention focused entirely on the cards, and her eyes repeatedly moved between her own hand and Stan’s. She began memorizing his discarded cards and paying close attention whenever he drew from the pile. Stan noticed the transformation almost immediately.
He nearly laughed.
Camilla wasn’t playing Uno anymore.
She was waging war.
"You know this is just Uno, right?" Stan asked after watching her stare at the discard pile for several seconds.
"I know."
"You look like you’re preparing to kill someone."
"I’m concentrating."
Stan glanced at the cards in her hand. She was holding only three.
"You’re holding three cards."
"Exactly."
Stan looked down at his own hand.
He had six.

The difference wasn’t particularly large, but it was enough for him to realize that Camilla had maneuvered herself into a considerably better position than he had expected. She had been quietly controlling the game while he had been treating it as entertainment.
"You’re terrifying," Stan said.
Camilla didn’t even look up from her cards. "I’ll take that as a compliment."

Several more turns passed. Stan attempted to recover his position, but Camilla had already anticipated his strategy. She changed the color whenever necessary, forced him to draw when she had the opportunity, and carefully preserved the cards she suspected would become useful later. Eventually, after a particularly well-timed sequence, she placed her final card onto the table.
"Uno."
Stan froze.
His gaze moved slowly toward Camilla’s empty hand. He then looked down at his own cards before looking back at her.
For several seconds, he said nothing.
"...You cheated."
Camilla’s eyes widened in genuine disbelief. "I did not."
"You definitely did."
"I played according to the rules."
"You’ve been counting my cards."
"That’s called strategy."
Stan stared at her.
Camilla simply smiled.
"I won.
Stan leaned back and released a resigned sigh. He couldn’t even argue with her reasoning. She hadn’t broken any rules. She had simply paid far more attention to the game than he had.
"Fine."
Camilla’s smile immediately became more pronounced.
"Again."
Stan blinked. "Already?"
"Again."
He shook his head in disbelief. "You’re addicted."
"Perhaps."
The second game began almost immediately.

Unlike the first, there was no longer any pretense that they were playing casually. Both of them had now become aware of what the other was capable of, and the atmosphere around the table subtly changed. Stan started paying closer attention to Camilla’s discarded cards, while Camilla became even more cautious about revealing the structure of her hand.

The second game lasted considerably longer than the first. Neither managed to gain a decisive advantage for a while, and the number of cards in their hands repeatedly shifted as Draw Two and Draw Four cards were exchanged. When one of them appeared close to victory, the other would inevitably find a way to disrupt the situation.
The third game lasted even longer.
By the fourth, Stan had reached a simple conclusion.
Camilla was far more competitive than he had expected.

She had started the evening treating Uno as a simple game she wanted to play because Stan had bought it for her. Now she was behaving as though the outcome would determine something of genuine importance. Every card was examined carefully before being played, every move was considered, and every unexpected draw visibly affected her mood.
At one point, Camilla was forced to draw several cards in succession. She stared down at the growing number of cards in her hand, her expression becoming increasingly dark.
Stan pressed his lips together, desperately trying not to laugh.
"Don’t laugh," Camilla said without looking at him.
"I’m not."
"You are."
"I’m not."
"You are."
"I promise I’m not."
Camilla slowly lifted her head and looked directly at him. Her expression made it obvious that she knew exactly how much he was enjoying her misfortune.
"You’re enjoying this."
Stan struggled to maintain a straight face. "A little."
Camilla immediately picked up one of her cards and placed it firmly on the table.
"Draw Four."
Stan’s smile vanished.
He looked at the card.
Then he looked at Camilla.
"...That’s personal."
"It isn’t."
"It feels personal."
Camilla’s lips curved into a sweet smile that somehow made the situation even worse. "Your turn."
Stan stared at her for a moment before reluctantly drawing the required cards.

By the time they finally decided to move on from Uno, Camilla had become thoroughly invested in the game. Stan wasn’t entirely sure whether she was more interested in the game itself or simply in proving that she could beat him.
Eventually, however, the Uno cards were pushed aside, and Camilla placed the chessboard on the table.
The atmosphere changed almost immediately.

Every piece was visible from the beginning, and every move carried consequences. Victory depended on planning, calculation, patience, and the ability to anticipate what the opponent intended to do several moves ahead.

Camilla sat across from Stan and rested her chin lightly on her hands as she stared at the board. Unlike Uno, where she had quickly become impulsive and competitive, chess forced her to slow down. Her eyes moved from one piece to another as she considered different possibilities. She studied the arrangement of the board carefully, apparently trying to determine which opening would give her the greatest advantage.
After several moments of consideration, she finally moved one of her pieces.
Stan responded almost immediately.
Camilla frowned.
She studied the board again before making another move.
Stan countered.
Her frown deepened.
"You saw that?" she asked.
"Yes."
"Before I moved?"
"Yes."
Camilla looked at him suspiciously. "How?"
Stan shrugged. "Experience."
She stared at him for a moment before looking back at the chessboard.
She looked down at the board again, but the suspicion in her expression remained. After several seconds, she sighed and moved another piece.
"Still."
A small smile appeared on Stan’s face.
There was something strangely peaceful about the entire situation.
After everything they had experienced, sitting across from each other over a chessboard felt almost unreal
It was simply the two of them sitting inside his residence, arguing over the rules of Uno and silently calculating their next moves on a chessboard.
For a brief moment, Stan almost forgot how complicated the world had become.

chapters.title: Chapter 499: Commissioner
paragraphs: For a brief moment, Stan almost forgot how complicated the world had become.
He looked at Camilla as she continued studying the board, completely absorbed in the game. The sight brought a quiet sense of satisfaction to his mind.
He could simply sit down and enjoy the company of someone he cared about.
The thought lingered for only a few seconds.
Then his phone suddenly rang.
The sharp sound cut through the quiet atmosphere of the room, instantly drawing Stan’s attention away from the chessboard.
Camilla also lifted her head.
Both of them looked toward the phone.
Stan’s relaxed expression gradually disappeared as he stared at the device, wondering who could possibly be calling him at a time like this.
Whatever it was, it had interrupted one of the few peaceful moments he had managed to enjoy in a long time.

Stan’s gaze shifted toward the phone as it continued ringing. The relaxed expression that had remained on his face throughout the game gradually disappeared, replaced by a faint look of curiosity. He reached for the device and glanced at the notification that had appeared across the screen.
His expression changed slightly.
A breaking-news alert occupied the top of the screen, accompanied by a headline that immediately caught his attention.
BREAKING NEWS — MAJOR PRISON BREAK REPORTED AT BLACKRIDGE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY
Stan’s eyebrows rose slightly.
"Blackridge?"

The name immediately stood out to him. He had heard it before, and he didn’t need more than a second to remember why. Blackridge Correctional Facility was the prison where Damien had been incarcerated.
Camilla, who had been sitting across from him with the chessboard still between them, noticed the change in his expression. She lifted her head and looked toward him.
"What is it?"

Stan didn’t answer immediately. Instead, he opened the news report and began reading through the article. The initial report was still developing, and many of the details remained unclear, but the central information was enough to make his expression gradually become more serious.

A large-scale breach had occurred at Blackridge Correctional Facility several hours earlier. According to the preliminary information released by the authorities, a significant number of inmates had managed to escape during the incident. Security forces had already regained control of the prison, and several escapees had been recaptured, but numerous others were still missing.
Stan’s eyes narrowed slightly as he continued scrolling.
"Isn’t that the prison Damien was in?" he muttered.
Camilla paused.

The name meant nothing to her. She had heard Stan mention many people over the course of their time together, but Damien was not someone she was particularly familiar with. She wondered briefly who this Damien was, what a prison and prison break was and why a prison break involving him had suddenly caught Stan’s attention.

However, she could tell from Stan’s expression that whatever connection existed between the man and the prison was important. Rather than interrupt him with questions, Camilla remained silent and watched as he opened another report.
Then another.

Stan searched the prison’s name directly and began comparing the information from different reports. The details varied slightly because the incident was still unfolding, but the central facts remained consistent.
Blackridge Correctional Facility.
A mass prison breach.
Multiple inmates had escaped.
Several had already been recaptured.
Many remained missing.
Stan’s expression darkened as the pieces came together.
"So it really happened."

He leaned back slightly, but his attention remained fixed on the phone. The reports were still incomplete, and the authorities had yet to provide a full explanation of how such a large number of prisoners had managed to escape from a supposedly secure facility. Some reports mentioned a sudden breakdown in the prison’s security systems, while others referred to confusion among the guards during the initial breach. At that point, however, none of the available information was detailed enough for Stan to determine exactly what had happened.
What concerned him wasn’t simply the prison break itself.
It was the possibility that Damien had escaped.
Stan had no reason to assume that Damien was among the recaptured inmates. Until he confirmed otherwise, there was a very real possibility that the man was somewhere outside the prison walls.
That possibility immediately changed the situation.
Stan lowered the phone slightly and frowned. "This is troublesome."

Camilla studied him carefully but still didn’t ask about Damien. She had learned that when Stan became this serious, there was usually a reason. Whatever connection he had to the escaped prisoner, he clearly needed more information before deciding what to do next.
Stan’s thoughts moved rapidly.

If Damien had escaped, he needed to know how it had happened, whether the authorities had identified him among the missing inmates, and whether there had been anything unusual about the breach. A normal prison escape was already a serious matter, but Stan had long since stopped believing that events involving powerful individuals could always be explained by ordinary circumstances.
Fortunately, there was someone he could ask.
Stan scrolled through his contacts, searching for a number he hadn’t needed to use in quite some time. His finger moved down the list until he finally found the name he was looking for.
He stared at it for a moment before pressing the call button.
The phone rang once.
Twice.
Three times.
Stan waited patiently, his expression remaining calm but his attention focused entirely on the call. After several more rings, the other person finally answered.
"Stan?"
The man’s voice carried a clear note of surprise. He obviously hadn’t expected to receive a call from Stan, especially after such a long period without contact.
There was a brief pause before the man continued.
"It’s been a long time."
A faint smile appeared on Stan’s face.
"Commissioner."

The simple exchange carried the familiarity of two people who had dealt with each other before, even if their circumstances had kept them apart for some time. Stan leaned back in his chair while Camilla quietly watched him from across the table.
The chessboard remained between them, the unfinished game forgotten for the moment.
Whatever had happened at Blackridge Correctional Facility, Stan intended to find out.

chapters.title: Chapter 500: Talk With Commissioner
paragraphs: “It’s been a long time, Commissioner.”
The man on the other end of the call let out a warm laugh, his familiar voice carrying a hint of amusement. “It really has.”
The person Stan had called was the police commissioner who had personally overseen the investigation surrounding Amelia’s kidnapping.

Their relationship had begun under circumstances neither of them would have expected. At the time, Stan had been directly involved in helping Amelia escape from the Red Serpents, an organization whose activities had made them a significant target for law enforcement. After rescuing Amelia, Stan had also provided the police with crucial information about the organization, giving them details that would have otherwise taken months of investigation to uncover.

The information had eventually contributed to a much larger operation. The police had followed the leads Stan provided, gathered additional evidence, tracked down several members of the organization, and ultimately captured many of the Red Serpents’ major figures. The commissioner had never forgotten Stan’s contribution.

“I’ve actually been meaning to properly thank you,” the commissioner said after a moment. “We finally managed to close out a lot of the Red Serpent investigation not too long ago. If you hadn’t given us those details, we probably wouldn’t have been able to bring the entire organization down.”
Stan shook his head lightly, even though the commissioner couldn’t see him. “You don’t have to thank me.”
“Don’t say that.”
“It’s true.”
“You gave us information that saved us months of work.”

“I only gave you what I knew.” Stan smiled faintly as he leaned back against the sofa. “I got those details because they were following me when Amelia was kidnapped. I managed to save her and learned some things in the process. The actual investigation, evidence gathering, arrests, and everything else were done by your people. I didn’t do the difficult part.”
The commissioner chuckled. “You’re still as modest as ever.”
“Not really.”

Stan’s gaze drifted toward the chessboard in front of him. The pieces remained scattered across the board exactly as they had been before the call. Across from him, Camilla was quietly observing the conversation, though she made no attempt to interrupt.
The commissioner was silent for a moment before his tone changed slightly. “Speaking of Amelia...”
Stan’s expression softened almost imperceptibly...
“How is she? I got news after she was treated in the hospital that she was searching for you...”
“She’s doing well.”
“That’s good.”
There was a brief pause between them before the commissioner continued, his voice becoming more thoughtful. “I actually wanted to ask you something.”
“Go ahead.”

“Before Amelia was kidnapped, the guards protecting her reported something rather strange. They said she seemed to have developed a strong hatred toward men. Not just toward particular individuals, but toward men in general.”
Stan listened without interrupting.

“After everything she went through, we assumed it was probably connected to her past experiences,” the commissioner continued. “Since you were the one who eventually saved her, did she ever get over that?”
Stan thought about the question for a few seconds before answering. “High chance she has.”
“You aren’t sure?”
“I haven’t exactly interviewed her about it.”
The commissioner laughed. “Fair enough.”
Stan smiled. “But from what I’ve seen, she seems to have changed.”
“That’s good to hear.”
“Though I can’t say for certain what she feels internally.”
“Understandable.”

The subject gradually shifted away from Amelia after that. Their conversation moved naturally toward the Red Serpent investigation, with the commissioner mentioning some of the difficulties the department had faced while tracking down the organization’s remaining members. Although the major investigation had largely been brought to a close, there had still been loose ends to deal with, and locating every individual connected to the organization had taken considerable time and manpower.

Stan listened as the commissioner briefly described how things had been progressing within the department. At one point, the commissioner jokingly complained about the endless paperwork, political pressure, and seemingly never-ending stream of problems that appeared whenever the department managed to resolve one of them.
Stan laughed. “You sound exhausted.”
“Police work.”
“Fair enough.”
The conversation then turned toward Stan. “And you?”
Stan raised an eyebrow despite himself. “What about me?”
“What have you been doing all this time?”
Stan paused briefly before giving the simplest answer he could. “Nothing particularly interesting.”
Across the table, Camilla immediately glanced at him.
Her expression made it obvious that she did not believe him for even a second.
Stan deliberately ignored her.
The commissioner laughed on the other end of the call. “With you, I doubt that’s true.”
“Maybe.”

Their conversation continued for several more minutes, touching on various subjects before Stan finally remembered the real reason he had made the call in the first place. He shifted slightly in his seat and became more serious.
“There was actually something I wanted to ask you about, it’s why I called you in the first place...”
“Go ahead.”
“Blackridge Correctional Facility.”
The moment Stan mentioned the name, the commissioner went silent.
Stan noticed the sudden change in his tone and continued. “Can you check whether a prisoner named Damien Bale was among those recaptured?”
For several seconds, there was no response.
Then the commissioner finally spoke.
“Wait.”
His tone had changed completely.
“Blackridge?”
“Yes.”
“You know about it?”
“I just saw the news.”
“The news?”
Stan frowned. “You haven’t heard?”
“Heard what?”
“A prison break happened a few hours ago.”
Another pause followed. This time, the commissioner sounded genuinely surprised.
“I’ve been extremely busy today. I haven’t even had time to look at the news.”
Stan stared at his phone for a moment, wondering if the commissioner was joking.
“Seriously?”
“I wish I were joking.”
The commissioner exhaled heavily before asking, “What exactly happened?”

Stan gave him the basic details he had seen in the report. A large-scale breach had occurred at Blackridge Correctional Facility several hours earlier, allowing multiple prisoners to escape. Some had already been recaptured, while others remained at large, and authorities were still working to determine the full extent of the incident.

“With you, I doubt that’s true.”
“Maybe.”
Their conversation continued for several more minutes, touching on various subjects before Stan finally remembered the real reason he had made the call in the first place.
He shifted slightly in his seat and became more serious.
“There was actually something I wanted to ask you about, it’s why I called you in the first place...”
“Go ahead.”
“Blackridge Correctional Facility.”
The moment Stan mentioned the name, the commissioner went silent.
Stan noticed the sudden change in his tone and continued.
“Can you check whether a prisoner named Damien Bale was among those recaptured?”
For several seconds, there was no response.
Then the commissioner finally spoke.
“Wait.”
His tone had changed completely.
“Blackridge?”
“Yes.”
“You know about it?”
“I just saw the news.”
“The news?”
Stan frowned.
“You haven’t heard?”
“Heard what?”
“A prison break happened a few hours ago.”
Another pause followed.
This time, the commissioner sounded genuinely surprised.
“I’ve been extremely busy today.
I haven’t even had time to look at the news.”
Stan stared at his phone for a moment, wondering if the commissioner was joking.
“Seriously?”
“I wish I were joking.”
The commissioner exhaled heavily before asking, “What exactly happened?”
Stan gave him the basic details he had seen in the report.
A large-scale breach had occurred at Blackridge Correctional Facility several hours earlier, allowing multiple prisoners to escape.
Some had already been recaptured, while others remained at large, and authorities were still working to determine the full extent of the incident.
